topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks at a map where 1 cm = 50 km, can they work out the real distance between two cities that are 4.5 cm apart on the map?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: 单位换算
topics.description: 在相关的标准测量单位之间自由换算（时间、长度、面积、体积/容积、质量），适当情况下使用小数表示，最多保留三位小数。
evidence: Convert between area units such as cm² and m² using the square of the linear scale factor
Perform multi-step conversions (e.g. convert 2.5 hours to seconds via minutes)
Convert volume units such as cm³ to litres and explain the relationship
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} convert between units confidently — for example, changing kilometres to metres, kilograms to grams, or hours and minutes to just minutes — including multi-step problems?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: 百分比（12岁以上）
topics.description: 解决涉及百分比增加、百分比减少、在百分比变化后求原始值以及计算单利的问题
evidence: Calculate a 15% increase on £240 using a decimal multiplier (× 1.15)
Find the original price before a 20% discount resulted in a sale price of £64
Calculate simple interest on £500 at 3% per annum for 4 years
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a bike originally costs £250 and its price goes up by 8%, can {{name}} work out the new price — and if a savings account earns 3% simple interest per year, how much interest would £500 earn in 4 years?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: 比例关系
topics.description: 认识并解决涉及正比例（一个量增加，另一个量以固定比率增加）和反比例（一个量增加，另一个量减少）的问题，包括图形和代数表示
evidence: Identify whether a real-world relationship is direct or inverse proportion and justify the choice
Set up and solve a direct-proportion equation (e.g. if 4 pens cost £6, find the cost of 10)
Sketch graphs showing direct proportion (straight line through origin) and inverse proportion (curve)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand the difference between quantities that grow together at the same rate (direct proportion) and ones where one goes up as the other goes down — like more workers meaning fewer days to finish a job (inverse proportion)?

topics.subject: Mathematics
topics.name: 比号与比的关系
topics.description: 理解两个数量之间的乘法关系可以用比来表示；使用比号；化简比
evidence: Explain why 'for every 2 red beads there are 5 blue beads' can be written as 2:5 or as 2/5 of the blue count
Identify the multiplicative relationship in a table of values (e.g. y is always 3 times x)
Connect the ratio a:b to the fraction a/b and to the linear function y = (a/b)x
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a ratio like 3:4 is really the same as the fraction ¾ — and show how that relationship connects to a straight-line graph through the origin?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 用语言表达感受
topics.description: 用语言而不是行动来恰当地表达自己的感受——比如说“我感到生气，因为……”，而不是打人、喊叫或退缩。
evidence: Use an 'I feel ___ when ___' statement during a disagreement
Choose to tell an adult how they feel instead of acting out physically
Describe their feelings about a difficult situation using at least two emotion words
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is frustrated — say a sibling takes their toy — do they use words to say how they feel rather than snatching it back or crying?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 感受会变化，也会不同
topics.description: 理解每个人都有自己的感受，感受在一天中会发生变化，而且同一件事可能让不同的人产生不同的感受。
evidence: Give an example of a time their feelings changed during a single day
Explain why two children might feel differently about the same event
Recognise that feelings are temporary and can change
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you and {{name}} watch the same film and you find it funny but {{name}} finds it scary, can they understand why you both felt differently?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 命名基本情绪
topics.description: 通过观察面部表情和身体语言，命名并识别自己和他人的基本情绪——开心、难过、生气、害怕、兴奋和惊讶
evidence: Label at least five basic emotions from pictures or real situations
Match facial expressions to emotion words in a sorting activity
Say 'I feel ___' using a correct emotion word when asked about their own day
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a friend crying at a birthday party, can they tell you what that friend might be feeling and name the emotion?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 情绪的原因和触发点
topics.description: 理解情绪是有原因的——发生了某件事（触发点），让我们产生某种感受——并开始识别是什么触发了自己的情绪
evidence: Describe a trigger for at least three different emotions from their own experience
Complete 'I felt ___ because ___' sentences accurately
Identify what made a character in a story feel a particular way
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} gets upset about something at school, can they explain to you what happened that made them feel that way?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 情绪词汇
topics.description: 使用更丰富的情绪词汇，超越基本情绪——包括沮丧、担心、焦虑、尴尬、嫉妒、骄傲、失望、感激和孤独——并区分相似的情绪
evidence: Use at least five emotion words beyond the basic six in everyday conversation
Explain the difference between two similar emotions such as angry and frustrated
Choose a precise emotion word that fits a described scenario
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} doesn't get invited to a classmate's party, can they describe whether they feel disappointed, jealous, lonely, or a mix — rather than just saying 'sad'?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 隐藏和掩饰的感受
topics.description: 认识到人们有时会隐藏或掩饰自己的真实感受——比如明明难过却微笑，或者明明不好却说“我没事”——并理解他们为什么可能会这样做。
evidence: Give an example of a time someone might hide their feelings and explain why
Identify mismatches between someone's words and their body language
Explain that hiding feelings is common but that it's usually better to share with someone trusted
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a friend at school says 'I'm fine' but looks upset and is being very quiet, can {{name}} recognise that the friend might not actually be fine?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 情绪在身体里的感觉
topics.description: 理解情绪与身体之间的联系——识别身体信号，比如紧张时肚子里的蝴蝶感（紧张）、握紧的拳头（生气）、心跳加速（害怕或兴奋）以及紧绷的肩膀（压力大）
evidence: Name at least three body sensations and match them to the emotions they signal
Notice a physical feeling in their own body and identify the emotion behind it
Explain why the body reacts physically when we have strong emotions
topics.assessmentPrompt: Before a school performance or sports day, can {{name}} notice and tell you about the physical feelings in their body — like butterflies in their tummy — and connect them to being nervous or excited?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 从轻微到强烈的情绪
topics.description: 理解情绪有不同的强度——从轻微到强烈——同一种情绪会因为强度不同而感觉大不一样（例如：有点烦 → 生气 → 暴怒，或者 紧张 → 焦虑 → 恐慌）
evidence: Place three related emotion words in order from mild to strong
Rate their own emotion on a simple scale (e.g., 1-5) in a real situation
Explain why recognising intensity matters for choosing how to respond
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell the difference between being a bit annoyed about losing a game and being truly furious — and explain that they're different levels of the same feeling?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 文化和经历塑造情绪
topics.description: 理解情绪反应是由个人经历、文化和情境塑造的——由于背景和过去经历不同，同一件事会引发不同的人不同的情绪
evidence: Explain why two people might have very different emotional reactions to the same event
Give an example of how a past experience shaped someone's emotional response
Describe how cultural background might influence what makes someone feel proud or embarrassed
topics.assessmentPrompt: If one child in {{name}}'s class gets very scared during a thunderstorm while others think it's exciting, can {{name}} understand that the scared child might have had a frightening experience with storms before?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 情绪模式随时间的变化
topics.description: 反思自己长期以来的情绪模式——注意反复出现的触发因素，理解自己典型的反应方式，并认识到自己的情绪觉察能力是如何成长的。
evidence: Identify a recurring emotional trigger and their typical response to it
Describe how their emotional understanding has changed compared to when they were younger
Set a personal goal related to emotional awareness, such as noticing when stress is building
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you something like 'I always get stressed before tests but I've learned that's normal for me' — showing they understand their own emotional patterns?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 情绪与决策
topics.description: 理解情绪如何影响思考和决策——强烈的情绪会干扰判断，我们在平静和心烦时常常做出不同的选择，认识到这一点能让我们更有掌控力。
evidence: Give an example of a time a strong emotion led them or someone else to a poor decision
Explain the idea of 'cooling off' before making an important choice
Describe how the same situation looks different when you're calm versus upset
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sends an angry message to a friend during an argument and later regrets it, can they explain how their anger affected their decision and what they might do differently next time?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 混合与矛盾的情绪
topics.description: 理解人们可以同时经历混合或矛盾的情绪——比如对新学校既兴奋又紧张，或者为朋友获胜而高兴却为自己失望
evidence: Describe a personal situation where they felt two emotions simultaneously
Explain why mixed feelings are normal and not something to worry about
Identify mixed emotions in a character from a book or film
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}}'s best friend gets picked for the team and they don't, can {{name}} explain that they feel happy for their friend AND disappointed for themselves at the same time?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 情绪的脑科学
topics.description: 了解杏仁核如何触发情绪反应，以及前额叶皮层（在青春期仍在发育）如何调节这些反应；解释为什么压力激素（皮质醇、肾上腺素）会影响思维和记忆；理解青少年大脑的多巴胺系统会让感受更加强烈；区分情绪调节（有效管理情绪）和情绪压抑（把情绪压下去，这反而适得其反）；介绍认知重评作为一种有研究支持的技术，用来改变我们对情境的解读。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain, in basic terms, why teenagers tend to feel emotions more intensely than adults — what's happening in the developing brain that makes feelings so powerful during adolescence, and what's the difference between managing a feeling and suppressing it?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 青春期的身份认同与归属感
topics.description: 理解青春期涉及主动构建身份认同，导致围绕“我是谁？”的问题产生情感复杂性；探索同时归属于多个群体（家庭、同伴群体、文化或宗教身份）的情感动态；理解社会比较及其通过社交媒体的加剧；认识到身份认同不是固定的，对身份的不确定是正常的，而非失败的标志；发展用于应对与群体成员身份和个人价值观相关情绪的语言。
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} goes through a phase of feeling unsure about who they are or where they belong, can they explain why this kind of uncertainty is a completely normal and even necessary part of adolescence — not a sign that something is wrong?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 情商
topics.description: 介绍戈尔曼的情商模型（自我觉察、自我调节、动机、共情、社交技能）；发展描述复杂情绪状态的词汇（矛盾心理、无聊感、幸灾乐祸、敬畏、怀旧、认知失调）；理解情商与幸福感、人际关系质量及长期生活成果相关的证据；反思中学阶段个人的情绪成长；探索情绪素养与心理健康的关系，并知道何时寻求专业支持。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe a real situation where being aware of their own emotions — knowing what they were feeling and why — helped them handle a difficult moment better than if they had just reacted automatically?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 日常中的善良与关爱
topics.description: 用简单日常的方式对他人表示善良和关心——安慰伤心的朋友、帮助掉了东西的人、主动分享、说友善的话
evidence: Spontaneously offer comfort to someone who is visibly upset
Help another person with a practical task without being asked
Use kind words to encourage or cheer up someone who is struggling
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a younger child at school falls over in the playground, does {{name}} go over to help or comfort them without being told to by an adult?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 别人的感受和想法
topics.description: 理解别人有自己的感受和想法，这些可能和你自己的不一样——这是认识到每个人对事物的看法和感受不一定相同的基础意识。
evidence: State that other people can feel differently about the same thing
Give an example of a time someone felt differently from them about the same situation
Accept another child's feeling as valid even when it differs from their own
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} loves dogs but their friend is scared of dogs, can {{name}} understand that their friend's fear is real even though they don't feel it themselves?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 相似与不同
topics.description: 注意并欣赏人们彼此相似和不同的地方——包括外貌、家庭结构、所说的语言、吃的食物和庆祝的节日——并理解差异让社区变得有趣
evidence: Name several ways people in their class or community are different from each other
Describe at least one thing they have learned from someone who is different from them
Express a positive attitude about differences rather than judging them
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} talk positively about how families in their class are different — some have two mums, some speak another language at home, some celebrate different holidays — and see this as interesting rather than strange?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 词汇：理解他人
topics.description: 认识并使用理解他人的关键词汇——共情、视角、善良、公平、社区、相似、不同和关心——并理解这些词语描述的是真实的思维和感受习惯。
evidence: Use the word 'empathy' correctly and distinguish it from 'sympathy' — e.g. 'Empathy means I try to feel what they feel'
Explain what 'perspective' and 'point of view' mean and demonstrate by describing how two people might see the same event differently
Use words like 'community', 'belonging', and 'inclusion' accurately when talking about their school or neighbourhood
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} sees someone who seems sad or left out, can they describe what that person might be feeling using words like 'empathy' or 'perspective' — showing they're thinking about the other person, not just themselves?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 不同的生活与经历
topics.description: 理解人们的生活和经历可能与自己的大不相同——有些孩子面临残疾、贫困、家庭困难或初到异国等挑战——培养同情心而非评判
evidence: Describe at least two ways another child's life experience might differ significantly from their own
Explain why it's important not to judge someone based on their circumstances
Suggest a kind action they could take to help someone facing a difficult situation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a new child joins {{name}}'s class who doesn't speak much English or whose family situation is very different, does {{name}} show understanding and try to include them rather than avoiding them?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 公平、平等与公正
topics.description: 理解公平的含义以及为什么它很重要——认识到公平并不总是意味着平等（每个人得到相同的东西），而可能意味着公正（每个人得到他们需要的东西），并在集体情境中应用这一理解。
evidence: Explain the difference between treating everyone the same and treating everyone fairly
Give an example of a situation where equal treatment wouldn't be fair
Apply fairness thinking when sharing resources or making group decisions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a child with a broken arm gets extra time to finish a task at school, can {{name}} explain why that's fair even though other children don't get extra time?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 换位思考
topics.description: 通过想象他人在特定情境下可能有的感受来练习换位思考——使用“如果这件事发生在你身上，你会有什么感受？”等提示语，并在阅读故事或真实互动中运用这一能力。
evidence: Describe how a character in a story feels and give reasons based on the plot
Predict how another child would feel in a described scenario
Use perspective-taking during a real disagreement to understand the other person's view
topics.assessmentPrompt: When reading a story together, can {{name}} pause and explain how a character might be feeling and why — putting themselves in the character's shoes?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 词汇：社会意识
topics.description: 认识并使用社会意识相关词汇——包括刻板印象、偏见、歧视、平等、公平、偏向、同情心和公正——并理解这些密切相关概念之间的区别
evidence: Explain what 'stereotype' and 'prejudice' mean and give an example of each from everyday life
Use words like 'equality', 'equity', and 'bias' correctly when discussing a scenario — e.g. 'That's not equity because not everyone got what they needed'
Identify an example of discrimination in a story or news article and explain why it is unfair using the correct vocabulary
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears a classmate say something that groups all people of a certain background together, can they explain why that's a stereotype and how it differs from a fact about an individual person?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 偏见与歧视
topics.description: 理解偏见和歧视对个人和社区的影响——因为身份而受到不公平对待会造成真正的伤害——并认识到自己有责任反对偏见和歧视。
evidence: Define prejudice and discrimination in their own words with examples
Describe the emotional and social impact of discrimination on the person experiencing it
Identify at least one action they can personally take to challenge unfair treatment
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees someone at school being excluded or teased because of their race, religion, or disability, can they explain why that's wrong and describe what they could do about it?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 质疑自己的偏见
topics.description: 反思自己的假设和偏见——认识到每个人都会对他人抱有下意识的假设，而主动质疑这些假设是一种持续的练习，能带来更多的公平和同理心。
evidence: Describe a time they made an assumption about someone that turned out to be wrong
Explain what unconscious bias means in simple terms
Describe a strategy for checking their own assumptions, such as asking questions before judging
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} catch themselves making an assumption about someone — like assuming a quiet child is unfriendly — and then question whether that assumption is fair?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 刻板印象与个体差异
topics.description: 识别刻板印象——基于性别、种族、年龄或其他特征对人群形成的过于简化的看法——并理解刻板印象是不公平的，因为它们忽视了个体差异
evidence: Define what a stereotype is in their own words
Identify a common stereotype and explain why it is inaccurate
Challenge a stereotype they encounter by giving a counter-example
topics.assessmentPrompt: If someone says 'boys don't cry' or 'girls aren't good at maths', can {{name}} explain why those statements are unfair stereotypes that don't apply to everyone?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 世界包含许多文化、传统和信仰体系
topics.description: 理解世界包含许多文化、传统和信仰体系，学习他人的观点能丰富我们自己的理解——培养对文化多样性的真诚好奇与尊重
evidence: Describe a cultural practice different from their own and explain what they find interesting about it
Ask respectful questions to learn about someone else's traditions or beliefs
Explain why understanding different cultures makes communities stronger
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} show genuine interest when learning about how families from different cultures celebrate, eat, or worship — asking questions respectfully rather than dismissing things that are unfamiliar?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 系统性不平等与盟友行动
topics.description: 超越“对所有人一视同仁”的观念，理解无论个人努力或意图如何，结构性优势和劣势都客观存在；探索系统性不平等的具体例子（教育成就差距、性别薪酬差距、领导层代表性不足）；区分个人偏见与结构性歧视；理解交叉性——身份的多个方面如何相互作用；培养基于证据而非怜悯的明智同情；探索在实践中成为真正盟友意味着什么。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between treating everyone 'the same' and actually making things fair — and give a real example of a structural barrier that means two people starting in different positions face unequal opportunities even if they try equally hard?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 同情与共情
topics.description: 区分同情（“我为你感到难过”）和共情（“我理解你正在经历什么”）；培养积极倾听技能：反映、复述、提出开放式问题、克制过快解决问题的冲动；理解共情好奇心是对他人内心世界的真正兴趣；练习在他人痛苦时陪伴而不试图修复或淡化他们的经历；理解替代性创伤和同情疲劳，以及有共情力的人如何在陪伴他人的同时保护自己的身心健康。
topics.assessmentPrompt: When a friend is going through something really difficult, can {{name}} describe what makes a listener genuinely helpful — and explain the difference between empathy and sympathy, using an example of something that sounds supportive but actually isn't?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 全球公民意识
topics.description: 理解在一个相互联系的世界中作为公民意味着什么，一个地方的决定会影响其他地方的人们；通过共情的视角探索全球性问题（气候正义、被迫移民、全球健康、贫困），区分事实与价值判断；面对我们对亲近之人的义务与对远方陌生人的义务之间的伦理张力；引入基于证据的给予和有效利他主义作为思考全球责任的一种框架；形成个人对全球公民意识的理性立场，承认其复杂性。
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads about a crisis happening in another country, can they describe how they think about their own responsibility — and name one practical thing young people can genuinely do about large-scale problems rather than just feeling helpless?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 寻求帮助
topics.description: 在需要时向朋友、老师或家人寻求帮助，并理解寻求帮助是力量的表现，而不是软弱。
evidence: Approach an appropriate person and ask for help clearly
Identify who to go to for different kinds of help (academic, emotional, practical)
Explain why asking for help is sensible rather than something to be embarrassed about
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is stuck on something at school or feeling worried about something, will they ask a teacher or friend for help rather than struggling in silence?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 倾听他人
topics.description: 别人说话时认真听——看着说话的人，等别人说完再开口，并且回应对方说的内容，而不只是讲自己的想法。
evidence: Face the speaker and maintain attention while someone else is talking
Wait until the other person has finished before responding
Respond to what was actually said rather than changing the subject to their own idea
topics.assessmentPrompt: When a friend is telling {{name}} about their weekend, does {{name}} actually listen and ask questions about it — rather than immediately jumping in to talk about their own weekend?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 成为好朋友
topics.description: 理解什么样的人才是好朋友——善良、诚实、可靠、接纳他人——并识别不友好的行为，如霸道、排挤他人或说刻薄的话
evidence: List at least four qualities of a good friend
Identify unfriendly behaviour in a story or real situation
Reflect on a time they were a good friend and explain what they did
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what makes a good friend and recognise when someone — including themselves — isn't being a good friend?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 轮流与分享
topics.description: 轮流做事、分享材料，并与他人合作玩耍——理解当每个人都得到公平机会时，集体活动会更好，等待轮到自己也是好朋友的一部分
evidence: Take turns in a game or group activity without needing adult reminders
Share materials willingly during a shared task or playtime
Explain why taking turns makes games and group work more fun for everyone
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is playing a board game with friends or siblings, can they wait for their turn and share the pieces without grabbing or getting upset?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 词汇：与他人合作
topics.description: 认识并使用与他人合作相关的词汇——合作、分享、轮流、团队、倾听、同意、礼貌地表达不同意见和包容——并理解这些词语描述了友谊和小组活动所依赖的习惯。
evidence: Use 'cooperate' and 'compromise' correctly — e.g. 'We cooperated by taking turns choosing the game'
Explain what 'active listening' means and demonstrate it: facing the speaker, not interrupting, responding to what was said
Use 'share', 'take turns', and 'include' to describe how they work with others in a group activity
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is working on something with a friend or sibling, can they use words like 'cooperate' or 'take turns' to describe what they're doing — and actually practise those things?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 沟通词汇
topics.description: 认识并使用健康沟通和冲突相关的词汇——自信、被动、攻击、妥协、冲突、解决、调解、旁观者、挺身而出者和同伴压力——并理解这些不同方法之间的区别。
evidence: Use 'assertive' correctly and distinguish it from 'aggressive' — e.g. 'Being assertive means saying what I need calmly'
Explain what 'conflict resolution' means and describe one strategy such as using 'I feel...' statements
Use words like 'negotiate', 'boundary', and 'respect' accurately in a discussion about friendships
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} and a friend have a disagreement, can they describe it using words like 'conflict' or 'compromise' — and explain how assertive communication is different from aggressive or passive behaviour?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 友谊会随时间变化
topics.description: 理解友谊会随时间变化——朋友之间渐渐疏远或形成新的友谊都是正常的——并学会结交新朋友和应对友谊变化的方法，而不会觉得自己有什么问题。
evidence: Explain that friendships changing is normal and doesn't mean something is wrong
Describe a strategy for making new friends, such as joining a club or inviting someone to play
Talk about a friendship that changed and how they handled it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s best friend starts spending more time with someone else, can they handle it without falling apart — understanding that friendships shift and they can make new friends too?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 解决朋友间的分歧
topics.description: 通过交谈解决与同伴之间的小分歧——说出自己的感受，倾听对方的想法，找到双方都能接受的折中办法或解决方案。
evidence: Explain their own point of view calmly during a disagreement
Listen to the other person's perspective without interrupting
Suggest a compromise or solution that addresses both sides
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} and a friend disagree about which game to play at break time, can they talk it through and find a compromise — rather than one person always getting their way or the argument escalating?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 小组中的角色
topics.description: 了解人们在小组中扮演的不同角色——领导者、支持者、调解者、点子大王——并认识到高效的小组需要各种角色搭配，而不是每个人都想当领导者。
evidence: Name at least three different roles people can play in a group
Identify their own preferred role and describe its strengths
Explain why groups work better when different people take different roles
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a group project, can {{name}} recognise that they don't always have to be in charge — and that sometimes the group works better when they support someone else's idea rather than pushing their own?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 在小组中好好合作
topics.description: 作为小组的一员有效工作——贡献自己的想法，倾听别人的想法，承担公平的一份任务，并支持小组达成共同目标。
evidence: Contribute at least one idea during a group discussion
Listen to and build on another group member's idea
Complete their assigned part of a group task on time
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} has to do a group project at school, do they pull their weight — sharing ideas and doing their part — rather than sitting back or trying to take over?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 自信表达
topics.description: 使用自信的沟通方式——清楚、尊重地表达自己的需求、观点和界限，既不强势（咄咄逼人/强求）也不被动（妥协/沉默）——包括在感觉不对劲时勇敢说“不”。
evidence: Explain the difference between assertive, aggressive, and passive responses
Role-play saying no in a peer pressure scenario
Express a personal boundary clearly and respectfully in a real situation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If friends want {{name}} to do something they're uncomfortable with — like excluding another child or breaking a rule — can {{name}} say 'I don't want to do that' firmly but politely?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 给予和接受反馈
topics.description: 给予和接受建设性反馈——以有帮助而非伤害的方式告诉别人他们做得好的地方和可以改进的地方，并接受关于自己作品的反馈而不变得防御。
evidence: Give feedback that includes both a specific positive point and a constructive suggestion
Receive feedback about their own work without getting upset or dismissive
Explain why constructive feedback helps people improve
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reviews a classmate's story and finds mistakes, can they give feedback that's helpful — like 'I loved this part, and this bit could be clearer' — rather than just saying 'it's wrong'?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 帮助他人解决冲突
topics.description: 调解他人之间的冲突——当两个朋友争吵时，倾听双方的说法，帮助他们理解彼此的观点，并引导他们达成公平的解决方案。
evidence: Listen to both sides of a conflict without taking sides initially
Help each person articulate their perspective to the other
Suggest a fair resolution or compromise that both parties can accept
topics.assessmentPrompt: If two of {{name}}'s friends are arguing and both come to {{name}} for support, can {{name}} help them talk it out fairly rather than just taking one side?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 人际关系中的自我反思
topics.description: 反思自己在人际关系中的角色和行为——识别与他人互动时的模式，理解自己对友谊的贡献，并找出作为朋友或团队成员可以改进的地方。
evidence: Identify a pattern in their own social behaviour, such as always wanting to lead or avoiding confrontation
Describe what they do well in relationships and one area they'd like to improve
Set a specific social goal, such as 'I will ask others for their ideas before sharing mine'
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} honestly reflect on their friendships and say something like 'I think I sometimes take over in group work and I'm trying to listen more' — showing awareness of their own social patterns?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 社交线索与群体动态
topics.description: 理解青少年同伴群体中的潜台词、间接沟通和社交线索；分析内群体和外群体动态的心理机制，以及为什么归属感可能以排斥他人为代价；理解八卦作为社交联结和地位机制的作用及其代价；制定在不违背价值观的情况下应对社交等级的策略；区分同伴环境中的自信与攻击性；理解如何应对排斥——无论是亲身经历还是目睹他人经历。
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} senses tension or unspoken 'undercurrents' in a group of friends, can they describe what social cues they pick up on and explain the difference between being assertive and being aggressive when they choose to address it?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 诚实的对话与冲突修复
topics.description: 理解如何进行诚实、直接的对话，在解决问题时不攻击对方；应用非暴力沟通的原则（观察、感受、需要、请求）；理解重大冲突后的修复过程：不设防地承担责任，真诚道歉（不推卸责任），并通过长期一致的行为重建信任；区分真正的道歉和保全面子的‘对不起’；理解友谊如何通过经历冲突而非回避冲突来存活并加深。
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} falls out seriously with a friend, can they describe what makes an apology actually repair a relationship — and what the difference is between a genuine apology and just saying sorry to end the awkwardness?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 领导风格与影响力
topics.description: 区分不同的领导风格（指令型、民主型、服务型、变革型），并理解每种风格分别在什么时候合适；理解在团队中的影响力伴随着责任，并探索通过激励来领导与通过强迫来领导之间的区别；练习包容性领导：主动为较安静的成员和不同的观点创造空间；理解影响力的道德规范，以及说服与操纵之间的界限；探索同伴关系中的同意与强迫的概念；反思他们希望在自己的社区中产生什么样的影响。
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were leading a group project where one person was dominating all the decisions, can they describe two different leadership approaches they could take and explain why the most authoritative person in a group isn't always the best leader?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 行为与后果
topics.description: 理解行为会带来后果——你的选择既会影响自己，也会影响他人——并开始在做之前思考可能会发生什么。
evidence: Describe what happened as a consequence of a specific action they took
Predict what might happen if they choose a particular action before doing it
Explain that actions can have good or bad consequences for themselves and others
topics.assessmentPrompt: Before {{name}} does something — like taking a toy from a sibling or running in the corridor — can they stop and think about what might happen as a result?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 日常安全意识
topics.description: 在日常生活中保护自己的安全——了解关于道路、陌生人、水和互联网的基本安全规则——并知道谁是可信赖的成年人，以及什么时候应该告诉他们事情
evidence: State at least three basic safety rules and explain why each matters
Name their trusted adults and describe when they should tell them something
Demonstrate safe behaviour in a familiar everyday situation without being reminded
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know their basic safety rules — like not going off with someone they don't know, looking both ways before crossing, and telling you if something online makes them uncomfortable?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 对与错的选择
topics.description: 在熟悉的日常情境中知道对与错的差别——理解关于诚实、不伤害他人、尊重他人财物和公平的基本规则——即使做正确的事更难，也选择去做
evidence: Identify the right and wrong choice in a simple moral scenario
Choose to be honest even when lying would avoid trouble
Explain why rules about not hurting others and being honest matter
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} accidentally breaks something at a friend's house, do they tell the truth about it rather than hiding it or blaming someone else?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 规则和约定是存在的
topics.description: 理解规则和约定为什么存在——它们帮助保证人们的安全、让事情公平，并帮助团队更好地合作——并且愿意遵守约定的规则，而不是只在被监督时才遵守。
evidence: Explain the reason behind at least two rules at home or school
Follow a rule consistently without needing to be reminded or monitored
Describe what would happen if nobody followed the rules in a specific context
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} follow the class rules or family agreements even when no adult is watching — not because they're scared of punishment but because they understand why the rules matter?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 词汇：做决定和保持安全
topics.description: 认识并使用与做决定和保持安全相关的词汇——选择、后果、规则、安全、公平、诚实、可信赖的成年人、对与错——并理解清楚地命名这些想法有助于做出更好的选择。
evidence: Explain what 'consequence' means and give an example of a positive and a negative consequence of a choice
Use 'responsible' and 'safe' correctly when talking about everyday decisions — e.g. 'The responsible choice is to tell an adult'
Define 'rule' and 'fairness' and explain why rules exist using their own examples from school or home
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} faces a situation where they need to make a choice — like whether to tell the truth about something that went wrong — can they talk through what might happen using words like 'consequence' and 'fair'?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 基础数字公民素养
topics.description: 理解基础的数字公民素养——在网上友善待人、保护个人信息、认识到屏幕背后的人是拥有真实感受的真实的人，以及知道如果网上有什么让他们感到不舒服时该怎么做
evidence: State at least three rules for staying safe and being kind online
Explain why hurtful messages online are just as harmful as saying them in person
Describe what they should do if someone online makes them feel uncomfortable or asks for personal information
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is chatting with friends online or playing multiplayer games, do they treat people kindly and know not to share personal details like their address or school name?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 旁观者与挺身而出者
topics.description: 理解旁观者的角色——当有人看到不友善或不公平的行为时，他们可以选择：做一个被动的旁观者（什么都不做）、加入其中，或者做一个挺身而出者（说出来或寻求帮助）——并培养成为挺身而出者的信心。
evidence: Explain the difference between a bystander and an upstander
Describe at least two safe actions an upstander can take
Give an example of a time they or someone they know stood up for someone else
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a group of children being mean to someone at school, do they have the courage to say something, walk away with the person being targeted, or tell a teacher — rather than just watching?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 停一停，想一想，再选择
topics.description: 面对选择时，使用一个简单的决策过程——停下来思考，找出可选方案，考虑每个方案可能带来的后果，然后再做选择——而不是冲动行事。
evidence: Describe at least two options when facing a decision
Predict a likely consequence for each option
Explain which option they chose and why, showing they considered the consequences
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} faces a tricky choice — like whether to tell the teacher that a friend cheated — can they think through their options and the consequences rather than just reacting?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 认识欺凌
topics.description: 理解什么是欺凌——反复做出意图伤害他人的行为，包括身体欺凌、言语欺凌、社交欺凌（排挤、散布谣言）和网络欺凌——并知道欺凌永远是错误的，以及在自己遭遇或看到欺凌时该怎么做。
evidence: Define bullying and distinguish it from a one-off conflict
Name at least three forms of bullying including cyberbullying
Describe the steps they should take if they experience or witness bullying
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand the difference between a one-off argument and bullying, and do they know what to do if they see someone being bullied — rather than just ignoring it?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 词汇：伦理与公民意识
topics.description: 认识并使用伦理与公民意识相关词汇——欺凌、网络欺凌、旁观者、挺身而出者、同伴压力、数字公民、权利、责任和合乎伦理的——并理解这些紧密相关术语之间的区别。
evidence: Explain what 'ethics' means in their own words and give an example of an ethical dilemma
Use 'citizen', 'rights', and 'responsibilities' correctly — e.g. 'A citizen has the right to vote and the responsibility to follow laws'
Define 'consent' and 'integrity' and explain why they matter in relationships and online behaviour
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw someone being treated unkindly online and you asked them about it, could they explain the difference between being a bystander and an upstander — and what 'digital citizenship' means?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 社区中的权利与责任
topics.description: 理解作为社区一员的权利和责任——每个人都有权受到尊重并感到安全，同时享有权利也意味着有责任以同样的方式对待他人。
evidence: Name at least three rights that every child has (e.g., safety, education, respect)
Describe the responsibilities that go along with those rights
Give an example of how exercising their own rights responsibly supports the community
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that they have a right to feel safe at school AND a responsibility to help make school safe for others — understanding that rights and responsibilities go together?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 困难的道德选择
topics.description: 理解道德决定并不总是黑白分明——有时没有完美的答案，合理的人也可能有不同意见——并练习在做出困难选择时权衡相互冲突的价值观。
evidence: Describe a moral dilemma where both sides have valid points
Explain the values in tension (e.g., loyalty vs safety, honesty vs kindness)
Describe how they would make a decision in such a situation and justify their reasoning
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s friend tells them a secret but the secret involves something dangerous, can {{name}} think through the tension between loyalty to their friend and the need to keep someone safe?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 现实世界问题中的伦理
topics.description: 评估他们在现实生活中遇到的伦理问题——例如环境责任、体育公平、数字伦理或社会正义——考虑多种视角，并形成有理有据的个人立场。
evidence: Identify an ethical issue and describe at least two different perspectives on it
Explain which perspective they agree with most and give reasons for their position
Acknowledge that the other perspective has some validity even if they disagree
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} discuss a real issue — like whether it's fair that some children have more than others, or whether animals should be kept in zoos — considering different viewpoints and explaining their own position thoughtfully?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 同伴压力与如何拒绝
topics.description: 理解同伴压力——朋友和同龄人可能对你的选择和举止产生的影响——并学会一些策略，用来拒绝那些你知道不对或让你不舒服的事情。
evidence: Define peer pressure in their own words and give a real-world example
Describe at least two strategies for resisting peer pressure, such as walking away or using humour
Explain why going along with something wrong to fit in usually makes things worse
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s friends dare them to do something risky or unkind — like shoplifting a sweet or posting an embarrassing photo of someone — can they resist the pressure and explain why they won't do it?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 风险、不确定性与认知偏差
topics.description: 区分风险（概率已知的决策）和不确定性（结果未知的决策）；识别扭曲风险评估的认知偏差：可得性启发（根据例子容易想到的程度判断可能性）、现时偏差（过度重视眼前而忽视未来）、乐观偏差（低估个人风险）和群体思维；理解青少年大脑在生物学上倾向于更高的风险容忍度；将结构化决策框架应用于真实选择；理解在仅靠事实无法决定答案的决策中个人价值观的作用。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why taking a risk isn't always irrational — and describe one cognitive bias that causes people to misjudge risk in their everyday decisions, such as why teenagers tend to underestimate certain dangers?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 网络身份与虚假信息
topics.description: 理解网络身份的伦理，以及线上与线下身份保持一致的重要性；解释推荐算法和过滤气泡如何限制信息接触；评估虚假信息的心理机制：它为何传播、聪明人为何相信，以及如何运用来源评估（横向阅读、核查证据、识别情绪操纵）；理解分享图片或个人信息时的数字同意；探讨人工智能、监控和数据隐私对日常生活的伦理影响；反思负责任的内容创作和网络影响力。
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} sees a convincing claim shared on social media, can they describe their process for deciding whether to believe or share it — and explain why even intelligent people are regularly misled online?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 伦理框架与道德推理
topics.description: 介绍三种主要的伦理框架：后果主义（根据行为的结果和整体福祉来判断行为）、义务论（根据是否遵守规则和义务来判断行为，而不考虑后果）和美德伦理（根据行为所反映的品格来判断行为）；将每种框架应用于现实世界的道德困境：气候责任、人工智能伦理、公民不服从、财富不平等、医疗资源分配；理解每种框架的优势和局限性；培养仔细道德推理的能力——系统思考伦理问题的能力，而不仅仅依赖直觉或群体意见。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} take a real ethical dilemma — like whether it's ever right to break a rule to help someone — and explain how a consequentialist, a deontologist, and someone focused on virtue ethics would each think about it differently, and which approach they find most persuasive?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 说出你的感受
topics.description: 注意自己正在感受什么，并给它起个名字——能够说出一种情绪，是理解和调节它的第一步。
evidence: emotional literacy research
Fostering Emotional Literacy in Young Children (HeadStart.gov)
emotion vocabulary development 4-11 years (PMC)
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} seems upset, excited, or frustrated, can they stop and tell you what emotion they're feeling — even if they can't fully explain why?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 自我认知词汇
topics.description: 认识并使用自我反思的词汇——自我意识、反思、模式、触发、假设、影响、视角和注意——并理解用准确的词语描述这些内心体验，能让我们更容易理解和谈论它们
evidence: Use words like 'reflect', 'pattern', and 'trigger' accurately when describing their own behaviour — e.g. 'I notice a pattern: I get frustrated when I rush'
Explain what 'self-awareness' means in their own words and give a personal example
Use the word 'perspective' correctly — e.g. 'From my perspective it felt unfair, but I can see theirs too'
topics.assessmentPrompt: After a difficult moment — a falling-out with a friend or a frustrating task — can {{name}} talk about what happened using words like 'trigger' or 'reflect', showing they're thinking about their own reactions rather than just what the other person did?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 感受与行为
topics.description: 理解感受和行为是分开的——你可以有强烈的感受，但不必马上采取行动。
evidence: emotion regulation development research
Effects of Age and Gender in Emotion Regulation (PMC 2020)
expressive control to emotion regulation (PMC)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand that feeling angry, scared, or jealous doesn't mean they have to act on it immediately — that there's a gap between the feeling and what they choose to do next?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 觉察自己的反应模式
topics.description: 留意自己反应中的规律——比如“当我累了、被冷落或突然被提问时，我往往会这样反应”。
evidence: middle childhood self-reliance in emotion regulation
7-year developmental shift in self-understanding research
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} ever noticed a pattern in how they react — for example, that they get more upset at certain times of day, or that a particular type of situation reliably triggers a strong feeling?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 你对他人的影响
topics.description: 反思自己的行为如何影响他人——不仅考虑你的本意，还要考虑对他人实际产生的影响。
evidence: Describe how something they said or did affected someone else — e.g. 'When I didn't include them, they looked upset'
Predict what might happen before acting — e.g. 'If I take the last one without asking, they'll feel it's unfair'
After a conflict, explain what they could have done differently and what effect that would have had
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} think about how something they said or did might have felt to the other person — not just what they meant by it, but what the impact actually was?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 质疑第一印象
topics.description: 注意自己对社交情境的第一判断可能有误——你对他人行为原因的假设并不总是事实。
evidence: Pause before reacting to a classmate's behaviour and consider an alternative explanation — e.g. 'Maybe they bumped me by accident, not on purpose'
Describe a time they assumed the worst about someone's intention and later found out they were wrong
When told about an ambiguous social situation, suggest at least two possible reasons for the other person's behaviour instead of jumping to one conclusion
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} felt sure someone was being unfair or unkind, could they pause and consider whether there might be another explanation for what happened?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 随时间成长
topics.description: 反思自己随时间的变化——现在遇到的挑战并非一成不变，注意到自己已经发生的变化能建立真正的自我认识。
evidence: emotion vocabulary development continues to age 11 (PMC)
self-reflection importance in children research
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} look back over the past year or two and point to something they used to find really difficult that they now handle better — and explain what changed?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 应对生活中的变化
topics.description: 理解变化是生活中正常的一部分——比如开始上学、换新老师、家里添了小宝宝或搬家——并学会一些简单的应对策略
evidence: Name at least two changes they have experienced and how they felt
Identify a person they can talk to when a change feels hard
Describe one strategy that helps them cope with change, such as keeping a familiar routine
topics.assessmentPrompt: When something changes in {{name}}'s life — like getting a new teacher at school — can they talk about how it makes them feel and think of ways to help themselves adjust?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 从错误中学习
topics.description: 理解犯错是学习中正常的一部分，每个人——包括大人——都会犯错，并开始将错误视为学习的机会，而不是放弃的理由。
evidence: Describe a time they made a mistake and what they learned from it
Respond to a mistake by trying again rather than giving up
Explain why mistakes help people learn
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets an answer wrong in class or messes up during a game, do they bounce back and keep trying rather than shutting down or saying 'I can't do it'?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 耐心与延迟满足
topics.description: 在等待想要的东西时不会变得非常烦躁——在日常生活中练习耐心和延迟满足，比如排队等待、等待点心或等待帮助
evidence: Wait for their turn in a game or activity without constant complaints
Describe what they do to help themselves wait, such as thinking about something else
Explain why sometimes we have to wait and that it is a skill they can practise
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has to wait their turn for something they really want — like a go on the iPad or being served dinner — can they wait without a big fuss?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 简单的冷静策略
topics.description: 在感到难过或不知所措时，使用简单的冷静策略——比如深呼吸、数到十，或者去一个安静的地方——并明白这些方法能帮助身体和心情平静下来。
evidence: Demonstrate at least two calming strategies when prompted
Choose to use a calming strategy independently during a real upset
Explain in simple terms why calming down helps them think better
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} gets really upset — say they lose a game or argue with a sibling — can they use a strategy like deep breaths to calm themselves down rather than staying in meltdown mode?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 表达强烈情绪的词
topics.description: 认识并使用管理强烈情绪的关键词——平静、策略、应对、平复、耐心、不知所措和深呼吸——并理解拥有这些词是运用它们的第一步
evidence: Use words like 'frustrated', 'anxious', 'overwhelmed', and 'disappointed' accurately to describe how they feel in difficult moments
Explain what 'calm down' strategies are in their own words and name at least two they have tried (e.g. deep breaths, counting, walking away)
Distinguish between similar feelings — e.g. explain the difference between being angry and being disappointed
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is feeling really upset or frustrated, can they use words like 'I need to calm down' or 'I'm feeling overwhelmed' instead of just acting out?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 把任务拆分成小步骤
topics.description: 把有挑战的任务拆分成更小、更容易完成的步骤，而不是被整个任务吓倒——并在过程中庆祝每一个进步。
evidence: Take a challenging task and list at least three smaller steps to complete it
Start with the first step rather than procrastinating on the whole task
Acknowledge progress after completing each step
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has a big school project that feels overwhelming, can they break it down into smaller steps — like 'first I'll research, then I'll write the introduction' — rather than panicking about the whole thing?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 选择合适的应对策略
topics.description: 理解不同情况需要不同的应对策略——对生气有效的方法可能对悲伤无效，在学校有帮助的方法可能和在家有帮助的方法不同。
evidence: Name at least two different coping strategies and explain when each one is most useful
Choose an appropriate strategy based on the specific situation and emotion
Reflect on a time a strategy didn't work and explain what they might try instead
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} recognise that when they're angry they need to do something physical like walk around, but when they're worried they need to talk it through — rather than using the same approach for every difficult feeling?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 成长型思维
topics.description: 理解成长型思维的概念——能力与智力可以通过努力、练习和好方法不断提升，而不是固定型思维所认为的要么擅长、要么不擅长。
evidence: Explain the difference between growth mindset and fixed mindset in their own words
Use 'yet' language when describing something they find difficult
Give an example of something they got better at through practice and effort
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} finds something difficult like learning to ride a bike or mastering times tables, do they say 'I can't do it YET' rather than 'I'm just not good at this'?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 积极的自我对话
topics.description: 用积极的自我对话来应对困难情境——把“我真笨”或“我永远做不到”这类没用的想法，换成“这很难，但我可以继续努力”或“我以前也做成过难事”这类鼓励自己的想法。
evidence: Give an example of an unhelpful thought and rephrase it as a helpful one
Use positive self-talk aloud or in writing when facing a challenge
Explain how the words we say to ourselves affect how we feel and perform
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is struggling with homework and starts saying 'I'm rubbish at this', can they catch that thought and replace it with something more helpful like 'I just need to try a different approach'?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 词汇：韧性与自我
topics.description: 认识并使用关于韧性和自我管理的词汇——包括调节、韧性、成长型思维、固定型思维、自我对话、触发点、挫折、坚持和痛苦——并理解每个词在实际中的含义。
evidence: Explain what 'resilience' means in their own words and give an example of a time they kept going when something was hard
Use 'growth mindset' correctly — e.g. 'I can't do it yet, but I can improve with practice'
Define 'self-regulation' and describe a strategy they use to manage frustration or setbacks
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s team loses a match or they fail a test, can they talk about what happened using words like 'resilience' or 'growth mindset' — showing they understand the difference between giving up and bouncing back?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 个人应对工具箱
topics.description: 反思哪些自我调节和应对策略最适合自己，建立一个可以在不同情况下使用的“工具箱”，并与他人分享有效的方法。
evidence: Describe at least three personal coping strategies and when each is most effective
Recommend a strategy to a friend based on the friend's specific situation
Evaluate whether a strategy they tried worked well and explain their reasoning
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you 'When I'm stressed about exams I go for a walk and that helps, but when I'm sad I need to talk to someone' — showing they know their own coping toolkit?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 个人目标设定
topics.description: 设定切合实际的个人目标，制定简单的实现计划，监控自己的进度，并在方法不奏效时调整策略
evidence: Write or state a specific, achievable personal goal with a timeframe
Describe the steps they will take to reach the goal
Review their progress and adjust their plan when something isn't working
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} set themselves a goal — like improving their swimming or finishing a book series — and actually work towards it step by step, adjusting their plan if needed?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 心理韧性与重新振作
topics.description: 理解心理韧性是指从挫折中恢复、适应困难环境并继续前进的能力——认识到心理韧性是一种通过经历培养出来的技能，而不是天生就有或没有的特质。
evidence: Define resilience in their own words and explain why it matters
Describe a time they bounced back from a setback and what helped them recover
Explain that resilience grows through experience and that struggling doesn't mean you're weak
topics.assessmentPrompt: After a real disappointment — like not getting a part in the school play or failing a test they studied for — can {{name}} feel upset but then pick themselves up and figure out what to do next?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 时间与注意力管理
topics.description: 有效管理自己的时间和注意力——优先处理任务，减少干扰，即使任务不那么有趣也能保持专注
evidence: Create a simple plan for completing multiple tasks in a sensible order
Identify their own common distractions and describe strategies to manage them
Complete a less enjoyable task before a more enjoyable one without constant reminders
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} has homework to finish but also wants to play a game, can they manage their time — doing the homework first or setting a timer — rather than always needing you to enforce it?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 良性压力与不良压力
topics.description: 区分良性压力（能激发动力、有成效的压力）和不良压力（有害的、令人不堪重负的压力）；解释生理压力反应（战斗-逃跑-僵住反应、HPA轴）以及长期压力如何影响身心；识别青少年常见的压力源（学业压力、社会比较、身体变化、对未来的不确定感）；评估基于证据的应对策略（运动、睡眠、正念、社会支持、表达性写作）；识别压力已演变为焦虑或抑郁的警告信号，并知道去哪里寻求帮助。
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is under pressure from exams or social situations, can they name two or three strategies that genuinely help them manage the stress — and explain why each one actually works, not just that it 'makes them feel better'?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 习惯与动机
topics.description: 理解习惯形成的提示-惯例-奖励循环，以及如何有意识地设计新习惯；区分内在动机（因为事情本身的价值而做）和外在动机（奖励/惩罚），并理解各自何时更有效；理解拖延主要是一个情绪调节问题（逃避不适），而不是时间管理失败；应用自我决定理论（自主性、胜任感、归属感）来增强内在动机；设计减少期望行为阻力的环境。
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} keeps meaning to do something important but finds themselves putting it off, can they explain the real reason people procrastinate — it's not laziness — and describe one practical change they could make to their environment to make starting easier?

topics.subject: Personal & Social Development
topics.name: 在逆境中成长
topics.description: 理解面对严重挑战可以在三个方面带来真正的成长：对生活的新视角、改善的人际关系以及增强的个人能力感（创伤后成长）；区分真正的成长与有毒的积极（“一切事情的发生都是有原因的”）和否认；理解韧性并不意味着不受逆境影响，而是通过逆境恢复和成长；基于意义建构发展处理挫折的个人哲学；探索如何在不轻视他人经历的情况下支持他们度过严重困难。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} ever come through something genuinely hard and found it changed them in a meaningful way? Can they explain what post-traumatic growth means and how it differs from just 'getting over it' or pretending something difficult was fine?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 动物的伪装
topics.description: 知道许多动物会使用伪装——即帮助它们融入周围环境的颜色和花纹——来躲避捕食者或悄悄接近猎物，比如看起来像树叶的叶虫，或者冬天会变白的北极兔。
evidence: Explains that camouflage means blending in with surroundings
Gives at least 3 examples of camouflaged animals
Explains that camouflage helps animals hide from predators or sneak up on food
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} tries to spot a grasshopper in the garden, can they explain that it's hard to see because its green colour helps it hide in the grass — and give other examples of animals that use camouflage?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 动物的家
topics.description: 知道动物会建造或寻找许多不同种类的家——鸟儿筑巢，兔子挖洞，蜜蜂住在蜂巢里，寄居蟹用空壳，蜘蛛结网——这些庇护所保护它们和它们的宝宝
evidence: Names at least 4 different types of animal homes (nest, burrow, hive, web, shell, den, lodge)
Explains that animals need homes for shelter and to keep their babies safe
Matches common animals to their homes
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} where different animals live, can they describe several animal homes — like a bird's nest, a rabbit's burrow, or a bee's hive — and say why animals need shelter?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 动物纪录保持者
topics.description: 认识一些世界动物纪录保持者——蓝鲸是史上最大的动物，猎豹是最快的陆地动物，吸蜜蜂鸟是最小的鸟，长颈鹿是最高的——并把它们的体型与熟悉的东西做比较。
evidence: Names at least 4 animal record-holders with their record (fastest, biggest, tallest, smallest, etc.)
Compares an animal's size or ability to a familiar reference
Shows enthusiasm for superlative animal facts
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} which animal is the fastest or the biggest in the world, can they name some record-holders like the cheetah or blue whale and compare their size to something familiar, like 'a blue whale is as long as three buses'?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 动物无处不在
topics.description: 知道动物生活在世界各地——在陆地上、水中和空中——每个大洲，甚至冰冷的南极洲，都是动物的家园，每种动物都适应它们所生活的环境。
evidence: Names at least 3 animals from different environments (e.g., forest, ocean, desert)
States that animals live on land, in water, and some can fly
Recognises that animals live on every continent
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you show {{name}} pictures of a polar bear, a parrot, a camel, and a penguin, can they tell you that animals live in all sorts of different places around the world?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 动物怎样生宝宝
topics.description: 知道不同的动物生宝宝的方式不一样——有些动物会下蛋（比如鸟类、爬行动物、鱼类、昆虫），有些动物会直接生出小宝宝（大多数哺乳动物）——而且动物宝宝有的长得像缩小版的大人，有的和爸爸妈妈长得完全不一样。
evidence: Gives examples of animals that lay eggs and animals that give birth to live young
Describes at least one example of a baby that looks different from its parent (e.g., tadpole/frog, caterpillar/butterfly)
Shows curiosity about how different animals have their babies
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a nest with eggs in a nature programme, can they explain that birds lay eggs and the babies hatch out, but dogs and cats have their babies born alive?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 夜行动物
topics.description: 知道有些动物是夜行动物——它们在夜间活动，白天睡觉——而且夜行动物通常有特殊的特征，比如大眼睛（猫头鹰、眼镜猴）、大耳朵（蝙蝠、耳廓狐）或敏感的胡须，帮助它们在黑暗中寻找食物。
evidence: Explains what 'nocturnal' means
Names at least 3 nocturnal animals (e.g., owl, bat, fox, hedgehog, moth)
Describes one feature that helps a nocturnal animal (e.g., big eyes, echolocation, whiskers)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears an owl hooting at bedtime, can they explain that owls are nocturnal — meaning they sleep during the day and come out at night — and that their big eyes help them see in the dark?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 野生动物、农场动物和宠物
topics.description: 了解野生动物、农场动物和宠物之间的区别——野生动物在自然界中自己寻找食物和住所；农场动物由人们饲养，用来获取食物、羊毛或鸡蛋；宠物是人们为了陪伴而饲养的动物——并知道应该与野生动物保持距离观察
evidence: Sorts animals into wild, farm, and pet categories with examples
Explains one key difference between each category
Understands that wild animals should be observed, not approached
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a fox in the garden, can they explain that it's a wild animal — different from their pet cat or a farm sheep — and that wild animals look after themselves and shouldn't be touched?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 动物的交流方式
topics.description: 了解动物会用许多不同的方式交流——鸟儿唱歌是为了吸引伴侣和保卫领地，鲸鱼能隔着广阔的海洋互相呼唤，蜜蜂用舞蹈告诉其他蜜蜂食物在哪里，狼用嚎叫让狼群保持团结，萤火虫则用闪光发信号——交流对动物的生存来说非常重要。
evidence: Describes at least 4 different methods of animal communication (sound, dance, light, scent, body language)
Gives a specific animal example for each method
Explains that animals communicate to find mates, warn of danger, or share food locations
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears birds singing in the morning, can they explain that birdsong is a way of communicating — and describe at least two other ways different animals send messages to each other?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 动物迁徙
topics.description: 了解许多动物会进行令人惊叹的长途旅行，称为迁徙——北极燕鸥从一极飞到另一极，黑脉金斑蝶穿越北美飞行数千英里，角马跟随降雨穿越塞伦盖蒂，座头鲸在极地觅食地和热带繁殖水域之间游动——这些旅行与食物、繁殖和季节有关。
evidence: Defines migration as a regular long journey animals make
Names at least 3 migratory animals with their routes or destinations
Explains that migration is driven by food availability, breeding, or seasonal changes
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learns about the monarch butterfly's journey, can they explain what migration means and name at least two other animals that make long journeys — and say why they travel?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 沙漠动物
topics.description: 探索沙漠中的动物——骆驼、耳廓狐、蝎子、响尾蛇、狐獴——了解沙漠动物如何通过夜间活动、储存水分或脂肪、白天在地下打洞以及长着大耳朵散热来在极端炎热和缺水的环境中生存。
evidence: Names at least 4 desert animals
Explains at least two desert survival adaptations (nocturnal behaviour, water storage, burrowing, large ears for cooling)
Knows deserts can be hot or cold but are always dry
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads about camels in a desert, can they explain at least two ways desert animals cope with the heat and lack of water — like being active at night or having special body features?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 极地动物
topics.description: 探索北极和南极的动物——北方的北极熊、北极狐和海象；南方的企鹅、海豹和信天翁——并了解极地动物如何通过厚厚的皮毛或鲸脂、抱团取暖以及像冬季白毛这样的季节性变化来在极端寒冷中生存。
evidence: Names at least 3 animals each from the Arctic and Antarctic
Explains at least two adaptations for surviving cold (blubber, thick fur, huddling, white camouflage)
Knows polar bears live only in the Arctic and penguins only in the Antarctic/Southern Hemisphere
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a nature programme about the Arctic, can they explain how polar bears stay warm in freezing temperatures and name at least two differences between Arctic animals (north) and Antarctic animals (south)?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 捕食者的捕猎策略
topics.description: 了解捕食者进化出了捕猎策略——狼群集体捕猎，变色龙用长舌头，蜘蛛结网，鳄鱼在水边伏击——而猎物也进化出了防御机制——豪猪的尖刺，臭鼬的喷雾，箭毒蛙的毒素，斑马的条纹迷惑捕食者，装死
evidence: Describes at least 3 predator hunting strategies with examples
Describes at least 3 prey defence mechanisms with examples
Understands the concept of an 'arms race' between predators and prey
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a nature programme showing a lion hunting, can they describe at least two different ways predators catch food and two ways prey animals defend themselves?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林动物
topics.description: 探索热带雨林中的动物——地球上物种最丰富的栖息地。了解雨林分为不同层次（树冠层、林下层、森林地面），每层生活着不同的动物：树冠层里有巨嘴鸟和猴子，地面上有美洲豹和青蛙。同时知道雨林位于赤道附近。
evidence: Names at least 4 rainforest animals from different layers
Describes the rainforest as having layers (canopy, understory, forest floor)
Explains that rainforests are near the equator and are hot and wet
Recognises that rainforests have more species than almost any other habitat
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a documentary about rainforests, can they describe at least three animals that live there and explain that different animals live at different heights in the forest — some in the treetops and some on the ground?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 稀树草原与草原动物
topics.description: 探索草原和稀树草原上的动物——非洲稀树草原上的狮子、斑马、角马、大象、猎豹；美洲草原上的野牛和草原犬鼠——了解为什么开阔的草原上会形成大群动物，以及捕食者和猎物在这些广阔空间里如何互动。
evidence: Names at least 5 grassland/savanna animals
Explains that herding provides safety in numbers against predators
Describes the predator-prey relationship (e.g., lions hunt zebras)
Knows grasslands/savannas are wide-open habitats with few trees
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees pictures of the African savanna, can they name at least four animals that live there and explain why some animals like zebras live in large herds?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 微小生物的世界
topics.description: 知道昆虫和其他微小生物（蜘蛛、蚯蚓、蜗牛、蜈蚣）是地球上数量最多、种类最丰富的动物群体——甲虫的种类比其他任何动物都多——并且它们在传粉（蜜蜂、蝴蝶）、分解（潮虫、蚯蚓）和作为其他动物的食物方面发挥着重要作用。
evidence: Knows that insects/minibeasts are the most numerous animal group
Names at least 3 roles minibeasts play: pollinators, decomposers, food source
Distinguishes insects (6 legs) from spiders (8 legs) from other minibeasts
Shows appreciation for the importance of invertebrates
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} spots a bee in the garden, can they explain why bees are important — and name at least two other jobs that insects and minibeasts do that help the natural world?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 动物的智慧
topics.description: 探索动物的智慧和复杂行为——黑猩猩和乌鸦会使用工具，海豚能在镜子里认出自己，章鱼能解开谜题并逃出围栏，大象会哀悼死去的同伴，猫鼬会教幼崽对付蝎子——了解许多动物会思考、学习，并且拥有比人们过去认为的更复杂的社交生活。
evidence: Gives at least 4 examples of animal intelligence or complex behaviour
Explains what 'tool use' means and names at least 2 tool-using animals
Discusses how scientists test animal intelligence (mirror test, puzzle boxes, observation)
Shows understanding that intelligence takes different forms in different species
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a video of a crow using a stick to get food from a tube, can they explain that this shows animal intelligence and give other examples of animals that use tools, solve problems, or show complex behaviour?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 生物多样性
topics.description: 理解生物多样性——生态系统中不同物种的多样性——对健康的生态系统至关重要，并且关键物种（如黄石公园的狼、海带林中的海獭或作为传粉者的蜜蜂）对其生态系统有着巨大的影响，因此失去一个关键物种可能引发连锁变化，影响许多其他物种。
evidence: Defines biodiversity as the variety of species in an ecosystem
Explains why biodiversity matters (stability, resilience, ecosystem services)
Defines keystone species and gives at least 2 examples
Describes a trophic cascade or chain reaction from removing/adding a species
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learns about how wolves were brought back to Yellowstone and the whole ecosystem changed, can they explain what a 'keystone species' is and why having many different species in an area matters?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 濒危与灭绝物种
topics.description: 了解为什么有些动物物种会濒危或灭绝——栖息地破坏、狩猎/偷猎、污染、气候变化和入侵物种——并认识大熊猫、山地大猩猩、远东豹等例子，以及已经灭绝的渡渡鸟和袋狼，同时知道世界自然保护联盟红色名录是科学家用来追踪受威胁物种的系统。
evidence: Defines endangered as a species at risk of extinction
Names at least 3 causes of species becoming endangered
Gives at least 3 examples of endangered or extinct animals
Knows the IUCN Red List exists as a tracking system
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a news story about an endangered animal, can they explain what 'endangered' means and describe at least three reasons why some animals are at risk of disappearing forever?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 入侵物种
topics.description: 理解入侵物种是指被引入到它们原本不属于的地方的动物（或植物）——比如英国的灰松鼠排挤红松鼠、澳大利亚的甘蔗蟾蜍毒害本地捕食者、或者兔子破坏澳大利亚的生态系统——它们会通过争夺食物、传播疾病或因为没有天敌而对本地野生动物造成严重伤害。
evidence: Defines invasive species as non-native animals introduced to a new environment
Names at least 2 examples of invasive species and their impacts
Explains at least 2 reasons invasive species are harmful (no predators, outcompete natives, spread disease)
Understands the difference between a species naturally expanding its range and being introduced by humans
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learns that grey squirrels were brought to the UK from America, can they explain why introduced animals can be a problem for the animals that were already living there?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 保护濒危动物
topics.description: 了解人们如何努力保护濒危动物——通过国家公园和海洋保护区、圈养繁殖计划（如拯救加州神鹫和阿拉伯剑羚的计划）、反偷猎巡逻、连接栖息地的野生动物走廊，以及禁止濒危物种贸易的法律——并理解孩子们可以通过对栖息地友好的选择做出贡献。
evidence: Describes at least 3 conservation strategies with specific examples
Names an animal saved from near-extinction by conservation efforts
Suggests at least one action children or families can take to help wildlife
Understands that conservation requires both protecting habitats and helping individual species
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visits a zoo with a breeding programme, can they explain how zoos help save endangered species and describe at least two other ways people protect wildlife?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 结构适应性
topics.description: 理解动物具有结构适应性（身体特征，如长颈鹿的长脖子、鹰的利爪、海豚的流线型身体）、行为适应性（迁徙、冬眠、使用工具）和生理适应性（北极鱼血液中的抗冻物质、蝙蝠的回声定位）——并且这些适应性是通过自然选择经过许多代发展而来的
evidence: Defines adaptation as a feature or behaviour that helps an animal survive in its environment
Gives examples of structural, behavioural, and physiological adaptations
Explains that adaptations develop over many generations, not during one animal's lifetime
Connects adaptations to the concept of natural selection at a basic level
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a woodpecker pecking a tree, can they explain that its strong beak, long tongue, and shock-absorbing skull are all adaptations — and describe what the word 'adaptation' means with other examples?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 共生关系
topics.description: 理解共生关系——不同物种之间的紧密联系——包括互利共生（双方都受益，比如小丑鱼和海葵）、偏利共生（一方受益而不伤害另一方，比如䲟鱼搭乘鲨鱼）和寄生（一方受益而另一方受损，比如鹿身上的蜱虫）——并能在自然界中识别这些关系。
evidence: Defines symbiosis as a close relationship between different species
Distinguishes mutualism, commensalism, and parasitism with an example of each
Identifies symbiotic relationships when presented with new scenarios
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a nature programme showing a small bird picking insects off a buffalo's back, can they explain that both animals benefit from this relationship and name the type of symbiosis?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 红皇后假说
topics.description: 介绍红皇后假说——物种必须不断进化，才能在与共同进化的伙伴的竞争中保持适应度；描述捕食者与猎物之间的军备竞赛（猎豹的速度与瞪羚的速度、蝙蝠的回声定位与飞蛾的听觉干扰）以及寄生虫与宿主的共同进化（兔子的黏液瘤病）；解释达尔文的鹰蛾与兰花作为互利共生共同进化的经典例子，并预测了一个未知物种；理解共同进化是生物多样性的主要驱动力。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the idea of an evolutionary arms race — how a predator and its prey keep evolving better attack and defence strategies in response to each other, never quite getting ahead?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 深海生存
topics.description: 解释深海动物如何应对巨大的压力（没有充气空间、柔性蛋白质、适应压力的酶）；描述体温调节的极端情况——南极鱼类的抗冻糖蛋白、木蛙的过冷现象；介绍缓步动物和隐生现象（在干燥、极端温度、辐射、真空中存活）；调查其他极端微生物（热液喷口处的嗜热菌、盐滩中的嗜盐菌）；思考这些生物告诉我们生命的极限是什么。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe an animal that can survive being frozen solid, completely dried out, or exposed to the vacuum of space — and explain roughly how it manages to survive conditions that would kill almost any other living thing?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 性选择
topics.description: 解释性选择作为自然选择的一种形式：孔雀尾巴的失控选择、极乐鸟的炫耀、青蛙的叫声；解释亲缘选择和利他行为——为什么工蜂会为保护蜂巢而死，为什么猫鼬会冒着个人风险站岗（汉密尔顿法则、广义适合度）；使用鹰鸽模型介绍动物行为中的博弈论；定义认知动物行为学，并综述动物情感、玩耍和文化的证据。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a worker bee dying to protect the hive actually makes evolutionary sense — even though the bee never has its own offspring? What's the logic that makes this a successful strategy?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 生物多样性危机
topics.description: 量化当前的生物多样性危机：物种灭绝速率是背景灭绝速率的100到1000倍；解释衡量生物多样性丧失的方法（物种-面积关系、种群生存力分析、世界自然保护联盟红色名录等级）；评估野化案例研究——黄石公园狼群重新引入引发营养级联，改变了河道；伊比利亚猞猁恢复；描述最小可存活种群理论和保护分类；探讨决定优先保护哪些物种时的伦理争论。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what happened to Yellowstone National Park after wolves were reintroduced — what unexpected changes rippled through the whole ecosystem, including effects on rivers, as a result of one predator coming back?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 使用DNA对物种进行分类
topics.description: 解释分支系统学：生物根据共享的衍生特征分组，而不仅仅是相似性；如何利用分子数据（DNA序列比对）和分子钟构建系统发育树；解释为什么鸟类在技术上属于恐龙类群（冠部鸟跖类）；区分趋同进化（不相关的物种进化出相似特征）和平行进化；介绍水平基因转移以及为什么生命之树更准确地说是生命之网；解释为什么随着新数据的出现分类系统不断变化。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why biologists now say that birds ARE a type of dinosaur — not just their descendants but literally within the dinosaur family tree? What does that tell us about how scientists classify animals?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 恐龙的体型
topics.description: 把恐龙的体型和孩子们熟悉的东西比一比——有些恐龙像房子一样高，有些像小鸡一样小——了解恐龙的体型有大有小，差别很大。
evidence: Compare the size of a large dinosaur to a familiar object like a bus or house
Name a very large dinosaur (e.g. Brachiosaurus) and a small one (e.g. Compsognathus)
Use words like 'taller than', 'longer than', 'heavier than' when comparing
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you that some dinosaurs were enormous and others were tiny — maybe using comparisons like 'as tall as a building' or 'as small as a cat'?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 恐龙真的存在过
topics.description: 理解恐龙是真实存在过的动物，很久很久以前生活在地球上，现在已经灭绝了——今天没有一只活着。
evidence: State that dinosaurs were real animals, not made up
Explain that 'extinct' means no living ones are left anywhere
Distinguish between 'a long time ago' and recent events like last year
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a dinosaur toy, can they tell you that real dinosaurs lived long ago but aren't alive any more?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 著名恐龙种类
topics.description: 认识并说出常见的著名恐龙种类：霸王龙、三角龙、剑龙和腕龙/梁龙，并描述每种恐龙的一个基本特征。
evidence: Name at least four common dinosaur species from pictures or models
Describe one visible feature of each (e.g. T. rex has tiny arms, Triceratops has three horns)
Match a dinosaur name to a picture or model without help
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees pictures of different dinosaurs, can they name at least three — like T. rex, Triceratops, and Stegosaurus?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 化石与古生物学家
topics.description: 理解化石是保存在岩石中的古代生物遗骸，而被称为古生物学家的科学家通过研究化石来了解恐龙。
evidence: Describe a fossil as the remains of a living thing preserved in rock
Name the job of a palaeontologist as someone who studies fossils
Identify examples of fossils: bones, teeth, footprints in rock
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} found a fossil-shaped rock on a beach or at a museum, could they explain what a fossil is and who studies them?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 植食恐龙与肉食恐龙
topics.description: 通过观察牙齿形状等线索，将恐龙分为植食恐龙（吃植物的恐龙）和肉食恐龙（吃肉的恐龙）——平坦的牙齿用来吃植物，尖利的牙齿用来吃肉。
evidence: Sort a set of dinosaur pictures or models into herbivore and carnivore groups
Explain that sharp pointed teeth are for tearing meat and flat teeth are for grinding plants
Give an example of one herbivore and one carnivore dinosaur
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you showed {{name}} a picture of a dinosaur's teeth, could they guess whether it ate plants or meat?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 真正的恐龙与虚构恐龙
topics.description: 区分真正的恐龙和虚构或容易混淆的生物——翼龙（会飞的爬行动物）和蛇颈龙（海洋爬行动物）不是恐龙，电影里的恐龙也不总是准确的。
evidence: State that pterosaurs could fly but were not dinosaurs
State that plesiosaurs lived in the sea but were not dinosaurs
Identify at least one way a movie or cartoon dinosaur differs from the real animal
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a flying reptile in a dinosaur book, can they tell you it's actually not a dinosaur but a different kind of prehistoric animal?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 世界各地的恐龙
topics.description: 了解不同的恐龙生活在不同的大陆上，世界各地的化石发现表明恐龙曾遍布全球，有些物种只出现在特定地区。
evidence: State that dinosaur fossils have been found on every continent including Antarctica
Name at least one dinosaur discovery location (e.g. T. rex in North America, Velociraptor in Mongolia)
Suggest a reason why the same type of dinosaur is sometimes found on continents now far apart
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you showed {{name}} a world map, could they tell you that dinosaur fossils have been found on every continent — and maybe name a place where a famous dinosaur was discovered?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 恐龙粪便化石
topics.description: 解释什么是粪化石（恐龙粪便形成的化石），以及古生物学家如何通过分析粪化石来了解恐龙吃什么，包括植物碎片、骨头和种子。
evidence: Define a coprolite as fossilised dung (animal droppings preserved as rock)
Explain that scientists cut coprolites open to find plant seeds, bone fragments, or fish scales inside
State one example of what coprolite contents reveal about a dinosaur's diet
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know what a coprolite is? Can they explain — with a giggle — how fossilised poo helps scientists figure out what a dinosaur ate?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 化石揭示古代环境
topics.description: 理解化石不仅告诉我们古代动物的信息，还能告诉我们古代环境的信息——例如，在山顶上发现的海洋化石表明该地区曾经在水下。
evidence: Give an example of a fossil that reveals a past environment different from today's
Explain that finding marine fossils inland means that area was once covered by sea
State that plant fossils can show whether an area was once a forest, desert, or swamp
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that seashell fossils were found on a mountain, could they explain what that tells us about what the area used to be like?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 化石是怎么形成的
topics.description: 用简单的话解释化石是怎么形成的：生物死后很快被泥沙埋起来；经过几百万年，矿物质替换了生物遗体，泥沙变成岩石，把形状保留下来。
evidence: Describe the basic sequence: organism dies, buried in sediment, minerals replace remains over time
Explain why fossilisation is rare — most organisms decompose before being buried
Use the words 'sediment', 'minerals', and 'rock' correctly when explaining
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} made a salt-dough fossil at school, could they explain how real fossils form underground over millions of years?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 玛丽·安宁，化石猎人
topics.description: 了解玛丽·安宁是谁——一位来自英国莱姆里吉斯的先驱化石猎人，她在19世纪初发现了鱼龙和蛇颈龙的骨架，为我们理解史前生命做出了贡献。
evidence: State that Mary Anning lived in England in the early 1800s and hunted for fossils along the coast
Name at least one of her major discoveries (ichthyosaur or plesiosaur)
Explain why her work was important — she helped scientists understand that extinct creatures once lived on Earth
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} heard of Mary Anning? Can they tell you who she was and why she was important to the study of fossils?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 解读恐龙足迹
topics.description: 利用恐龙足迹（脚印化石）来推断恐龙的大小、速度和行为——脚印间距大表示奔跑，间距小表示行走。
evidence: Explain that larger footprints generally mean a larger dinosaur
Compare spacing between prints to infer walking versus running
Suggest what a set of parallel trackways might mean (e.g. dinosaurs travelling in a group)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a line of dinosaur footprints at a museum, could they figure out whether the dinosaur was walking or running based on how far apart the prints are?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 中生代
topics.description: 按顺序排列中生代的三个时期——三叠纪、侏罗纪和白垩纪，并理解不同的恐龙生活在不同的时期，而不是同时存在
evidence: List Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous in the correct chronological order
Assign at least one well-known dinosaur to the correct period
Explain that millions of years separated these periods and different species lived in each
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that T. rex and Stegosaurus didn't actually live at the same time — and can they name the three dinosaur time periods in order?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 化石的类型
topics.description: 区分遗体化石（保存下来的骨骼、牙齿、贝壳）和遗迹化石（脚印、行迹、蛋、洞穴、粪化石），并解释每种类型能告诉科学家什么信息。
evidence: Sort examples into body fossils (bones, teeth, shells) and trace fossils (footprints, eggs, dung)
Explain that body fossils show what an animal looked like physically
Explain that trace fossils show how an animal behaved — how it moved, what it ate, where it nested
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a dinosaur footprint in rock at a museum, could they explain how it's different from a fossil bone and what scientists can learn from it?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 化石作为证据
topics.description: 分析和解读化石中的数据，为很久以前存在的生物和环境提供证据
evidence: Explain that fossils are preserved remains or traces of organisms that lived long ago
Use fossil evidence to make inferences about past organisms and their environments
Describe how comparing fossils with living organisms helps us understand how life has changed
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a fossil of a fish in a rock on a hillside, can they explain that the area must have been underwater millions of years ago?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 鸟类从恐龙进化而来
topics.description: 理解现代鸟类是从一群小型带羽毛的兽脚类恐龙进化而来的，使用化石始祖鸟、来自中国的带羽毛恐龙化石以及共有的骨骼特征等证据
evidence: State that birds evolved from small theropod dinosaurs
Name Archaeopteryx or Chinese feathered dinosaurs as key fossil evidence
List at least two features birds share with theropods (e.g. hollow bones, wishbone, three-toed feet)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why scientists say birds are actually living dinosaurs — and point to evidence like feathered dinosaur fossils?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 科学知识的变化
topics.description: 通过权衡化石证据来评估关于恐龙的不同科学解释——理解科学知识会随着新化石的发现和新分析方法的开发而改变。
evidence: Give an example of a scientific idea about dinosaurs that changed when new evidence was found
Explain that different scientists may interpret the same fossil evidence differently
State that the best scientific explanation is the one supported by the most evidence from multiple sources
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read two different explanations for why dinosaurs went extinct, could they discuss what evidence supports each idea and why scientists sometimes change their minds?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 恐龙髋部类群
topics.description: 根据髋部结构将恐龙分为两大类：蜥臀目（蜥蜴髋，包括兽脚类和蜥脚类）和鸟臀目（鸟类髋，包括三角龙和剑龙）
evidence: Name the two major dinosaur groups: Saurischia and Ornithischia
Explain the difference is based on hip bone structure (lizard-hipped vs bird-hipped)
Correctly classify at least two dinosaurs into each group (e.g. T. rex = Saurischia, Triceratops = Ornithischia)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that scientists divide dinosaurs into two big groups based on their hip bones — and tell you which group includes T. rex?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 古生物学家如何工作
topics.description: 描述古生物学家如何在野外和实验室工作：寻找暴露的化石、使用手工工具小心挖掘、用石膏包裹以便运输、在实验室进行修理、以及科学描述和发表
evidence: List the main stages: prospecting, excavation, jacketing, transport, preparation, study, display
Explain why careful excavation with small tools is necessary to avoid damaging the fossil
