Compare an ant colony or bee hive to a human team, describing how different members do different tasks
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watched a nature programme about ants or bees, could they tell you about the different jobs inside the colony — like the queen, the workers, and the guards?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 分类与识别小生物
topics.description: 使用分类检索表来识别小生物。分支式是/否问题：'它有腿吗？' → '有几条腿？' → '它有翅膀吗？' 二歧检索表是分类和识别生物的系统工具。
evidence: Follow a simple branching key to correctly identify at least four different minibeasts
Create a yes/no question that separates insects from spiders, such as 'Does it have six legs?'
Explain why asking questions in a set order helps identify a creature you have never seen before
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} found an unfamiliar minibeast, could they use a set of yes/no questions — like 'Does it have legs? How many?' — to work out what group it belongs to?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 昆虫的身体结构
topics.description: 昆虫的身体结构：所有昆虫都有三个身体部分（头部、胸部、腹部），六条腿长在胸部，头上有一对触角。大多数昆虫有翅膀。它们有外骨骼——一层坚硬的外壳——而不是身体里面有骨头。
evidence: Label the three body parts of an insect — head, thorax, and abdomen — on a diagram or real specimen
State that all insects have exactly six legs and that the legs attach to the thorax
Explain that insects have an exoskeleton, a hard outer covering, instead of bones inside their body
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a picture of a beetle or ant, could they point out the head, thorax, and abdomen, and tell you that all insects have six legs and a hard outer shell?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 昆虫的适应
topics.description: 昆虫的适应与进化：以桦尺蛾作为自然选择的著名例子（工业革命期间，在布满煤烟的树上，深色蛾子存活得更好）。竹节虫进化出像树枝一样的外形。拟蚁蜘蛛进化出欺骗捕食者的本领。许多代的小变化如何导致惊人的伪装。
evidence: Retell the peppered moth story and explain how the environment changed which colour moth survived best
Describe how a stick insect's body shape is an adaptation that helps it avoid being eaten
Explain that adaptations develop over many generations through natural selection, not during one insect's lifetime
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why peppered moths changed colour during the Industrial Revolution — and how that's an example of how living things adapt over many generations?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 昆虫解剖深入探索
topics.description: 深入探索昆虫解剖：由数千个小眼组成的复眼、气门（身体两侧的呼吸孔）、多样的口器（甲虫的咀嚼式上颚、蝴蝶的吸管式喙、苍蝇的海绵状舐吸式口器），以及通过蜕去外骨骼来生长。仿生学——工程师如何模仿昆虫的设计。
evidence: Describe at least two specialised insect structures such as compound eyes or spiracles and explain their function
Compare the mouthparts of a beetle (chewing) and a butterfly (sucking) and explain how each is suited to its food
Give one example of biomimicry where human technology is inspired by an insect structure or ability
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a close-up photo of an insect's eye or mouth, could they explain how those body parts work and why they look so different from ours?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 昆虫的交流与行为
topics.description: 昆虫的交流与行为：蜜蜂通过跳摇摆舞告诉蜂巢同伴花朵在哪里。蚂蚁留下信息素踪迹让其他蚂蚁跟随。萤火虫闪烁光图案来寻找配偶。蟋蟀通过摩擦翅膀发出鸣叫声。帝王蝶跨越大陆迁徙数千英里。昆虫如何不用语言‘交谈’。
evidence: Describe at least three ways insects communicate such as the bee waggle dance, ant pheromone trails, and firefly light signals
Explain what information a bee conveys through its waggle dance, including direction and distance to flowers
Describe the monarch butterfly migration and explain why it is remarkable in terms of distance and navigation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how bees tell each other where to find flowers, how ants leave invisible trails, or how fireflies use light to send messages?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 昆虫在生态系统中的作用
topics.description: 昆虫在生态系统中的多种角色：传粉者（蜜蜂、蝴蝶、食蚜蝇）、分解者（蜣螂、蝇蛆）、鸟类、蝙蝠、鱼类和青蛙的食物来源，以及害虫控制者（瓢虫吃蚜虫）。思考实验：如果所有昆虫都消失了会怎样？
evidence: Name at least three different ecological roles that insects play such as pollinator, decomposer, and food source
Explain how the removal of one insect group like bees would affect plants, other animals, and humans
Describe a specific example of insects as pest controllers such as ladybirds controlling aphid populations
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you asked {{name}} what would happen if all the insects in the world disappeared tomorrow, could they explain the chain of problems that would cause — for plants, animals, and people?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 地球上最成功的动物
topics.description: 地球上最成功的动物：目前大约有一百万种已被描述的昆虫，科学家估计可能还存在500万到1000万种。昆虫的种类比所有其他动物类群加起来还要多。为什么这么多？体型小意味着需要的食物少，繁殖快、后代多，飞行能力让它们能到达新的栖息地，而外骨骼的适应性极其多样。
evidence: State that insects are the most species-rich group of animals with about one million known species
Give at least two reasons why insects are so successful such as small size, fast reproduction, or flight
Compare insect diversity to another animal group, explaining that there are far more insect species than mammals or birds
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know which group of animals has more species than any other on Earth — and can they explain why insects are so incredibly successful?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 昆虫面临的威胁与保护
topics.description: 昆虫面临的威胁与保护：全球昆虫数量正在减少。原因包括栖息地丧失、农药使用、光污染干扰夜行昆虫以及气候变化。传粉昆虫减少威胁粮食生产。孩子们可以做什么：种植对传粉昆虫友好的花园、减少农药使用、参与公民科学项目如“大蝴蝶计数”。
evidence: Name at least three threats to insect populations such as habitat loss, pesticides, and light pollution
Explain why declining bee populations are a problem for humans and the food we eat
Suggest at least two actions that children or families can take to help insects such as planting wildflowers or joining a butterfly count
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you why insect numbers are falling around the world, why that matters for people too, and what your family could do to help?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 变态发育的类型
topics.description: 完全变态和不完全变态。完全变态：卵→幼虫→蛹→成虫（蝴蝶、甲虫、苍蝇）。不完全变态：卵→若虫→成虫——若虫看起来像成虫的小版本，随着生长会蜕皮（蚱蜢、蜻蜓、蟋蟀）。为什么有些昆虫完全变形，而另一些则逐渐长大？
evidence: Compare complete and incomplete metamorphosis by describing the stages of each on a diagram
Classify at least three insects into the correct metamorphosis type such as butterfly (complete) and grasshopper (incomplete)
Explain that nymphs resemble adults while larvae look completely different from their adult form
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between a butterfly's life cycle and a grasshopper's — why the caterpillar looks nothing like the butterfly, but a baby grasshopper already looks like a small grasshopper?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 描述材料的特性
topics.description: 描述日常材料的简单物理特性，如硬/软、有弹性/僵硬、有光泽/暗淡、粗糙/光滑、防水/吸水、透明/不透明
evidence: Use at least five property words correctly: hard, soft, stretchy, shiny, rough, smooth, transparent, waterproof
Describe the properties of three different materials using at least two property words each
Explain why a property matters (e.g. 'waterproof means water doesn't soak through')
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} pick up different objects and describe their properties — like 'this is smooth and shiny' or 'this is rough and bendy'?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 材料分类
topics.description: 根据简单的物理特性比较和分类日常材料
evidence: Sort a set of materials into groups based on a chosen property (e.g. transparent vs opaque)
Compare two materials and state which properties they share and which differ
Explain the reasoning behind a grouping decision using property vocabulary
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} sort a pile of objects into groups based on their properties, like all the waterproof ones together or all the transparent ones?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 常见材料命名
topics.description: 识别并说出各种日常材料的名称，包括木头、塑料、玻璃、金属、水和岩石
evidence: Name at least six everyday materials: wood, plastic, glass, metal, water, rock
Identify the material of at least ten different objects around the home or classroom
Recognise that some objects are made from more than one material
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} look around a room and correctly name the materials things are made of — like glass in the window, metal in the radiator, and plastic in a pen?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 物体与材料
topics.description: 区分物体和构成它的材料，理解同一物体可以由不同材料制成。
evidence: Explain the difference between an object (e.g. a chair) and the material it is made from (e.g. wood)
Give examples of the same object made from different materials (e.g. plastic cup, glass cup)
Identify what material a given object is made from by looking at and touching it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you hold up a wooden spoon and a metal spoon, can {{name}} explain that both are spoons (the object) but made from different materials?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 物质状态词汇
topics.description: 用性质词汇（硬、有固定形状、流动、会流淌、保持自己的形状、填满容器）说出并区分物质的三种状态——固体、液体和气体；用“状态变化”来描述材料被加热或冷却时发生的变化。
evidence: Correctly sort a set of everyday materials as solid, liquid, or gas and give a reason for each
Use the terms solid, liquid, and gas accurately when describing everyday substances
Use 'change of state' to describe what happens when ice melts or water boils
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you point to water, ice, and steam from a kettle, can {{name}} correctly call each one a liquid, solid, or gas — and use those words naturally?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 改变固体的形状
topics.description: 探究如何通过挤压、弯曲、扭曲和拉伸来改变固体物体的形状
evidence: Demonstrate four ways to change the shape of a solid: squashing, bending, twisting, stretching
Compare how different materials respond to these forces (e.g. clay squashes easily, wood does not)
Explain that the material itself stays the same even when the shape changes
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} show you how to change the shape of clay by squashing it, twist a pipe cleaner, and explain that some materials bend while others snap?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 选择合适的材料
topics.description: 识别并比较日常材料在特定用途中的适用性，解释为什么特定用途要选择特定材料。
evidence: Explain why a specific material is chosen for a purpose based on its properties (e.g. glass for windows because it's transparent)
Compare two materials and decide which is more suitable for a given use with reasoning
Suggest an alternative material for an object and explain why it would or wouldn't work
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why windows are made of glass and not wood, or why wellies are made of rubber and not paper?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 变化与分离词汇
topics.description: 使用过程词汇来描述状态变化和材料分离——溶解、溶液、可溶、不可溶、蒸发、凝结、融化、凝固、过滤、筛分、混合物、分离——并准确理解每个术语所描述的内容，包括溶解和融化之间的重要区别。
evidence: Distinguish 'dissolve' from 'melt' correctly in context and explain the difference
Use 'soluble' and 'insoluble' accurately when describing whether a material dissolves in water
Explain the difference between evaporation and condensation using the correct terms
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} stirs sugar into tea, can they explain whether the sugar dissolved or melted — and tell you those are different things?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 材料分类
topics.description: 计划并进行一项调查，根据可观察的特性对不同的材料进行分类。
evidence: Design a simple test to compare one property across several materials
Record observations in a table or chart during the investigation
Classify the tested materials into groups based on the results
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} test a set of objects and sort them by properties like whether they float, conduct heat, or are magnetic?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 绘制粒子示意图
topics.description: 绘制并解读粒子示意图——用点表示固体（排列紧密、规则、在原地振动）、液体（排列紧密、无规则、相互流动）和气体（间隔很大、向各个方向快速运动）中粒子的排列、间距和运动方式，并用这些示意图解释可观察到的性质，如固定形状、固定体积和可压缩性。
evidence: Draw labelled particle diagrams for solids, liquids, and gases showing the correct arrangement and spacing of particles
Use their particle diagram to explain why solids keep their shape but liquids flow
Sketch what happens to particles during a change of state (e.g. melting) and explain the energy changes involved
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s science teacher draws a diagram with dots packed tightly in rows versus dots spread far apart and moving around, can {{name}} tell you which represents a solid and which a gas — and explain why, using the particles?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 加热与冷却的变化
topics.description: 观察并描述一些材料在加热或冷却时会改变状态，并用摄氏度测量发生这些变化时的温度。
evidence: Describe melting (solid to liquid) and freezing (liquid to solid) with everyday examples
State that water freezes at 0°C and boils at 100°C
Explain that heating adds energy causing particles to move more, leading to state changes
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happens to an ice cube when you heat it, and at what temperature water freezes and boils?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 拆开与重建
topics.description: 观察由少量零件组成的物体可以被拆开并重新组合成新物体，理解零件仍然存在。
evidence: Explain that taking apart an object and rebuilding it uses the same pieces in a new arrangement
Describe how the pieces themselves don't change even though the object looks different
Give an everyday example of reusing materials to make something new
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} builds a tower with building bricks and then takes it apart to build a car, can they explain that the same bricks are used but arranged differently?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 测试材料用途
topics.description: 基于比较和公平测试的证据，说明日常材料（包括金属、木材和塑料）特定用途的原因
evidence: Design a fair test to compare a specific property of two or more materials
Present test results as evidence for why a material is suited to a particular use
Explain the link between a material's tested properties and its real-world application
topics.assessmentPrompt: After testing different materials, can {{name}} explain with evidence why saucepans are made of metal but their handles are plastic?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 蒸发与水循环
topics.description: 识别蒸发和凝结在水循环中的作用，并将蒸发速度与温度联系起来。
evidence: Describe evaporation as liquid turning to gas and condensation as gas turning to liquid
Explain the water cycle: evaporation from seas/lakes → condensation into clouds → precipitation
Explain why evaporation happens faster at higher temperatures (e.g. puddles dry faster on hot days)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why puddles disappear on a sunny day and where the water goes, and why the bathroom mirror steams up after a hot shower?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 固体、液体和气体
topics.description: 根据可观察的性质和行为，将材料比较并分类为固体、液体或气体
evidence: Define solids (fixed shape, hard to compress), liquids (flow, take shape of container), gases (spread out, fill space)
Sort at least eight everyday materials into solid, liquid, or gas categories
Explain tricky cases like sand (solid particles) or steam (gas, not visible water droplets)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between a solid like ice, a liquid like water, and a gas like steam, and sort everyday things into these three groups?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 进阶材料特性
topics.description: 根据进阶特性比较和分组日常材料：硬度、溶解性、透明度、导电性、导热性和对磁铁的反应
evidence: Define and test for at least four properties: hardness, solubility, conductivity, magnetism
Group a set of materials based on test results for each property
Use results to explain why certain materials are chosen for specific uses (e.g. copper for wires because it conducts electricity)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} test materials and sort them by whether they dissolve in water, conduct electricity, or are attracted to a magnet?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 溶解与溶液
topics.description: 理解有些材料能溶解在液体中形成溶液，并描述如何通过蒸发从溶液中回收物质。
evidence: Explain that dissolving means a solid mixes completely into a liquid to form a solution
Describe how to recover a dissolved substance by evaporating the liquid
Distinguish between a mixture (can see separate parts) and a solution (looks clear, fully dissolved)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happens when sugar dissolves in tea, and figure out how to get the salt back from salty water?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 不可逆变化
topics.description: 解释有些变化会产生新物质，而且通常无法恢复原状，例如燃烧、生锈以及与酸反应。
evidence: Define an irreversible change as one that creates new materials that cannot be changed back
Give at least three examples: burning, rusting, mixing bicarbonate of soda with vinegar
Describe observable signs of irreversible change: gas produced, colour change, heat given off, new substance formed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why you can't un-burn a piece of toast or turn rust back into shiny iron, because a completely new material has been made?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 材料特性词汇
topics.description: 使用专业词汇来描述和比较材料的特性——导体、绝缘体、导热、导电、透明、不透明、半透明、可溶、不可溶、磁性、柔性、刚性、密度——并在选择和论证特定用途的材料时准确应用这些术语。
evidence: Classify a set of materials as electrical conductors or insulators and explain why using the correct terms
Use 'transparent', 'translucent', and 'opaque' correctly and distinctly in descriptions
Apply at least four property terms correctly when justifying a material choice for a given purpose
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} had to choose a material to make a window, could they use words like 'transparent' and 'insulator' to explain their choice — not just say 'you can see through it'?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 可逆变化
topics.description: 证明溶解、混合和状态变化是可逆变化，不会产生新物质。
evidence: Define a reversible change as one where the original materials can be recovered
Give at least three examples of reversible changes: melting, freezing, dissolving, evaporating
Explain how to reverse each example (e.g. freeze melted chocolate, evaporate a solution)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that melting chocolate or dissolving sugar can be undone — you can get the original material back — because these are reversible changes?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 分离混合物
topics.description: 运用关于固体、液体和气体的知识，判断如何通过过滤、筛分和蒸发来分离混合物
evidence: Choose the correct separation method for a given mixture (sieving for large particles, filtering for small, evaporating for dissolved)
Describe a multi-step separation plan for a complex mixture like sand, salt, and water
Explain why each method works based on the properties of the materials
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has a mixture of sand, salt, and water, can they figure out a step-by-step plan to separate all three using a sieve, filter, and evaporation?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 质量守恒
topics.description: 测量并提供证据，证明无论发生哪种变化（加热、冷却或混合），物质的总重量保持不变。
evidence: State the principle that matter is neither created nor destroyed during physical or chemical changes
Describe an investigation weighing materials before and after a change to show mass is conserved
Explain why dissolved sugar still contributes to the total weight even though it can't be seen
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} dissolves sugar in water, can they explain why the total weight of the water and sugar stays the same even though the sugar seems to disappear?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 物质由粒子构成
topics.description: 建立一个模型来描述物质是由肉眼看不见的微小粒子构成的，并用这个模型解释固体、液体和气体的性质。
evidence: Describe matter as made of particles too small to see with the naked eye
Use a particle model to explain differences: particles tightly packed (solid), loosely arranged (liquid), spread far apart (gas)
Use the particle model to explain a state change (e.g. heating makes particles move faster and spread apart)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that everything is made of tiny particles we can't see, and that how tightly packed they are determines whether something is a solid, liquid, or gas?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 原子、元素和化合物
topics.description: 解释原子、元素和化合物之间的区别；描述简单的原子玻尔模型（带质子和中子的原子核，电子在电子层中）；书写和解读化学符号及简单化学式。
evidence: Defines atom, element, and compound and distinguishes between them with examples
Draws a simple Bohr model of an atom labelling nucleus (protons/neutrons) and electron shells
Reads a chemical formula to identify the elements and number of each atom (e.g. H₂O, CO₂, NaCl)
Identifies the difference between a mixture and a compound
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw the formula H₂O on a label, could they explain what it means — which atoms are involved, how many of each, and why water is a compound rather than just a mixture of hydrogen and oxygen?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 物质如何改变状态
topics.description: 用粒子模型解释熔化、凝固、沸腾、冷凝和升华，解读加热和冷却曲线以识别熔点和沸点
evidence: Describes what happens to particles during each change of state
Reads a heating/cooling curve and identifies the melting point and boiling point from the flat regions
Explains why temperature stays constant during a change of state
Distinguishes between evaporation (from surface, any temperature) and boiling (throughout liquid, at boiling point)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was heating a block of ice in a pan and drew a graph of temperature over time, could they explain why the line goes flat at certain points — and what's happening to the particles when it does?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 金属与非金属
topics.description: 比较金属和非金属的物理和化学性质，解释金属特性（延展性、光泽、导电性），以及元素在周期表中的位置如何预测其反应性。
evidence: Lists physical properties typical of metals (shiny, malleable, good conductor) and non-metals
Explains why metals are used in wires, cookware, and construction based on their properties
Uses the periodic table to predict whether an element is likely to be reactive or unreactive
Explains what lustre and malleability mean in terms of real-world observations
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} had an unknown substance that was shiny, could be bent without breaking, and conducted electricity, could they identify it as likely a metal and explain how each property points to that conclusion?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 物理变化与化学变化
topics.description: 区分物理变化（可逆，不产生新物质）和化学变化（产生新物质，通常不可逆），并利用质量守恒定律来理解这两种变化。
evidence: Classifies given changes as physical or chemical with justification
Explains what conservation of mass means and why mass is conserved in chemical reactions
Names observable signs that a chemical reaction has occurred (colour change, gas produced, temperature change, precipitate)
Explains why dissolving is a physical change but burning is a chemical change
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} dissolved sugar in tea versus burnt toast in the toaster, could they explain which is a physical change and which is a chemical change — and what test would show that mass is conserved in both cases?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 纯净物与混合物
topics.description: 区分纯净物和混合物，认识配方是成分精确的有用混合物，并利用熔点和沸点来检验纯度
evidence: Explains why a pure substance has a sharp, fixed melting point but a mixture melts over a range
Identifies common formulations (medicines, alloys, paints, fuels) as deliberate mixtures
Explains what impurities do to melting and boiling points
Distinguishes mixtures from compounds at the particle level
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was checking whether a sample of water was pure, could they explain one test they could do — and say what result would tell them it was definitely pure versus a mixture?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 分离混合物
topics.description: 针对不同类型的混合物，选择并实施合适的分离技术：过滤（不溶性固体）、蒸馏（根据沸点分离液体）、结晶（溶解的固体）和色谱法（有色物质）
evidence: Selects the correct separation technique for a given mixture with justification
Describes the steps of simple distillation and explains why it works
Interprets a chromatography result (Rf values, number of components)
Explains why filtration removes sand from water but not salt
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} needed to separate salt from sand mixed together in water, could they describe two stages of separation, the equipment needed, and explain why each step works?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 粒子模型
topics.description: 用粒子模型解释固体、液体和气体的性质——包括粒子排列、运动和间隔的差异——并运用该模型解释密度、可压缩性和水的反常膨胀。
evidence: Draws particle diagrams for solids, liquids, and gases showing correct arrangement and spacing
Explains why gases are compressible but liquids and solids are not
Explains why ice floats on water using the anomalous expansion of water
Uses particle spacing to explain why gases are much less dense than solids and liquids
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why you can squash a balloon but not a water bottle full of liquid, could they explain using the idea of particles what's different about gases and liquids?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 元素周期表
topics.description: 描述元素周期表如何按周期和族进行组织，解释门捷列夫的贡献，并使用周期表识别金属、非金属，并预测反应性的规律。
evidence: Explains why the periodic table is arranged into periods (rows) and groups (columns)
States that elements in the same group have similar chemical properties
Locates metals, non-metals, and metalloids in the periodic table
Explains how Mendeleev ordered elements by atomic weight and predicted missing elements
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was looking at a periodic table, could they explain why elements in the same column tend to behave similarly — and say what Mendeleev did that made it so useful to chemists?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 酸的反应与盐
topics.description: 描述并写出酸与金属、碱（中和反应）以及金属氧化物/氢氧化物反应的文字方程式，并指出每种情况下生成的盐
evidence: Writes word equations for: acid + metal → salt + hydrogen; acid + alkali → salt + water; acid + metal oxide → salt + water
Names the salt formed from a given acid and base (e.g. hydrochloric acid + sodium hydroxide → sodium chloride)
Describes the test for hydrogen gas (squeaky pop)
Explains what neutralisation means and gives a practical example (indigestion tablets, treating acidic soil)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked how an indigestion tablet works to relieve stomach acid, could they explain what type of chemical reaction is happening and write a simple word equation for it?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 酸、碱与pH值
topics.description: 从氢离子浓度的角度定义酸和碱，描述pH标度（0–14），并解释如何使用指示剂来识别和测量酸碱性
evidence: States that acids have pH below 7, alkalis have pH above 7, and neutral is pH 7
Explains what hydrogen ions (H⁺) have to do with acidity
Names common indicators (litmus, universal indicator) and describes colour changes
Identifies everyday acids (vinegar, lemon juice) and alkalis (bleach, bicarbonate of soda)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} used a piece of universal indicator paper to test lemon juice and baking soda solution, could they predict what colour each would turn and explain what that tells you about each substance?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 地球大气与二氧化碳
topics.description: 描述地球大气的组成（主要是氮气和氧气，以及少量的二氧化碳和其他气体），解释人类活动如何增加二氧化碳，并描述对全球气候的影响。
evidence: States the approximate percentages of nitrogen, oxygen, CO₂, and argon in the atmosphere
Explains how burning fossil fuels and deforestation increase atmospheric CO₂
Describes the greenhouse effect and how it leads to climate change
Discusses one specific consequence of climate change (e.g. rising sea levels, extreme weather)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why scientists are worried about CO₂ levels rising, could they explain what CO₂ does in the atmosphere, why human activities produce more of it, and what effects it's having on the planet?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 有限资源与回收利用
topics.description: 解释许多原材料（金属、化石燃料、矿物）是有限资源，描述开采的环境代价，并评估回收利用和循环经济的好处。
evidence: Identifies examples of finite natural resources and explains why they are finite
Describes the environmental impact of mining and fossil fuel extraction
Explains why recycling metals saves energy compared to extraction from ores
Discusses trade-offs between the cost of recycling and the benefit of resource conservation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was deciding whether to recycle an aluminium drinks can or throw it away, could they explain what goes into making new aluminium from scratch — and why recycling it uses much less energy?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 放热反应与吸热反应
topics.description: 区分放热反应（释放能量，温度升高）和吸热反应（吸收能量，温度降低），并了解日常生活和工业中的例子
evidence: Defines exothermic and endothermic in terms of energy transfer to and from the surroundings
Gives two examples of each type from everyday life (e.g. combustion, hand warmers; photosynthesis, cold packs)
Explains energy changes during changes of state (melting is endothermic, freezing is exothermic)
Interprets a temperature change in an experiment to classify the reaction type
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} shook a sports cold pack to activate it and it got cold, or lit a match and it got hot, could they explain what type of reaction is happening in each case and why one gets hot while the other gets cold?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 金属活动性顺序
topics.description: 按金属活动性顺序排列常见金属，并解释较活泼的金属如何置换较不活泼的金属；描述工业上如何用碳从金属氧化物中提取金属。
evidence: Recalls the order of common metals in the reactivity series (potassium to gold)
Predicts whether a displacement reaction will occur given two metals
Explains why carbon can be used to extract iron from iron oxide but not aluminium from aluminium oxide
Links the reactivity series to the history of metal use (gold found free, iron smelted, aluminium electrolytic)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why humans used gold and copper before iron and aluminium, could they explain how a metal's reactivity determines how easy it is to extract — and why carbon can extract some metals but not others?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 岩石循环
topics.description: 解释岩石循环：岩浆如何形成火成岩，沉积物如何被压缩形成沉积岩，热量和压力如何形成变质岩，以及所有岩石类型在地质时间中如何相互转化。
evidence: Describes how each rock type (igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic) is formed
Gives an example of each rock type and its formation (e.g. granite, limestone, marble)
Traces a rock sample through possible transitions in the rock cycle
Explains what geological time means and why rock cycle changes are slow
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} picked up a piece of marble on a school trip, could they explain how it was originally limestone, what changed it into marble, and how long that process took?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 化学反应的类型
topics.description: 识别并描述四种化学反应类型：燃烧（在氧气中燃烧）、氧化（获得氧）、热分解（通过加热分解）和置换（较活泼的金属置换较不活泼的金属）
evidence: Writes a word equation for each type of reaction with an example
Identifies the type of reaction from a given word equation or description
Explains what makes a displacement reaction happen (relative reactivity)
Distinguishes complete combustion (CO₂ and H₂O) from incomplete combustion (CO and soot)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw iron going rusty and a candle burning, could they explain what type of chemical reaction is happening in each case — and write a simple word equation for one of them?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 陶瓷、聚合物与复合材料
topics.description: 描述陶瓷（坚硬、易碎、耐热）、聚合物（柔韧、轻便、性能多样）和复合材料（结合组成材料的特性）的性质与用途，并给出每种材料的实际例子
evidence: Gives the key properties of ceramics, polymers, and composites with examples of each
Explains why a composite material is used rather than a single material in a given application (e.g. carbon-fibre reinforced plastic in bikes)
Identifies natural and synthetic polymers
Explains why polymer properties can be tailored during manufacturing
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was looking at a racing bicycle made of carbon fibre, could they explain why neither carbon nor plastic alone would work as well — and what makes the combination a composite better than either material on its own?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 海岸与海滩
topics.description: 知道什么是海岸或海滩——陆地与海洋相遇的地方——并且知道不同的海岸可以是沙质的、岩石的或泥泞的，每种海岸都有不同的植物和动物。
evidence: Define a coast as where land meets the ocean
Describe at least two types of coast: sandy, rocky, or muddy
Name an animal likely found at each type of coast
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visited a sandy beach and then a rocky shore, could they describe how the two coasts look different and name animals you might find at each one?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 海洋动物的多样性
topics.description: 认识到海洋是各种各样动物的家园——从微小的海马、色彩斑斓的小丑鱼到巨大的鲸鱼和鲨鱼——海洋动物有各种形状和大小
evidence: Name at least five different ocean animals
Describe differences in size between small and large ocean creatures
Express curiosity or wonder about the variety of life in the ocean
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visited an aquarium or watched an ocean documentary, could they name at least five different ocean animals and describe how different they are from each other?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 海洋食物链
topics.description: 描述一个简单的海洋食物链：微小的植物（浮游植物）被小动物吃掉，小动物被大鱼吃掉，大鱼被鲨鱼等顶级捕食者吃掉——说明所有海洋生物都依赖其他生物获取食物。
evidence: Describe a food chain with at least three levels
Identify that ocean food chains start with tiny plants or algae
Explain that bigger animals eat smaller ones in a chain of dependence
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw or describe a chain showing how tiny ocean plants are eaten by small creatures, then by bigger fish, then by a shark — explaining that each animal depends on the one before it?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 岩石池栖息地
topics.description: 探索岩石池（潮池）作为小型海洋栖息地，这里可以发现螃蟹、海葵、海星和小鱼，并了解这些生物如何适应生存于拍打的波浪和变化的水位中。
evidence: Name at least three creatures found in rock pools
Describe a rock pool as a small ocean habitat on the shore
Explain one way rock pool animals cope with waves or changing water levels
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} explored a rock pool at the beach, could they point out the creatures living there and explain how they hold on tight or hide in cracks when waves come?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 鲸鱼和海豚是哺乳动物
topics.description: 知道鲸鱼和海豚是哺乳动物，不是鱼——它们呼吸空气、是温血动物、用乳汁喂养宝宝——尽管它们生活在海洋里
evidence: State that whales and dolphins are mammals, not fish
Give at least two reasons why: they breathe air and feed babies milk
Explain that living in water does not make an animal a fish
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a dolphin jumping out of the water, could they explain that dolphins are mammals like us — they breathe air and feed their babies milk — not fish?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 什么是海洋？
topics.description: 知道海洋是覆盖地球大部分表面的巨大咸水体，海洋是无数生物的家园
evidence: State that oceans cover more of Earth than land does
Explain that ocean water is salty, unlike the fresh water in rivers and lakes
Describe the ocean as home to a huge variety of living things
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you asked {{name}} to point to the oceans on a globe, could they show you and explain that most of our planet is covered by salty water where millions of creatures live?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 海洋动物需要什么
topics.description: 了解海洋动物需要食物、住所和合适的生存条件才能活下去——就像陆地动物一样——并且海洋的不同区域能满足不同动物的需求
evidence: List basic needs of ocean animals: food, shelter, suitable water conditions
Give an example of how a specific ocean animal meets its needs
Compare an ocean animal's needs to a familiar land animal's needs
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that a clownfish needs a sea anemone for shelter and small creatures to eat, just like a bird needs a tree for a nest and seeds to eat?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 海洋动物分类
topics.description: 将海洋动物分为主要类别：鱼类（用鳃呼吸，有鳞片）、海洋哺乳动物（呼吸空气，恒温，哺乳）、无脊椎动物（没有脊椎——水母、章鱼、螃蟹、海星）
evidence: Sort ocean animals into fish, marine mammals, and invertebrates
Give defining features of each group (gills vs lungs, backbone vs none)
Correctly classify at least two animals in each group
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw pictures of a tuna, a seal, and a jellyfish, could they sort them into fish, marine mammals, and invertebrates, and explain what makes each group different?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 珊瑚礁
topics.description: 知道珊瑚礁是由叫做珊瑚虫的微小活体动物建造的，珊瑚礁是比几乎任何其他海洋栖息地都更多物种的家园，它们有时被称为“海洋中的雨林”。
evidence: State that coral is built by tiny living animals called polyps, not made of rock
Describe coral reefs as one of the most biodiverse habitats in the ocean
Explain why reefs are compared to rainforests
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watched a documentary about coral reefs, could they explain that coral is actually made by tiny living animals, and that reefs are home to an incredible number of different species?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 海洋动物的适应本领
topics.description: 了解海洋动物为了适应环境，拥有特殊的本领：流线型的身体帮助它们快速游泳，伪装色帮助它们躲避天敌，鲸脂帮助它们在寒冷的海水中保暖，触手或吸盘帮助它们捕捉猎物。
evidence: Name at least three different ocean animal adaptations
Explain how each adaptation helps the animal survive in its environment
Connect an adaptation to the specific challenge it addresses (cold, predators, catching food)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} pick an ocean animal and explain at least two ways its body is specially designed for life in the sea — like a seal's blubber for warmth or an octopus's camouflage for hiding?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 海洋深度分层
topics.description: 了解海洋根据深度和光线分为不同的区域：靠近海面的阳光带，大部分生物生活在这里；光线逐渐变暗的暮光带；以及完全黑暗的午夜带。
evidence: Name the three main ocean zones: sunlight, twilight, and midnight
Explain that light decreases with depth until it disappears completely
State that most ocean life is found in the sunlight zone because plants need light to grow
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a diagram showing the ocean getting darker as you go deeper, could they name the three main zones and explain why most ocean animals live near the sunlit surface?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 海洋食物网
topics.description: 理解海洋食物网：多个相互连接的食物链，能量从浮游植物（生产者）流向浮游动物、小鱼和大型捕食者，并且移除一个物种会影响整个食物网。
evidence: Distinguish a food web from a simple food chain
Trace at least two paths of energy through an ocean food web
Explain what could happen if one species in the web were removed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why catching too many of one type of fish doesn't just affect that fish — it affects the whole food web, including the animals that eat it and the things it eats?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 五大洋
topics.description: 在世界地图上说出并找到五大洋——太平洋（最大）、大西洋、印度洋、南冰洋和北冰洋（最小最冷），并理解它们全部相连，构成一个统一的全球海洋。
evidence: Name all five oceans: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic
Locate at least three oceans on a world map
Explain that the five named oceans are all connected as one continuous body of water
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a world map, could they point to each of the five oceans by name and explain that they're all connected into one big global ocean?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 海底地形
topics.description: 知道海底不是平坦的——它有山脉、山谷和地球上最深的海沟——最深处是马里亚纳海沟，比珠穆朗玛峰的高度还要深
evidence: State that the ocean floor has varied terrain including mountains, ridges, and trenches
Name the Mariana Trench as the deepest point on Earth
Compare its depth to a familiar reference like Mount Everest's height
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that the ocean floor has mountains and valleys, could they explain that it's not flat and that the Mariana Trench is the deepest spot on Earth — deeper than Everest is tall?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 潮汐、波浪与洋流
topics.description: 了解海洋有潮汐（水位每天涨落两次，主要由月球的引力引起）、波浪（由风引起）和洋流（在海洋中流动的水流，将温暖和营养物质带到世界各地）
evidence: Describe tides as the regular rise and fall of water level, caused by the Moon's gravity
Explain that waves are caused by wind blowing across the water surface
Describe ocean currents as large flows of water that carry heat and nutrients around the globe
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} noticed the water level changing at the beach during the day, could they explain that tides are caused by the Moon's pull, and that the ocean also has waves from wind and currents that flow like underwater rivers?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 深海生物
topics.description: 探索深海中的生命：能自己发光的动物（生物发光）、适应巨大压力和完全黑暗环境的生物，以及不依赖阳光、生命繁盛的热液喷口
evidence: Define bioluminescence as the ability of some deep-sea creatures to produce their own light
Describe at least two adaptations deep-sea animals have for life in darkness and pressure
Explain that hydrothermal vents support life without sunlight through chemical energy
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw footage of glowing deep-sea creatures, could they explain how some animals make their own light and why life can exist even in the deepest, darkest parts of the ocean?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 探索海洋
topics.description: 了解海洋学家和海洋生物学家利用潜水艇、遥控潜水器（ROV）、卫星和潜水来研究海洋，并且海洋的大部分区域仍未被探索——我们对月球表面的了解甚至比深海海底还要多。
evidence: Name at least two tools scientists use to explore the ocean: submarines, ROVs, satellites
State that most of the deep ocean remains unexplored
Explain why ocean exploration is difficult: darkness, pressure, vastness
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how scientists explore the deep ocean using robots and submarines, and why we've still only explored a small fraction of the ocean floor — less than we know about the Moon?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 海洋动物迁徙
topics.description: 知道许多海洋动物会进行令人惊叹的迁徙——座头鲸在觅食地和繁殖地之间游动数千英里，海龟会回到它们孵化的同一片海滩产卵——并理解这些旅程与季节性的食物供应和繁殖有关。
evidence: Describe at least one example of marine animal migration in detail
Explain that migrations are driven by seasonal food availability and breeding needs
Estimate the scale of these journeys (thousands of miles)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that a humpback whale swims from Antarctica to the tropics every year, could they explain why — that it's following food in summer and heading to warmer waters to have its baby?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 海洋生态系统
topics.description: 理解海洋生态系统是一个相互关联的系统，其中生物（生产者、消费者、分解者）和非生物因素（温度、盐度、光照、洋流）相互作用，并且一个部分的变化会影响整个系统。
evidence: Describe an ocean ecosystem as a system of living and non-living parts that interact
Name key non-living factors that affect ocean life: temperature, salinity, light, currents
Explain how a change in one factor (like temperature) cascades through the whole ecosystem
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why warmer ocean temperatures don't just affect one species — they change the whole ecosystem, from the plankton at the bottom of the food web to the whales at the top?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 海洋污染与危害
topics.description: 识别人类危害海洋的方式——塑料污染、过度捕捞、石油泄漏以及二氧化碳导致的海洋酸化——并理解大多数海洋污染来自陆地活动，而不仅仅是船只
evidence: Name at least three ways humans harm the ocean
Explain that most ocean pollution originates on land, not from ships
Describe how plastic pollution or overfishing specifically harms marine animals
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw plastic washed up on a beach, could they explain where it came from, how it harms sea life, and name other ways humans damage the ocean like overfishing and pollution from factories?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 海洋与气候
topics.description: 了解海洋与气候之间的联系：海洋吸收热量和二氧化碳，通过蒸发驱动天气模式，洋流将温暖输送到全球各地——使海洋成为地球的气候引擎。
evidence: Explain that the ocean absorbs a large amount of the Sun's heat and atmospheric carbon dioxide
Describe the ocean's role in the water cycle through evaporation
Explain how ocean currents distribute warmth and affect weather patterns in distant places
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the ocean is sometimes called Earth's climate engine — that it absorbs heat, drives rain through evaporation, and moves warmth around the world through currents?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 保护海洋
topics.description: 了解人们如何保护海洋：海洋保护区限制捕鱼和污染，可持续捕鱼防止过度捕捞，海滩清洁减少塑料，国际协议旨在减少导致海洋酸化的碳排放。
evidence: Explain what a marine protected area is and why it helps
Describe sustainable fishing as taking only what the ocean can replace
Name at least two actions people can take to protect oceans: reducing plastic, marine reserves, cutting emissions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard about a marine protected area where fishing is banned, could they explain why it helps — and name other ways people are working to protect the ocean from pollution, overfishing, and climate change?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 没有阳光的深海生命
topics.description: 对比光合作用（利用阳光获取能量）和化能合成作用（通过氧化硫化氢等化学物质获取能量）；描述热液喷口生物群落：化能自养细菌构成食物网的基础，支撑着管虫、巨型蛤蜊和喷口蟹等生物，无需阳光；探索深海生命对地球生命起源的启示；解释为什么NASA研究海洋喷口，将其作为木卫二和土卫二上热液活动周围可能存在生命的类比对象。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe a community of animals living at the bottom of the ocean that gets its energy from volcanic chemicals rather than sunlight — and explain why scientists are excited about what this might mean for life on other planets?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 洋流与全球热量
topics.description: 解释温盐环流（全球传送带）是由温度和盐度差异驱动的，这些差异导致密度大的水下沉；描述大西洋经向翻转环流（AMOC）如何将热量从热带输送到欧洲；解释海洋吸收了人类排放的超过90%的多余热量和约25%的二氧化碳；探讨如果环流减弱，北欧气候会发生什么变化。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the UK has mild winters compared to parts of Canada at similar latitudes — what does ocean circulation have to do with it, and what might change if that circulation slows down?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 珊瑚白化与海洋酸化
topics.description: 解释珊瑚虫与光合虫黄藻之间的互利共生关系；描述热应激如何导致白化（珊瑚排出虫黄藻并变白）；解释海洋酸化的化学过程：二氧化碳溶于海水形成碳酸，降低pH值并溶解碳酸钙骨骼；将珊瑚礁消失与约25%海洋物种栖息地崩溃联系起来；评估当前的珊瑚礁恢复工作。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} heard of coral bleaching? Can they explain what's actually happening to the coral — what breaks down between the coral and the tiny algae living inside it, and why warmer or more acidic water triggers this?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 捕食者消失与生态系统影响
topics.description: 量化营养级之间的能量传递效率（约10%规则）；解释营养级联：顶级捕食者的消失如何引发一系列生态系统变化（海獭→海胆暴增→海藻林崩溃）；定义“捕捞食物网下层”；评估海洋再野化的证据——鲨鱼重新引入、鲸鱼恢复驱动营养循环；理解为什么需要基于生态系统的渔业管理
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} trace the chain of events that happened to Pacific kelp forests when sea otters were hunted almost to extinction — what domino effect did removing one species set off through the whole ecosystem?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 深海探索技术
topics.description: 解释载人潜水器（如阿尔文号、深海挑战者号）和遥控潜水器（ROV）如何帮助探索深海；描述使用声纳进行海底声学测绘，以及为什么只有约25%的海底被高分辨率测绘；探讨为什么深海比月球表面更难探索（压力、寒冷、黑暗、通信困难）；调查针对太阳系中海洋世界的天体生物学任务。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why more of the Moon's surface has been mapped in detail than Earth's ocean floor — what makes deep ocean exploration so much harder than looking at the Moon?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 动物身体分组
topics.description: 描述并比较常见动物类群（鱼类、两栖类、爬行类、鸟类、哺乳类）的外部身体结构。
evidence: Describe key structural features of at least three animal groups (e.g. scales, feathers, fur)
Compare two animals from different groups, noting at least two differences
Use words like 'wings', 'fins', 'legs', 'tail' correctly when describing an animal
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how a fish's body is different from a bird's body and explain features like scales, feathers, or fins?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 身体部位与感官
topics.description: 识别、说出并找到人体的基本部位，并将每个身体部位与其对应的感官联系起来。
evidence: Label eyes, ears, nose, mouth, and skin on a body outline
Match each sense organ to its sense: sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch
Describe a simple scenario for each sense (e.g. 'I use my nose to smell cookies baking')
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} point to their eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin and tell you which sense each one is used for?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 常见的植物和树木
topics.description: 识别并说出常见的野生植物和花园植物，包括落叶树和常绿树
evidence: Name at least five common wild or garden plants from direct observation
Sort trees into deciduous (loses leaves) and evergreen (keeps leaves) with examples
Match a plant to its name when shown a picture or real specimen
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you point to a tree in the park, can {{name}} tell you what kind it is and whether it keeps its leaves in winter?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 食草动物、食肉动物和杂食动物
topics.description: 将常见动物分类为食肉动物（吃肉）、食草动物（吃植物）或杂食动物（两者都吃）
evidence: Define carnivore, herbivore, and omnivore in own words
Sort at least six common animals into the three diet groups
Give a reason for each sorting decision based on what the animal eats
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a cat is a carnivore, a rabbit is a herbivore, and a bear is an omnivore?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 生物词汇
topics.description: 说出并运用关于生物特征的词汇——活的、死的、从未活过、运动、营养、生长、繁殖、感应、排泄——并在对物体进行分类时应用这些术语，解释为什么植物和动物属于生物
evidence: Correctly classify objects as living, dead, or never been alive and give a reason using one of the life process terms
Name at least five life processes using the correct vocabulary
Explain why a plant is alive using at least two life process words
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a rock is not alive but a weed is — using a science word like 'nutrition' or 'growth' rather than just saying 'it moves'?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 说出常见动物的名称
topics.description: 识别并说出主要动物类群中的常见动物：鱼类、两栖动物、爬行动物、鸟类和哺乳动物
evidence: Name at least two animals from each group: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals
Sort a set of animal pictures into the five groups
Explain one feature of each group (e.g. 'birds have feathers', 'fish have gills')
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} sees a frog, a robin, or a goldfish, can they tell you which animal group each belongs to?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 植物的组成部分
topics.description: 识别并描述常见开花植物（根、茎、叶、花）和树木（根、树干、树枝、树叶）的基本结构
evidence: Label roots, stem, leaves, and flowers on a diagram of a flowering plant
Name the main parts of a tree: roots, trunk, branches, leaves
Explain that roots take in water and leaves catch sunlight
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you pick a flower from the garden, can {{name}} point to the roots, stem, leaves, and petals and say what each part does?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 生物需要什么
topics.description: 了解植物和动物（包括人类）生存所需的条件：水、食物、空气和适宜的环境
evidence: List the basic needs of animals: water, food, air, shelter
List the basic needs of plants: water, light, air, suitable temperature
Explain what happens if one basic need is missing (e.g. 'the plant wilts without water')
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} what a pet dog or a garden plant needs to stay alive, can they list the basic things like water, food, and air?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 动物的生命阶段
topics.description: 认识到动物（包括人类）都有后代，后代会长成成年个体，并描述动物基本的生命阶段
evidence: Describe the basic life stages of a human: baby, child, teenager, adult
Give examples of other animals and their young (e.g. kitten → cat, chick → hen)
Explain that offspring grow and change as they develop into adults
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how a kitten grows into a cat, or how a baby grows into an adult?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 后代与父母相似
topics.description: 观察幼小的植物和动物与它们的父母相似但并不完全相同，认识遗传的相似性和个体差异。
evidence: Describe at least three features that offspring inherit from parents (e.g. eye colour, petal colour, fur type)
Explain that offspring are similar to parents but not identical copies
Give examples from both plants and animals showing resemblance with variation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} look at a family photo and point out features children share with their parents, while also noticing how each child looks a bit different?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 种子与植物生长
topics.description: 观察并描述种子和鳞茎如何通过发芽和生长阶段长成成熟的植物
evidence: Describe the stages: seed absorbs water → root appears → shoot pushes up → leaves open
Compare how a bulb and a seed start growing differently
Record observations of a growing plant over several days using drawings or a simple diary
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} planted a seed or bulb and been able to describe what happened as it grew — first a root, then a shoot, then leaves?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 植物生长需要什么
topics.description: 了解植物需要水、光和适宜的温度才能生长并保持健康
evidence: Name three things plants need to grow: water, light, suitable temperature
Predict what happens to a plant kept in the dark, with no water, or in freezing cold
Describe the results of a simple test comparing plants grown in different conditions
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a plant on the windowsill grows better than one left in a dark cupboard?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 动物分类词汇
topics.description: 使用动物分类和生命周期描述的词汇——脊椎动物、无脊椎动物、哺乳动物、鸟类、爬行动物、两栖动物、鱼类、昆虫、蛛形纲动物、幼虫、蛹、变态、妊娠、后代、完全变态、不完全变态——并在分类和比较生物时正确应用这些词汇。
evidence: Correctly classify a set of animals as vertebrates or invertebrates, then into more specific groups
Use 'metamorphosis' correctly to describe insect and amphibian life cycles and distinguish complete from incomplete metamorphosis
Compare a mammal's life cycle with an insect's using precise vocabulary
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know the difference between a vertebrate and an invertebrate — and could they sort a list of animals into the right group?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 动物的营养
topics.description: 了解动物（包括人类）需要正确种类和数量的营养，并且动物不能自己制造食物。
evidence: Name the main food groups: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre, water
Explain that animals get energy from food they eat, unlike plants which make their own
Describe what happens with too much or too little of a food group (e.g. weak bones without calcium)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why people need to eat different types of food like fruit, protein, and carbohydrates to stay healthy?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 绘制生命周期图
topics.description: 为开花植物、昆虫（完全变态和不完全变态）、鸟类和哺乳动物绘制并解读生命周期图——标注阶段、描述过渡过程，并比较不同物种的生命周期
evidence: Draw a labelled life cycle diagram for a flowering plant including seed, seedling, mature plant, and flower/fruit
Compare a butterfly life cycle (complete metamorphosis) with a grasshopper life cycle (incomplete metamorphosis) using diagrams
Label a blank life cycle diagram for a given organism correctly, including transitions between stages
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is given a blank circular diagram, can they fill in the stages of a butterfly's life cycle in the right order with labels — and explain what changes at each stage?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 植物各部分的作用
topics.description: 识别并描述开花植物不同部分的功能：根吸收水分和养分，茎运输物质，叶制造食物，花帮助植物繁殖。
evidence: Describe the function of roots (absorb water and minerals from soil)
Explain that the stem transports water up and food around the plant
State that leaves use sunlight to make food and flowers produce seeds for new plants
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a flower needs roots underground and leaves up top — what job does each part do?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 生物的生命周期
topics.description: 建立模型来描述生物具有独特而多样的生命周期，但都共同经历出生、生长、繁殖和死亡这些阶段
evidence: Describe the life cycle of at least two different organisms (e.g. butterfly, frog, plant)
Identify the common stages all life cycles share: birth, growth, reproduction, death
Explain how life cycles can look very different (metamorphosis vs gradual growth) but follow the same pattern
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} compare the life cycle of a butterfly with that of a frog and explain what stages they all share — being born, growing, having babies, and dying?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 传粉与种子传播
topics.description: 了解开花植物的生命周期，包括传粉、种子形成和种子传播
evidence: Describe the stages: pollination → fertilisation → seed formation → seed dispersal
Explain at least two methods of seed dispersal (wind, animal, water, explosion)
Describe pollination as the transfer of pollen from one flower to another, often by insects or wind
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a flower turns into a fruit with seeds inside, and how those seeds get spread to grow new plants?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 骨骼与肌肉
topics.description: 了解人类和一些其他动物有骨骼和肌肉，用于支撑、保护和运动
evidence: Name the three functions of the skeleton: support, protection, movement
Identify that muscles are attached to bones and pull to create movement
Give examples of bones protecting organs (skull protects brain, ribs protect heart and lungs)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why we have a skeleton inside our body and what our muscles do when we bend an arm?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 植物中的水分运输
topics.description: 探究水分在植物体内是如何运输的，通过观察有色水被茎吸收上升等现象进行了解
evidence: Describe an investigation using coloured water to track water movement in a plant
Explain that water travels from roots through the stem to the leaves and flowers
Draw or label a diagram showing the path of water through a plant
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} seen a white flower turn a different colour in coloured water and been able to explain that the stem carries water up to the petals?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 植物茁壮成长需要什么
topics.description: 探索并比较植物生存和生长所需的条件：空气、光照、水分、土壤中的养分和生长空间
evidence: List five requirements for plant growth: air, light, water, nutrients, space
Explain how needs vary between plants (e.g. cacti need less water than ferns)
Predict what happens when one requirement is removed or limited
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you why a crowded pot of seedlings doesn't grow as well as one with just a few plants?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 动物如何适应环境
topics.description: 了解动物和植物如何适应它们所处的环境，并理解适应可能会随着时间的推移导致进化
evidence: Define adaptation as a feature that helps an organism survive in its environment
Give at least three examples of adaptations in different organisms and explain how each helps survival
Explain that over many generations, organisms with helpful adaptations survive and reproduce more, leading to evolution
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a camel's humps, a cactus's thick skin, or a polar bear's white fur help them survive where they live, and how these adaptations developed over time?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 遗传词汇
topics.description: 使用关于变异和遗传的词汇——遗传特征、获得性特征、变异、后代、性状、物种、品种、遗传的、环境——并在比较生物体、解释物种内部和物种之间的相似性和差异时应用这些词汇
evidence: Distinguish between inherited and acquired characteristics with a correct example of each
Use 'variation' correctly to describe differences within a species and explain what causes variation
Use 'offspring', 'species', and 'trait' correctly in written descriptions of living things
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why children look similar to but not exactly like their parents — using words like 'inherited' or 'variation'?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 遗传特征
topics.description: 通过分析和解读数据，提供证据说明植物和动物具有从父母遗传的特征，并且这些特征在相似生物群体中存在差异。
evidence: Define inherited traits as characteristics passed from parents to offspring
Collect or interpret data showing variation within a group (e.g. different heights, colours, sizes)
Explain that while traits are inherited, there is natural variation among individuals of the same species
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} measures the height of all the sunflowers in the garden, can they see that they're all sunflowers but each one is a slightly different height?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 消化系统
topics.description: 描述人体消化系统基本部位（口腔、食道、胃、小肠、大肠）的简单功能。
evidence: Name the main organs in order: mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine
Describe the function of each (mouth chews, stomach breaks down, small intestine absorbs nutrients)
Draw or label a simple diagram of the digestive system
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} trace the journey of a sandwich through the body — from chewing in the mouth all the way to the intestines?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 特征：遗传与环境
topics.description: 用证据支持这样的解释：特征既受遗传影响，也受环境影响。
evidence: Explain that traits result from both inheritance and environmental factors
Give examples of environmental influence on traits (e.g. sunlight affects plant growth, diet affects animal size)
Distinguish between inherited traits (e.g. eye colour) and environmentally influenced traits (e.g. muscle strength from exercise)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why two identical seeds might grow into different-sized plants if one gets more sunlight than the other?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 牙齿的种类
topics.description: 认识人类牙齿的不同种类（门牙、犬齿、臼齿），并说出它们在吃东西时的作用。
evidence: Name three types of teeth: incisors, canines, molars
Describe the function of each: incisors cut, canines tear, molars grind
Relate tooth type to diet (e.g. herbivores have flat molars, carnivores have sharp canines)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} point to different teeth in their mouth and explain that front teeth cut food while back teeth grind it?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 变异与生存优势
topics.description: 用证据解释同一物种个体间的特征差异如何为生存、寻找配偶和繁殖提供优势
evidence: Explain that variation within a species means some individuals have traits better suited to their environment
Give examples of advantageous variations (e.g. camouflage, speed, drought resistance in plants)
Connect variation to survival advantage: individuals with beneficial traits are more likely to survive and reproduce
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a faster rabbit in a group might survive longer because it can escape predators better than slower ones?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 人类生命阶段
topics.description: 描述人类从发育到衰老的变化，包括人类生命周期的主要阶段。
evidence: Name the main stages of human development: baby, toddler, child, teenager, adult, elderly
Describe key changes at puberty (growth spurt, body changes)
Explain that old age brings changes like reduced strength, greying hair, and slower healing
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the main stages of a human life — from baby to toddler to child to teenager to adult to old age — and some changes at each stage?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 器官系统词汇
topics.description: 使用专业词汇来描述主要器官系统——器官、器官系统、循环系统、消化系统、呼吸系统、骨骼系统、肌肉系统、营养素、氧气、二氧化碳、血管、动脉、静脉、毛细血管、酶——并运用这些术语描述每个系统的功能。
evidence: Name the main organs in at least two body systems and state their functions using the correct vocabulary
Use 'circulatory', 'digestive', and 'respiratory' correctly in written descriptions of the body
Explain the difference between an artery and a vein using the correct anatomical terms
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the circulatory system does — not just 'the heart pumps blood', but using words like 'oxygen', 'artery', and 'blood vessel'?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 感官、大脑与反应
topics.description: 用模型描述动物通过感官接收信息，在大脑中处理信息，并以不同方式做出反应
evidence: Describe the pathway: sense organ detects stimulus → brain processes information → body responds
Give examples of different animal senses (sight, smell, hearing, echolocation, vibration)
Explain how the same stimulus can produce different responses in different animals
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a dog uses its senses to detect a squirrel and then decides to chase it?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 生存结构
topics.description: 能够论证植物和动物具有内部和外部结构，这些结构的功能支持生存、生长、行为和繁殖。
evidence: Give examples of external structures and their survival functions (e.g. thorns for protection, claws for catching prey)
Give examples of internal structures and their functions (e.g. heart pumps blood, lungs take in air)
Construct a reasoned argument linking a specific structure to how it helps the organism survive or reproduce
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a cactus's thick stem helps it survive in a desert, or how a bird's wings help it find food?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 饮食、运动与生活方式
topics.description: 认识饮食、运动、药物和生活方式对人体机能的影响
evidence: Describe how a balanced diet provides energy and nutrients the body needs
Explain the positive effects of regular exercise on the heart, muscles, and mental health
Describe harmful effects of drugs, alcohol, or tobacco on the body
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why eating well and exercising regularly helps the body stay healthy, and why drugs and smoking are harmful?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 食物与太阳的能量
topics.description: 用模型描述动物食物中的能量最初来自太阳，通过植物或其他生物传递。
evidence: Explain that plants capture energy from sunlight to make food (photosynthesis)
Trace an energy pathway: sun → plant → animal → another animal
Explain that animals use food energy for body repair, growth, movement, and warmth
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} trace the energy in their breakfast cereal all the way back to the sun, explaining each step?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 进化词汇
topics.description: 使用进化与自然选择的专业词汇——适应、进化、自然选择、灭绝、灭绝、化石记录、物种、共同祖先、突变、变异——并按正确顺序用这些术语解释自然选择的机制。
evidence: Use 'adaptation' correctly to describe a feature that helps an organism survive in its environment
Explain natural selection using 'variation', 'selection pressure', and 'reproduction' correctly in sequence
Use 'extinct' and 'extinction' correctly and distinguish them from 'endangered'
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in their own words why giraffes have long necks — using words like 'adaptation' or 'natural selection' rather than just 'so they can reach leaves'?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 动物体内的营养运输
topics.description: 描述营养物质和水如何在动物体内运输，包括循环系统在将消化后的营养物质输送至全身过程中的作用。
evidence: Describe how nutrients from digested food pass through the wall of the small intestine into the blood
Explain that blood transports dissolved nutrients and water to all parts of the body
Connect the digestive system and circulatory system as working together to deliver nourishment
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the sandwich they ate at lunch actually gets to their muscles — from the stomach into the blood and then around the body?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 植物从空气和水中生长
topics.description: 支持一个论点：植物生长所需的物质主要来自空气和水，而不是土壤
evidence: Explain that plants take in carbon dioxide from air and water from soil to make food (photosynthesis)
Argue that most of a plant's mass comes from air (CO₂) and water, not soil minerals
Describe a simple investigation showing soil mass barely changes while a plant grows significantly
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} knows plants need water and sunlight, can they also explain that most of a plant's 'building material' actually comes from air and water rather than dirt?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 循环系统
topics.description: 识别并说出人体循环系统的主要部分，描述心脏、血管和血液的功能。
evidence: Name the main components: heart, arteries, veins, capillaries, blood
Describe the heart as a pump that pushes blood around the body in a continuous loop
Explain that blood carries oxygen and nutrients to cells and removes waste products like carbon dioxide
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the heart does, why we have blood vessels throughout the body, and what blood actually carries?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 计算膳食能量
topics.description: 计算和评估健康日常饮食中的能量摄入和需求，解读食品标签和营养数据
evidence: Reads and interprets a nutritional information label (kJ and kcal)
Estimates daily energy requirements for a person of a given age/activity level
Compares the energy content of different diets and identifies surpluses or deficits
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was reading food labels at the supermarket with you, could they work out roughly whether a meal gives too much, too little, or about the right amount of energy for a day?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 从细胞到器官系统
topics.description: 描述多细胞生物的分层组织：细胞 → 组织 → 器官 → 器官系统 → 生物体
evidence: Places cells, tissues, organs, and organ systems in the correct order of organisation
Gives a specific example of each level (e.g. muscle cell → muscle tissue → heart → circulatory system → human)
Explains why specialised cells are needed in a multicellular organism
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked to explain how the body is built up from the smallest parts to the whole, could they describe the levels from individual cells all the way up to organ systems — with a real example at each level?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 显微镜下的细胞
topics.description: 理解所有生物体都是由细胞组成的，并使用光学显微镜观察、解释和记录细胞结构。
evidence: States that all living things are made of cells
Prepares or examines a slide of cells (e.g. onion skin, cheek cells) under a microscope
Draws and labels a diagram of cells observed
Identifies nucleus, cytoplasm, and cell membrane in a microscope image
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} prepared a slide of onion skin and looked at it through a school microscope, could they identify what they were seeing and explain that all living things are made of these tiny units?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 饮食失衡与营养缺乏
topics.description: 解释饮食不均衡对健康的影响，包括肥胖（能量过剩）、饥饿（严重能量不足）和营养缺乏病（缺乏特定营养素，如坏血病、佝偻病）。
evidence: Defines obesity, starvation, and deficiency disease and links each to dietary imbalance
Identifies at least two specific deficiency diseases and the missing nutrient causing each
Explains why the impact of poor diet can be long-term
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard about conditions like obesity or vitamin deficiency diseases, could they explain how eating too much, too little, or the wrong mix of foods leads to those health problems?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 消化与酶
topics.description: 描述人体消化系统的器官，以及食物如何通过物理和化学方式被消化，包括酶作为生物催化剂的作用。
evidence: Traces the journey of food from mouth to large intestine, naming each organ and its role
Explains what enzymes do and names where they are produced (salivary glands, stomach, small intestine)
Distinguishes physical digestion (chewing, churning) from chemical digestion
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} ate a meal with you, could they describe what happens to the food step by step as it travels through the body — naming the organs it passes through and what each one does?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 关节、肌腱和韧带
topics.description: 解释生物力学——骨骼和肌肉在关节处的相互作用，包括肌腱（将肌肉连接到骨骼）和韧带（将骨骼连接到骨骼）的作用
evidence: Distinguishes between tendons and ligaments and gives the function of each
Describes how a synovial joint works (e.g. the knee or elbow)
Explains how force is transmitted from muscle through tendon to bone to produce movement
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hurt their knee playing sport, could they explain what a ligament and a tendon are, where each is found, and what would happen if one got damaged?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 肌肉成对工作
topics.description: 解释肌肉以拮抗对的形式工作——一块收缩时另一块放松——从而产生运动，以肱二头肌和肱三头肌作为关键例子
evidence: Explains why muscles can only pull, not push
Describes what happens to the bicep and tricep when the arm is bent and straightened
Gives another example of an antagonistic muscle pair
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} bent and straightened their arm, could they explain why two different muscles are needed — one to bend and one to straighten — and which muscle is which?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 健康饮食中的营养素
topics.description: 认识健康饮食的七大组成部分——碳水化合物、脂质、蛋白质、维生素、矿物质、膳食纤维和水，并解释它们在人体中的作用
evidence: Names all seven dietary components and a food source for each
Explains what each nutrient does in the body (e.g. proteins for growth and repair)
Identifies which nutrients provide energy and which do not
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was planning a packed lunch, could they explain what each food group does for the body — why we need protein, carbohydrates, fats, vitamins, and minerals?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 植物细胞和动物细胞的组成部分
topics.description: 描述植物细胞和动物细胞主要组成部分的功能：细胞壁、细胞膜、细胞质、细胞核、液泡、线粒体、核糖体和叶绿体
evidence: Names the main organelles in plant and animal cells
Explains the function of each organelle in their own words
Links organelle function to the needs of the whole cell (e.g. mitochondria produce energy for cell activities)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was shown a diagram of a plant cell, could they point to parts like the nucleus, chloroplasts, and cell wall and explain in plain words what each one does?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 光合作用
topics.description: 解释光合作用是植物利用光能将二氧化碳和水转化为葡萄糖和氧气的过程，并描述矿物质营养如何通过根吸收。
evidence: Writes and explains the word equation for photosynthesis
Identifies the raw materials needed and the products made
Explains the role of chlorophyll in capturing light energy
Distinguishes between what plants get from the air (CO₂), soil (water and minerals), and light
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why plants don't need to eat food like animals do, could they explain how plants make their own food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide — and write the equation?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 植物细胞与动物细胞
topics.description: 比较植物细胞和动物细胞，识别它们共有的特征以及植物细胞特有的结构（细胞壁、液泡、叶绿体）。
evidence: Lists features common to plant and animal cells
Identifies structures found only in plant cells and explains why
Draws and annotates labelled diagrams of both cell types showing similarities and differences
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was shown unlabelled diagrams of a plant cell and an animal cell side by side, could they spot which features are shared and which ones only appear in plant cells — and say why?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 单细胞生物
topics.description: 解释细菌和变形虫等单细胞生物如何在一个细胞内完成所有生命活动
evidence: Names examples of unicellular organisms
Lists the seven life processes (MRS NERG) and explains how a single cell performs each one
Contrasts how unicellular organisms meet their needs compared to multicellular organisms
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learned that bacteria are made of just one cell, could they explain how that single cell still manages to feed, grow, and reproduce — doing everything a whole body does?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 人体骨骼
topics.description: 描述人体骨骼的结构和四大主要功能：支撑、保护、运动以及骨髓中血细胞的生成
evidence: Lists and explains the four functions of the skeleton with examples
Names key bones and identifies which organs they protect (e.g. ribcage protects heart and lungs)
Explains what bone marrow is and where blood cells are made
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why we have bones, could they explain that bones do more than just hold us up — describing at least three different things the skeleton does for the body?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 使用显微镜
topics.description: 正确使用光学显微镜来准备、对焦和观察生物标本，包括在适当放大倍数下绘制准确的带标注的细胞图。
evidence: Sets up a light microscope safely and correctly (course focus then fine focus)
Prepares a wet mount slide with a biological specimen (e.g. onion skin)
Calculates the magnification of an image (magnification = image size ÷ actual size)
Draws an accurate labelled diagram of observed cells with a scale
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} had to use a school microscope to study a biological specimen, could they set it up correctly, find what they're looking for, and produce a labelled scientific drawing of what they see?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 有氧呼吸
topics.description: 解释有氧呼吸是生物体利用氧气从葡萄糖中释放能量，并产生二氧化碳和水的过程；写出并解释文字表达式：葡萄糖 + 氧气 → 二氧化碳 + 水
evidence: Writes and explains the word equation for aerobic respiration
Explains where in the cell aerobic respiration takes place (mitochondria)
Links aerobic respiration to why breathing rate and heart rate increase during exercise
Explains that respiration is not the same as breathing
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} had just finished PE and was breathing hard, could they explain what aerobic respiration is doing inside their muscle cells — and write out the word equation that describes it?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 无氧呼吸
topics.description: 解释动物在氧气供应不足时，葡萄糖不完全分解为乳酸的无氧呼吸过程，导致肌肉疲劳；并与有氧呼吸在能量产出和产物方面进行对比。
evidence: Writes the word equation for anaerobic respiration in animals
Explains why lactic acid causes muscle pain and fatigue
Compares the energy released by aerobic and anaerobic respiration
Explains oxygen debt and recovery after vigorous exercise
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sprinted as fast as they could and their legs started to burn and ache afterwards, could they explain what's happening inside their muscles — why there isn't enough oxygen, and what the body produces instead?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 体温调节
topics.description: 解释人体如何感知并应对环境变化（包括温度），以及皮肤在体温调节中的作用（出汗、发抖、血管舒张、血管收缩）。
evidence: Explains what homeostasis means in the context of body temperature
Describes at least two mechanisms the body uses to cool down and two to warm up
Explains why maintaining a constant core body temperature is important for enzyme activity
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} got too hot on a summer day and started sweating, could they explain what the body is doing to cool itself down — and why it's so important to keep body temperature steady?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 气体交换与呼吸
topics.description: 描述人体气体交换系统的结构（气管、支气管、细支气管、肺泡），并解释呼吸的机制——利用肋骨和膈肌运动产生的压力变化，使空气进出肺部。
evidence: Labels a diagram of the lungs showing trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, and alveoli
Explains that breathing in lowers air pressure in the chest and air rushes in
Describes how the structure of alveoli (large surface area, thin walls, good blood supply) aids gas exchange
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} took a deep breath after running, could they explain what's happening in their lungs — how the air gets in, where the oxygen crosses into the blood, and how carbon dioxide leaves?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 肠道细菌与消化
topics.description: 解释肠道微生物群中的细菌在消化过程中的作用，包括分解膳食纤维和维持健康的肠道环境。
evidence: Explains that many gut bacteria are beneficial, not harmful
Describes what gut bacteria do that human digestive enzymes cannot (e.g. break down fibre)
Explains what might happen if the gut microbiome is disrupted
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that there are billions of bacteria living in our gut, could they explain why that's actually helpful for digestion rather than something to worry about?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 心脏结构与双循环
topics.description: 描述心脏的结构（四个腔室、瓣膜、冠状动脉），并解释心脏如何在双循环系统中将缺氧血泵入肺部、将富氧血泵向全身。
evidence: Labels a diagram of the heart showing atria, ventricles, valves, aorta, vena cava, and pulmonary vessels
Traces the route of blood through the double circulatory system
Explains the role of valves in preventing backflow
Compares arteries, veins, and capillaries
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} felt their heartbeat, could they describe what the heart is doing — explaining the two sides of the heart, where the blood goes from each side, and why we need a double loop?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 扩散是如何进行的
topics.description: 解释扩散是粒子从高浓度区域向低浓度区域的净移动，并描述其在细胞内外运输物质（氧气、二氧化碳、葡萄糖）中的作用。
evidence: Defines diffusion using particle theory
Explains the direction of diffusion of oxygen and carbon dioxide at the alveoli
Explains how cells get glucose from the blood using diffusion
Identifies factors that affect the rate of diffusion (concentration gradient, surface area, distance)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why oxygen moves from the lungs into the blood without the body needing to pump it, could they explain what diffusion is and why it always moves in one particular direction?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 人类生殖
topics.description: 描述男性和女性人类生殖系统的结构和功能，并解释受精、妊娠和分娩的过程，包括胎盘的作用。
evidence: Labels diagrams of the male and female reproductive systems
Explains the roles of gametes (sperm and egg) in sexual reproduction
Describes what happens during fertilisation and where it occurs
Explains the function of the placenta and the impact of maternal lifestyle on foetal development
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was studying human reproduction, could they describe how the male and female reproductive systems work together and explain what happens between fertilisation and birth?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 病原体与免疫系统
topics.description: 解释病原体（细菌、病毒和真菌）如何引起疾病，并描述免疫系统如何应对，包括白细胞的作用（吞噬作用、抗体产生）以及免疫的概念。
evidence: Distinguishes between bacteria, viruses, and fungi as pathogens with examples of each
Explains two ways white blood cells destroy pathogens (engulfing and antibodies)
Explains how vaccination works and why it prevents disease
Explains the difference between being infected and being ill
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} got a cold, could they explain what type of pathogen caused it, how the immune system tries to fight it off, and why a vaccine for flu won't protect you from all colds?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 植物的繁殖
topics.description: 描述花的结构，并解释风媒传粉和虫媒传粉、受精、种子和果实的形成以及种子传播的过程
evidence: Labels the main parts of a flower (sepals, petals, stamens, carpel, ovary, ovule)
Compares wind-pollinated and insect-pollinated flowers and explains adaptations of each
Traces the journey from pollination to seed dispersal
Identifies and explains at least two methods of seed dispersal
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watched bees visiting flowers in a garden, could they explain what role the bees are playing and trace the full journey from pollination through to seed dispersal?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 药物与酒精的影响
topics.description: 解释包括酒精、烟草和非法物质在内的娱乐性药物对行为、健康和身体系统的影响，并区分抑制剂、兴奋剂和致幻剂
evidence: Categorises common recreational drugs as depressants, stimulants, or hallucinogens
