Explains specific effects of alcohol and tobacco on the body (e.g. liver damage, lung cancer)
Discusses the difference between physical and psychological dependence
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a news story about drug misuse, could they explain what different types of drugs do to the body and behaviour — and why some are more harmful than others?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 北极与南极
topics.description: 知道北极（北极点）和南极（南极点）非常不同——北极是被陆地包围的冰冻海洋，那里有人和北极熊居住，而南极是被海洋包围的巨大冰盖大陆，那里有企鹅居住，但没有人永久居住。
evidence: State that the Arctic is a frozen ocean surrounded by land, while the Antarctic is a continent covered in ice surrounded by ocean
Explain that polar bears live in the Arctic and penguins live in the Antarctic, not the other way around
Know that people (like the Inuit) live in the Arctic but nobody lives permanently in Antarctica
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the big difference between the two poles — that the Arctic is frozen sea with land around it, while the Antarctic is a frozen continent with sea around it?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 勇敢的极地探险家
topics.description: 了解勇敢的极地探险家的简单故事——罗伯特·法尔肯·斯科特和罗尔德·阿蒙森比赛到达南极点，以及欧内斯特·沙克尔顿的船“坚忍号”被冰压碎，但他把所有船员安全带回——并理解极地探险需要极大的勇气和耐力。
evidence: Name at least two polar explorers: Scott, Amundsen, or Shackleton
Tell the basic story of Scott and Amundsen's race to the South Pole in simple terms
Describe what happened to Shackleton's ship Endurance and how he brought his crew home safely
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you the story of explorers who went to the South Pole — like Scott and Amundsen's race, or Shackleton whose ship got trapped in the ice but who saved all his crew?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 冰和雪
topics.description: 知道水可以是固体（冰和雪）或液体，雪是由微小的冰冻冰晶组成的，冰山是漂浮在海洋中的巨大冰块，大部分隐藏在水下，冰会浮起来是因为它比液态水轻
evidence: Explain that ice and snow are frozen water (solid) and that water can change between solid and liquid
Describe an iceberg as a huge piece of ice floating in the ocean with most of it hidden below the surface
State that ice floats because frozen water is lighter than liquid water
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that icebergs are like floating ice mountains with most of the ice hidden under the water — and that the polar regions are covered in ice because it's so cold the water stays frozen?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 极昼与极夜
topics.description: 知道在极地，白天和黑夜非常极端——夏天太阳一直不落（极昼），冬天太阳一直不升（极夜，持续好几个月）——这和我们家里每天都有白天和黑夜很不一样
evidence: Describe midnight sun: in polar summer, the Sun stays above the horizon all day and night
Describe polar night: in polar winter, the Sun stays below the horizon for weeks or months
Compare this to normal day-night patterns at home, noting the dramatic difference
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know the amazing fact that at the poles, the Sun doesn't set at all in summer and doesn't rise at all in winter — so there can be months of daylight or months of darkness?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 企鹅
topics.description: 了解企鹅的基本知识——它们生活在南极和南半球，不会飞但游泳很棒，帝企鹅是最大的企鹅，冬天会挤在一起取暖，企鹅爸爸妈妈轮流把蛋放在脚上保暖，即使在冰点以下的温度里也是如此。
evidence: State at least three facts about penguins: they can't fly, they're excellent swimmers, and Emperor penguins are the biggest
Describe how Emperor penguins huddle together in winter to keep warm
Explain that penguin parents take turns keeping their egg warm on their feet in freezing temperatures
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you about penguins — that they can't fly but swim brilliantly, that Emperor penguins huddle in huge groups to stay warm, and that the dad balances the egg on his feet for weeks?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 极地动物
topics.description: 了解企鹅和北极熊以外的其他极地动物——在冰下游动的海豹、长着长牙的海象、冬天变白的北极狐、雪鸮、长着像独角兽一样长牙的独角鲸，以及迁徙到极地水域觅食的鲸鱼——并知道这些动物都有在极寒中生存的特殊本领。
evidence: Name at least four polar animals beyond penguins and polar bears, such as seals, walruses, Arctic foxes, snowy owls, or narwhals
Describe one way each named animal survives the cold (e.g. walrus blubber, Arctic fox white winter coat)
State that narwhals have a long spiral tusk and live in Arctic waters
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name several animals that live in the freezing polar regions — like walruses, Arctic foxes, snowy owls, or narwhals — and explain how they cope with the cold?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 北极熊
topics.description: 了解北极熊的关键知识——它们只生活在北极（不是南极），有厚厚的白色皮毛和一层脂肪（鲸脂）来保暖，是出色的游泳健将，它们会在海冰的洞口等待海豹来呼吸，从而捕猎海豹
evidence: State that polar bears live in the Arctic, not the Antarctic
Describe at least two ways polar bears stay warm: thick white fur and a layer of blubber (fat)
Explain how polar bears hunt seals by waiting at breathing holes in the sea ice
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you about polar bears — that they live only in the Arctic, their thick fur and blubber keep them warm, and they hunt seals by waiting patiently at holes in the ice?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 两极在哪里？
topics.description: 知道地球有北极和南极——地球上最冷的地方——并能在世界地图或地球仪上找到它们，理解它们位于地球的最顶端和最底端，离赤道最远。
evidence: Point to the North Pole and South Pole on a globe or world map
Explain that the poles are the coldest places on Earth because they are farthest from the Equator
State that the North Pole is at the top and the South Pole is at the bottom of the Earth
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you hand {{name}} a globe, can they point to the North Pole and the South Pole and tell you they're the coldest places on Earth?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 寒冷天气的适应
topics.description: 了解极地动物如何适应极端寒冷的环境——海豹和鲸鱼有厚厚的脂肪层（鲸脂）来保暖，北极熊的中空毛发能锁住空气保暖，企鹅鳍状肢中的逆流热交换能防止热量散失，北极狐会长出厚厚的白色冬毛来伪装和保暖，还有一些动物会迁徙以避开最严酷的月份。
evidence: Describe at least three cold-weather adaptations: blubber, hollow fur, counter-current heat exchange, white winter coats, or migration
Explain the purpose of each adaptation (e.g. blubber insulates against cold water, white fur provides camouflage in snow)
Use the word adaptation correctly to mean a feature that helps an animal survive in its environment
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain several ways polar animals survive the freezing cold — like a polar bear's hollow fur trapping warm air, a seal's thick blubber, or an Arctic fox changing colour in winter?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 比较北极和南极
topics.description: 详细比较北极和南极——北极是被浮冰覆盖的海洋，周围有陆地（加拿大、俄罗斯、格陵兰、斯堪的纳维亚），而南极是被厚达4公里冰层覆盖的大陆，比欧洲还大；北极熊、北极狐和海象只生活在北极，而企鹅、豹海豹和信天翁只生活在南极。
evidence: State that the Arctic is a frozen ocean surrounded by land (name at least two bordering countries), while Antarctica is a continent covered by ice sheet up to 4 km thick
Correctly assign at least three animals to the Arctic and three to the Antarctic
Name at least two differences in human presence: indigenous peoples in the Arctic vs research stations only in Antarctica
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in detail how the Arctic and Antarctic are different — which animals live where, that one is frozen ocean and the other is a frozen continent, and which countries border the Arctic?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 冰与物质的状态
topics.description: 了解冰的不同形态和物质的状态——海水结冰会形成海冰（含盐、比较薄），积雪经过数百年压实会形成冰川冰（淡水、非常厚），冰山从冰川上断裂后漂浮在海面上；知道水有固态（冰）、液态（水）和气态（水蒸气）三种状态，并且盐会降低水的冰点。
evidence: Distinguish between sea ice (frozen ocean, salty, thin) and glacial ice (compacted snow, fresh water, thick)
Explain that icebergs break off from glaciers and float because ice is less dense than liquid water
Describe the three states of water (solid, liquid, gas) and explain that salt lowers the freezing point
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between sea ice and glacier ice, and describe how water changes between solid, liquid, and gas — maybe by doing a simple freezing experiment with salt and fresh water?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 因纽特人和萨米人
topics.description: 了解原住民已经在北极地区生活了数千年——因纽特人分布在加拿大、阿拉斯加和格陵兰，萨米人生活在斯堪的纳维亚北部——他们积累了非凡的环境知识，使用狗拉雪橇和皮划艇作为交通工具，穿着兽皮衣服保暖，建造冰屋作为临时住所，并深深尊重他们赖以生存的动物和土地。
evidence: Name the Inuit (Canada, Alaska, Greenland) and Sami (northern Scandinavia) as Arctic indigenous peoples
Describe at least three aspects of traditional Arctic life: dog sleds, kayaks, animal-skin clothing, igloos, or hunting practices
Explain that indigenous Arctic peoples have deep knowledge of their environment developed over thousands of years
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you about the Inuit and Sami peoples who have lived in the Arctic for thousands of years — how they travel by dog sled, wear animal-skin clothing, and know the ice and animals incredibly well?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 极地食物链
topics.description: 了解极地食物链——在南极，浮游植物被磷虾吃掉，磷虾被鱼类和企鹅吃掉，企鹅被豹海豹和虎鲸吃掉；在北极，冰下的藻类喂养浮游动物，浮游动物喂养鱼类，鱼类喂养海豹，海豹喂养北极熊——像磷虾和浮游生物这样的小生物是所有极地生命的基础。
evidence: Construct an Antarctic food chain: phytoplankton → krill → penguin → leopard seal or orca
Construct an Arctic food chain: algae → zooplankton → fish → seal → polar bear
Explain why krill and plankton are critical — without them, the entire food chain collapses
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain a polar food chain — starting from tiny plankton, through krill and fish, up to seals and polar bears or orcas — and explain why the tiny creatures at the bottom are so important?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 北极苔原
topics.description: 了解什么是北极苔原——一片广阔、没有树木的土地，地表下方是永久冻土（永远冻结的地面），夏季生长期非常短，苔藓、地衣和耐寒的草类会迅速生长，这里也是驯鹿、麝牛、旅鼠和雪鸮的家园。
evidence: Describe the tundra as a treeless landscape with permafrost (permanently frozen ground) beneath the surface
Explain that the tundra has a very short summer growing season when mosses, lichens, and grasses grow quickly
Name at least three tundra animals: caribou/reindeer, musk oxen, lemmings, or snowy owls
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know what tundra is — the huge flat landscape near the Arctic with no trees, frozen ground underneath, and short summers where everything bursts into life?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 南极竞赛
topics.description: 详细了解南极竞赛的故事——挪威人罗尔德·阿蒙森和英国人罗伯特·法尔肯·斯科特都在1911年出发，阿蒙森使用狗拉雪橇并精心计划，于12月14日率先到达；斯科特晚34天到达，使用人力拉雪橇，在返程中与队员不幸遇难；还要了解欧内斯特·沙克尔顿1914年的坚忍号探险，船被冰困住并压碎，以及沙克尔顿乘小船到南乔治亚岛营救全体船员的非凡旅程。
evidence: Describe the Scott vs Amundsen race: Amundsen arrived 14 December 1911 using dog sleds; Scott arrived 34 days later and died on the return
Explain at least two reasons Amundsen succeeded: better planning, dog sleds, polar experience, and lighter supplies
Narrate the key events of the Endurance expedition: ship crushed, camps on ice, boat journey to South Georgia, all crew rescued
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you the detailed story of Amundsen and Scott's race to the South Pole — who won and why, what went wrong for Scott, and the incredible survival story of Shackleton's Endurance?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 为什么极地季节如此极端
topics.description: 了解为什么两极有极端的季节——地球的自转轴倾斜约23.5°，因此当它绕太阳公转时，每个极点在半年内朝向太阳倾斜（持续白天，较温暖的夏季），半年内背离太阳倾斜（持续黑暗，严寒的冬季）；这种倾斜也驱动了海冰在冬季扩张、夏季退缩的年度循环，并引发动物的迁徙和繁殖等行为。
evidence: Explain that Earth's axis is tilted at about 23.5° and this tilt causes the extreme polar seasons
Describe how the tilt means each pole faces toward the Sun for half the year (summer/daylight) and away for the other half (winter/darkness)
Connect the seasonal cycle to at least one animal behaviour, such as migration or sea ice retreat affecting hunting
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain WHY the poles have months of daylight in summer and months of darkness in winter — that it's because Earth is tilted on its axis as it goes around the Sun?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 南极条约与科学研究
topics.description: 知道南极洲受《南极条约》管理（1959年签署，1961年生效）——该条约将南极洲专用于和平目的和科学研究，禁止军事活动和采矿，已有50多个国家签署；理解国际研究站研究气候、天文、生物学和地质学，南极洲是地球上最接近一个为科学而非政治而存在的大陆
evidence: State that the Antarctic Treaty (1959) sets Antarctica aside for peace and science, banning military activity and mining
Know that over 50 countries have signed the treaty and that many operate research stations
Name at least two areas of scientific research conducted in Antarctica: climate, astronomy, biology, or geology
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know about the Antarctic Treaty — that over 50 countries agreed Antarctica should be used only for science and peace, not war or mining — and that research stations there study everything from ice to stars?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 极地气候变化
topics.description: 了解气候变化如何影响极地地区——北极海冰正在急剧减少（自1979年以来每十年减少约13%），格陵兰和南极冰盖正在融化，导致海平面上升，永久冻土正在解冻并释放甲烷（一种强效温室气体），这些变化形成了正反馈循环：融化导致更多变暖，更多变暖又导致更多融化。
evidence: State that Arctic sea ice has been declining at roughly 13% per decade since 1979
Explain the positive feedback loop: warming → ice melts → dark ocean absorbs more heat → more warming → more melting
Describe at least two consequences of polar ice loss: sea level rise and permafrost thawing releasing methane
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how climate change is melting polar ice — that Arctic sea ice is shrinking, ice sheets are losing mass, and that melting actually makes more melting happen in a vicious cycle?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 地球的冰冻水
topics.description: 了解冰冻圈及其在地球水系统中的作用——冰冻圈是地球上所有冰冻的水（冰盖、冰川、海冰、永久冻土、积雪）；极地冰盖储存了地球约69%的淡水；如果所有极地冰都融化，海平面将上升超过65米；水循环通过蒸发、降水和融水流入海洋，将极地冰与全球系统连接起来。
evidence: Define the cryosphere as all frozen water on Earth and name its components: ice sheets, glaciers, sea ice, permafrost, snow
State that polar ice sheets hold approximately 69% of Earth's fresh water
Explain how polar ice connects to the global water cycle and what would happen if it all melted (65m+ sea level rise)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that most of Earth's fresh water is actually locked up as ice at the poles — and that if it all melted, the sea would rise over 65 metres, flooding coastal cities worldwide?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 冰川与冰盖
topics.description: 了解冰川和冰盖是如何形成和运动的——积雪经过数百年堆积并压缩成密实的冰，冰川在自身重量的作用下缓慢向下流动，刻蚀出U形山谷并堆积冰碛物；格陵兰冰盖和南极冰盖加在一起所储存的冰足以让海平面上升超过65米；从这些冰盖钻取的冰芯中封存着气泡，能揭示地球过去80万年的气候历史。
evidence: Describe how glaciers form: snow accumulates, compresses, and becomes dense ice that flows slowly under its own weight
Explain that the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets hold enough water to raise sea levels dramatically if melted
Describe how ice cores reveal climate history through trapped air bubbles from hundreds of thousands of years ago
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how glaciers form from layers of snow pressed into ice, how they slowly carve valleys, and that scientists drill into ice sheets to learn about Earth's climate thousands of years ago?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 极地气候带
topics.description: 了解极地地区属于极地气候带——地球五大主要气候带之一（热带、干旱带、温带、大陆性气候带、极地气候带）。极地气候的特点是：即使在夏天，气温也很少超过10°C；降水极少（极地沙漠的降雨量比撒哈拉沙漠还少）；风力强劲。知道纬度是决定气候带的关键因素，极地地区位于北纬/南纬60°以上。
evidence: Name the five main climate zones and place polar regions correctly within them
State that polar regions are above approximately 60° latitude and explain that distance from the Equator is the main reason they are cold
Describe polar climate characteristics: rarely above 10°C in summer, very low precipitation, strong winds
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain where the polar climate zone fits among Earth's five climate zones, and why the poles are so cold — linking it to their position at high latitudes far from the Equator?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 极地保护与未来
topics.description: 了解极地地区面临的保护挑战——南大洋的海洋保护区旨在保护南极生态系统；随着冰层退缩，北极国家就北方航线和资源的归属权产生争议；原住民为土地权利和参与环境决策的权利而斗争；国际合作（《巴黎协定》、《南极条约》）至关重要，但随着经济压力增大，维持合作变得困难。
evidence: Describe at least two conservation measures: marine protected areas in the Southern Ocean and the Antarctic Treaty
Explain why Arctic sovereignty is contested as ice retreats and shipping routes open
Describe the role of indigenous peoples in Arctic environmental decisions and why their knowledge matters
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} discuss the big challenges facing the poles — like countries arguing over Arctic resources as ice melts, the push for marine protected areas in Antarctica, and why indigenous peoples' voices matter in these decisions?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 极地生态系统对比
topics.description: 比较北极和南极的生态系统——北极既有陆地（苔原）生态系统，也有海洋生态系统，支持着大型陆地哺乳动物和原住民人类社区；而南极几乎完全以海洋为基础，几乎没有陆地植物或哺乳动物。两个地区的食物链都很短但强度大，以浮游植物和磷虾为基础，并且都受到气候变化和人类活动的极大影响。
evidence: Compare Arctic (terrestrial + marine, land mammals, human communities) with Antarctic (almost entirely marine, no land mammals)
Explain that both polar food chains depend on phytoplankton and krill at the base
Describe why polar ecosystems are particularly vulnerable to climate change (short food chains, specialised organisms)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} compare the Arctic and Antarctic ecosystems — explaining that the Arctic has land animals and people while Antarctica's life is almost all in the sea, and that both depend on tiny creatures like krill?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 极地探索的过去与现在
topics.description: 比较历史上的极地探索与现代极地科学——英雄时代（1897-1922年）依靠船只、雪橇犬和人类的耐力，许多人因此丧生；而今天的极地科学家使用GPS、卫星、破冰船、供暖研究站和飞机；了解现代挑战包括研究气候变化数据，并且极地科学现在包括多元化的国际团队，其中包括像冰川学家莉兹·托马斯和海洋生物学家西尔维亚·厄尔这样的女性科学家。
evidence: Compare Heroic Age exploration (dog sleds, man-hauling, many deaths) with modern science (GPS, satellites, icebreakers, heated stations)
Name at least two technologies that make modern polar science possible
Name a modern polar scientist and explain that today's polar teams are diverse and international
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} compare old polar exploration — dog sleds, freezing camps, real danger of death — with modern polar science using satellites, heated research stations, and diverse international teams?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 极地海洋与全球气候
topics.description: 了解极地海洋如何与全球气候系统相连——寒冷、密度大的极地海水下沉，驱动温盐环流（全球洋流传送带）；海冰将阳光反射回太空（反照率效应），帮助调节地球温度；南极洲周围的南大洋因上升流带来营养盐，是地球上生产力最高的海洋生态系统之一。
evidence: Explain that cold, dense polar water sinks and drives global ocean circulation (thermohaline circulation)
Describe the albedo effect: white ice reflects sunlight back to space, while dark ocean absorbs heat
State that the Southern Ocean is extremely productive because upwelling brings nutrients to the surface
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how cold polar water sinks and drives a global conveyor belt of ocean currents, and how white sea ice reflects sunlight to help keep the planet cool?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 来自雨林的日常食物
topics.description: 知道许多日常食物来自雨林——巧克力由可可豆制成，香蕉生长在热带森林中，咖啡果在森林树荫下成熟，巴西坚果从巨树上掉落——将我们的日常生活与遥远的森林联系起来
evidence: Name at least three foods that come from rainforests, such as chocolate (cacao), bananas, and Brazil nuts
Explain that cacao beans grow on trees in the rainforest and are made into chocolate
Connect their own food choices to rainforest origins by identifying a product they eat that comes from the forest
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is eating a chocolate bar or a banana, can they tell you that those foods originally come from rainforests?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林原住民
topics.description: 知道像亚诺马米人这样的原住民已经在雨林里生活了几千年，他们用森林里的材料建造房屋，通过打猎、捕鱼和采集来寻找食物，并且对森林及其动植物有着深入的了解。
evidence: Explain that indigenous peoples like the Yanomami have lived in rainforests for thousands of years
Describe how they use the forest for shelter, food, and medicine
Show respect for indigenous knowledge by explaining that these communities understand the forest very deeply
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that some people have lived in rainforests for thousands of years — building their homes from the trees and knowing which plants are food and which are medicine?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林里面
topics.description: 描述身处雨林中的感觉——又热又黏（潮湿），因为树冠遮挡阳光所以地面很暗，到处是动物的叫声和昆虫的嗡嗡声，还有雨水和凝结的水珠不断滴落。
evidence: Describe the air inside a rainforest as hot and sticky (humid)
Explain that the forest floor is dark because tall trees block most of the sunlight
Name at least two sounds you would hear in a rainforest, such as bird calls, insect buzzing, or rain dripping
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a rainforest video clip, can they describe what it would feel, sound, and look like to stand inside — the heat, the noise, the darkness on the ground?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林动物
topics.description: 说出并认识雨林中的标志性动物——美洲豹、巨嘴鸟、树懒、箭毒蛙、吼猴、金刚鹦鹉和蝴蝶——并知道它们各自生活在雨林的哪一层
evidence: Name at least five iconic rainforest animals such as jaguars, toucans, sloths, poison dart frogs, and howler monkeys
Match at least three animals to the rainforest layer where they live (e.g. monkeys in the canopy, jaguars on the forest floor)
Describe one distinctive feature of each named animal
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name at least five animals that live in the rainforest and tell you something about each — like a toucan's big colourful beak or a sloth hanging upside down in the trees?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林昆虫
topics.description: 知道雨林是数百万昆虫的家园——切叶蚁会种植真菌，巨型甲虫、宝石般闪亮的蝴蝶、巨大的蜘蛛和竹节虫都生活在这里——昆虫是雨林里数量最多的动物
evidence: Name at least three types of insect or minibeast found in the rainforest, such as leaf-cutter ants, morpho butterflies, and giant beetles
Explain that insects are the most numerous animals in the rainforest
Describe one interesting behaviour, such as leaf-cutter ants carrying leaf pieces back to grow fungus
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that rainforests are packed with insects — like leaf-cutter ants that carry bits of leaf in a long line, or butterflies as big as a dinner plate?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林分层
topics.description: 知道雨林从地面到天空共有四层——森林地面层（黑暗、潮湿，满是正在腐烂的落叶）、林下层（树荫下的小树和灌木）、树冠层（厚厚的树顶像屋顶，大多数动物住在这里）和露生层（最高的树穿过树冠层，伸进明亮的阳光里）
evidence: Name the four rainforest layers in order from ground to sky: forest floor, understory, canopy, emergent
Describe one key feature of each layer, such as the canopy being a thick roof of leaves or the forest floor being dark and damp
Explain that most rainforest animals live in the canopy because that is where there is food and light
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} draws a rainforest, can they show the four layers — the dark forest floor, the shady understory, the leafy canopy, and the tallest emergent trees poking into the sky?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林植物
topics.description: 了解雨林中植物种类极其丰富——高耸的吉贝树和巴西坚果树、称为藤本的攀缘藤蔓、生长在树枝上的彩色兰花、巨大的睡莲，以及能汇聚雨水的巨大叶片
evidence: Name at least three types of rainforest plant, such as kapok trees, lianas (climbing vines), and orchids
Explain that rainforest plants grow very tall because they compete for sunlight
Describe one unusual feature, such as orchids growing on tree branches or lianas climbing up trunks
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name some plants that grow in the rainforest — like giant trees, climbing vines, or orchids that grow on branches — and explain why they grow so big and tall?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 什么是雨林？
topics.description: 知道雨林是生长在赤道附近炎热潮湿地区的茂密高大的森林，那里几乎天天下雨，形成温暖潮湿的环境，植物和动物在那里茁壮成长。
evidence: Describe a rainforest as a forest that is hot and wet, located near the Equator
Explain that it rains very often in a rainforest, which is why the plants grow so tall and thick
Point to the Equator on a globe and say that rainforests are found in the hot belt near it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a picture of a thick, green jungle with huge trees and dangling vines, can they tell you it's a rainforest and explain that it's hot and rainy there almost every day?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林在哪里
topics.description: 知道雨林分布在地球中部的一条带上——在南美洲（亚马逊）、中非（刚果）和东南亚——并且除了南极洲和欧洲，每个大洲都有雨林。
evidence: Point to the Amazon, Congo, and Southeast Asian rainforest regions on a world map
Explain that rainforests grow near the Equator where it is hot and wet all year
Name at least two continents that have large rainforests
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you show {{name}} a world map, can they point to where rainforests grow — near the middle of the Earth in places like South America, Africa, and Asia?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林生物分类
topics.description: 根据可观察的特征，将雨林生物分到主要类别中——哺乳动物（美洲豹、猴子、蝙蝠）、鸟类（巨嘴鸟、金刚鹦鹉、蜂鸟）、爬行动物（蛇、蜥蜴、凯门鳄）、两栖动物（树蛙、箭毒蛙）、昆虫（蝴蝶、蚂蚁、甲虫）和植物（树木、附生植物、蕨类）
evidence: Sort at least eight rainforest organisms into correct groups: mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, insects, or plants
State the key feature that defines each group (e.g. mammals have fur and feed milk to their young)
Explain why classification helps scientists understand and study the huge variety of life in rainforests
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks at pictures of different rainforest creatures, can they sort them into groups like mammals, birds, reptiles, and insects, and explain why each one belongs in its group?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 原住民生态知识
topics.description: 了解雨林原住民在数千年中积累了深厚的生态知识——他们用植物做药、食物和建筑材料，采用轮耕等可持续农耕方式，并理解动物行为和森林生态，而现代科学才刚刚开始认识到这些知识的价值。
evidence: Give at least two examples of indigenous knowledge, such as using specific plants as medicine or practising sustainable farming
Explain what shifting cultivation is and why it is less harmful to the forest than permanent clearing
Describe how indigenous knowledge and modern science can work together to protect rainforests
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that indigenous rainforest peoples know an enormous amount about forest plants and animals — like which plants cure illnesses — and that scientists are learning from this knowledge?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林动物的生存绝招
topics.description: 了解雨林动物如何适应环境——伪装帮助叶虫和树蛙躲藏，鲜艳的警告色（警戒色）表明箭毒蛙有毒，卷尾让猴子能抓住树枝，巨嘴鸟的大嘴帮助够到远处的果实，许多动物在夜间活动以避开白天的炎热
evidence: Describe at least three animal adaptations such as camouflage, warning colours, and prehensile tails
Explain how each adaptation helps the animal survive (e.g. camouflage hides prey from predators)
Give a specific example for each adaptation, linking the animal to its rainforest layer
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a poison dart frog is so brightly coloured — that it's warning predators it's dangerous — or why a sloth moves so slowly that algae grows on its fur, helping it blend in?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林食物网
topics.description: 了解能量和营养物质如何在雨林食物网中流动——从植物（生产者）到食草动物（初级消费者）再到捕食者（次级消费者）——以及像真菌和昆虫这样的分解者如何分解森林地面上的死亡物质，将营养物质回收回土壤中供植物再次利用。
evidence: Construct a simple rainforest food chain with at least three levels: producer → herbivore → predator
Explain the role of decomposers in breaking down dead material and returning nutrients to the soil
Use the terms producer, consumer, and decomposer correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain a rainforest food chain — like how a fruit tree feeds a monkey, the monkey might be hunted by a jaguar, and when things die, tiny organisms break them down to feed the trees again?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林植物的适应
topics.description: 了解雨林植物如何适应它们的环境——滴水叶尖能让雨水快速流走，防止腐烂；板根宽宽地展开，在贫瘠的土壤中支撑高大的树木；附生植物（如兰花和凤梨）长在树枝上，不用土壤就能获得阳光；藤本植物攀爬树干，到达树冠层
evidence: Describe at least three plant adaptations: drip-tip leaves, buttress roots, and epiphytes
Explain the purpose of each adaptation (e.g. drip-tips shed water to prevent rot)
Use the word adaptation to mean a feature that helps an organism survive in its environment
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why some rainforest trees have huge roots spreading out like wings, or why leaves have pointy tips that water drips off — that these are clever adaptations to life in a hot, wet forest?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林水循环
topics.description: 了解雨林中的水循环是如何运作的——树木通过根部吸收水分，再通过叶片释放水分（蒸腾作用），这些水汽在树冠上方形成云，云产生降雨，雨水又落回森林——形成一个自我维持的循环，为雨林提供了大部分自身的降雨
evidence: Describe the sequence: trees absorb water → release it through leaves (transpiration) → moisture rises → clouds form → rain falls
Explain that rainforests generate much of their own rainfall through this cycle
Use the word transpiration correctly when describing how water leaves a plant through its leaves
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how rainforest trees help make their own rain — by releasing water from their leaves, which forms clouds, which rain back down on the forest?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 亚马逊雨林
topics.description: 知道亚马逊是地球上最大的雨林——横跨南美洲九个国家，拥有世界上水量最大的河流，并且是地球上约10%物种的家园，包括40,000种植物、1,300种鸟类和3,000种鱼类。
evidence: Locate the Amazon rainforest on a map of South America and name at least two countries it spans
State that the Amazon contains the world's largest river by volume and is home to roughly 10% of all species on Earth
Give at least two specific numbers showing the Amazon's biodiversity, such as 40,000 plant species or 1,300 bird species
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you about the Amazon — that it's the biggest rainforest in the world, spread across nine countries, with more types of animals and plants than almost anywhere else on Earth?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 热带雨林气候
topics.description: 了解热带雨林属于热带气候——全年持续炎热（25–30°C），年降雨量超过2000毫米——这种高温高湿的组合为植物快速生长和极其丰富的生物多样性创造了理想条件。
evidence: State that tropical rainforests are hot (25–30°C) and wet (over 2000 mm rain per year) all year round
Explain that the constant heat and moisture create ideal growing conditions for plants
Compare tropical rainforest climate to the UK or local climate, noting key differences in temperature and rainfall
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why rainforests grow so well — that it's the combination of being really hot and really rainy all year round that makes everything grow so fast?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 森林砍伐的原因与规模
topics.description: 了解雨林被砍伐的原因和规模——养牛（亚马逊地区最大的驱动因素）、大豆和棕榈油种植园、木材采伐和采矿——并知道全球每年约损失1000万公顷森林，对生物多样性、气候和土著社区造成毁灭性后果。
evidence: Name at least three major causes of deforestation: cattle ranching, palm oil, soy, logging, and mining
State that approximately 10 million hectares of forest are lost globally each year
Explain the impact of deforestation on at least two of: biodiversity, climate, and indigenous peoples
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why rainforests are being cut down — naming causes like cattle farming, palm oil, and logging — and say roughly how fast it's happening?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 薄土壤中的养分循环
topics.description: 理解雨林养分循环的悖论——尽管雨林生长茂盛，但雨林土壤通常很薄且缺乏养分，因为大部分养分被锁在生物体内，而不是土壤中；在温暖潮湿的条件下，分解速度很快，死亡物质释放的养分立即被植物根系和真菌吸收，形成一个快速、闭环的回收系统。
evidence: Explain that rainforest soil is thin and nutrient-poor despite the lush growth above
Describe the rapid decomposition cycle: dead material → decomposers → nutrients released → immediately absorbed by roots
Explain why clearing rainforest for farming fails after a few years — once the trees are gone, the nutrients are lost
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the surprising fact that rainforest soil is actually poor and thin — that the nutrients aren't in the ground but locked inside the living plants and animals, constantly being recycled?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林生物多样性
topics.description: 理解雨林是生物多样性的热点地区——它们只覆盖地球陆地表面的6%，却拥有超过50%的已知动植物物种——这种极其丰富的生物多样性使雨林在全球生物多样性中不可替代，也是保护工作的优先区域。
evidence: State that rainforests cover about 6% of Earth's land but hold over 50% of all species
Explain why this concentration of species makes rainforests a conservation priority
Give specific examples of rainforest biodiversity, such as one hectare containing more tree species than all of northern Europe
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the mind-boggling fact that rainforests cover only a tiny fraction of Earth but are home to more than half of all species — and why that makes protecting them so important?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林保护
topics.description: 了解保护雨林的主要方法——保护区和国家公园、重新造林和野化项目、可持续认证体系（雨林联盟、FSC）、承认原住民土地权是最有效的森林保护形式，以及像REDD+这样通过付费让国家保留森林的国际协议
evidence: Name at least three conservation approaches: protected areas, reforestation, sustainable certification, and indigenous land rights
Explain why protecting indigenous territories is one of the most effective ways to prevent deforestation
Describe what certification labels like Rainforest Alliance or FSC mean and how they help
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what people are doing to save the rainforests — like creating nature reserves, planting new trees, supporting indigenous land rights, and buying certified sustainable products?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林的未来与权衡取舍
topics.description: 理解雨林的未来取决于平衡相互竞争的需求——当地社区的经济发展、原住民对其祖传土地的权利、全球生物多样性保护以及气候稳定——并且没有简单的答案，需要政府、企业、科学家、原住民领袖和全球消费者之间的合作。
evidence: Name at least three competing interests: economic development, indigenous rights, biodiversity, and climate stability
Explain why there is no single simple solution to rainforest protection
Suggest how different groups (governments, businesses, consumers, scientists) can each contribute to a better outcome
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} discuss the tricky problem of rainforest protection — that farmers need land, companies want resources, indigenous people have rights, and the whole planet needs the forests for climate — and there's no easy answer?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 日常生活中的雨林产品
topics.description: 了解雨林产品如何通过全球供应链与日常生活紧密相连——棕榈油存在于零食、肥皂和化妆品中；大豆喂养着世界各地的牲畜；可可变成巧克力；橡胶用于轮胎和手套；木材变成家具；许多药物源自雨林植物——而消费者的选择可以推动雨林走向毁灭或可持续发展。
evidence: Name at least four products linked to rainforests: palm oil, soy, cocoa, rubber, timber, and medicines
Explain how a product like palm oil travels from a rainforest region to a supermarket shelf
Describe how consumer choices (e.g. buying Rainforest Alliance certified products) can reduce deforestation pressure
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} check ingredient labels at the supermarket and spot products linked to rainforests — like palm oil in biscuits or cocoa in chocolate — and explain why choosing sustainable versions helps protect forests?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨林与全球气候
topics.description: 了解雨林与全球气候之间的联系——雨林通过光合作用吸收二氧化碳并释放氧气，在生物量中储存大量碳，并通过蒸腾作用产生降雨；当森林被烧毁或砍伐时，储存的碳会以二氧化碳的形式释放出来，加速气候变化并破坏区域降雨模式。
evidence: Explain that rainforests absorb CO₂ and store carbon in their trees, acting as a carbon sink
Describe how deforestation releases stored carbon back into the atmosphere, accelerating climate change
Explain that transpiration from rainforest trees generates rainfall, and losing trees disrupts rain patterns
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how rainforests help fight climate change by absorbing carbon dioxide — and how cutting them down makes climate change worse by releasing all that stored carbon?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 温带雨林
topics.description: 知道并非所有雨林都是热带的——温带雨林存在于较凉爽湿润的地区，如北美太平洋西北部、苏格兰西部和威尔士、智利南部以及新西兰——它们具有相似的特征（降雨量高、树木披满苔藓、树冠茂密），但物种不同，包括古老的橡树、巨型红杉和树蕨
evidence: Name at least two locations of temperate rainforests, such as the Pacific Northwest, western Scotland, or southern Chile
Compare temperate and tropical rainforests: both have high rainfall and dense canopy, but differ in temperature and species
Name species found in temperate rainforests, such as ancient oaks, giant redwoods, or tree ferns
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that rainforests aren't only in hot places — that there are cool, misty rainforests in places like Wales, Scotland, and the Pacific Northwest, with mossy trees and ferns instead of monkeys and parrots?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 提出科学问题
topics.description: 提出简单的科学问题，并认识到这些问题可以通过不同的方式回答，包括观察、实验和研究
evidence: Ask at least three 'how' or 'why' questions about the natural world
Suggest different ways to answer a question: observing, testing, asking an expert, reading a book
Choose an appropriate method to investigate a specific question
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} wonders about something — like 'why do leaves change colour?' — can they suggest how to find the answer, whether by looking closely, doing a test, or looking it up?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 比较设计方案
topics.description: 分析两个为解决同一问题而设计的物体的测试数据，比较每种设计的优缺点。
evidence: Test two designs that address the same problem and collect data on their performance
Compare the results, identifying strengths and weaknesses of each design
Use data as evidence to recommend which design works better and suggest improvements
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} tests two different paper aeroplane designs, can they compare the results and explain which one flew better and why?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 用草图建模
topics.description: 绘制简单的草图、图画或制作实物模型，说明物体的形状如何帮助它发挥功能，以解决给定的问题。
evidence: Create a sketch, drawing, or physical model of a design solution
Explain how the shape or structure of the design helps solve the problem
Relate the model to the real-world problem it addresses
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw or build a model to show how they'd design something — like a boat shape that floats well — and explain why the shape matters?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 使用简单工具观察
topics.description: 使用手持放大镜等简单工具仔细观察，并利用观察结果来描述、比较和识别事物。
evidence: Use a hand lens or other simple equipment to make detailed observations
Describe observations using specific vocabulary (colour, shape, size, texture, pattern)
Compare two objects based on careful observation, noting similarities and differences
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} use a magnifying glass to look carefully at something like a leaf or an insect and describe in detail what they see?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 记录数据
topics.description: 用简单的方法收集和记录数据，比如表格、计数符号和图画，来帮助回答问题
evidence: Record observations and measurements in a simple table or tally chart
Use drawings or labelled diagrams to record what was observed
Explain how the recorded data helps answer the original question
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} collect information during an experiment — like counting, measuring, or drawing — and put it into a simple table or chart?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 简单测试和实验
topics.description: 进行简单的测试，并运用观察和想法来提出问题的答案
evidence: Carry out a simple test with one thing changing at a time
Observe what happens and describe the result
Use the result to suggest an answer to the original question
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} do a simple experiment — like testing which paper towel absorbs the most water — and use what they find out to answer the question?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 用证据改变想法
topics.description: 当证据不支持你的预测时，要愿意改变自己的想法——一个让你惊讶的结果比一个证实你原有想法的结果更有价值。
evidence: belief revision in children research (PMC 2020)
hypothesis testing and argumentation from evidence in young children
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} predicts what will happen in an experiment and gets a different result, do they accept the evidence rather than deciding the experiment must have gone wrong?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 观察与解释
topics.description: 注意区分你观察到的事实和你认为它意味着什么——'冰融化了'是观察；'冰因为受热而融化'是解释。
evidence: observation vs interpretation in primary science
BERA: children's observation skills in nature
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} does a science activity, can they tell the difference between what they actually saw or measured — and what they think caused it or what it means?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 生物分类
topics.description: 通过表格、条形图、标注图和分类检索表等多种方式收集、记录、分类和展示数据
evidence: Organise data into a clear table with appropriate headings
Create a bar chart or pictogram from collected data
Use labelled diagrams and classification keys to present findings
topics.assessmentPrompt: After doing an experiment, can {{name}} put their results into a neat table, draw a bar chart, and add labels to a diagram to show what they found?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 还有别的解释吗？
topics.description: 对于任何结果，都要问一问：还有别的解释吗？——第一个看似合理的解释不一定就是对的，优秀的科学家会主动寻找其他可能的解释。
evidence: prompts to consider alternative possible worlds research (6-7 year olds)
scientific thinking promotes critical thinking (MDPI 2025)
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} comes up with an explanation for something they observed, do they try to think of at least one other possible explanation before deciding they've found the answer?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 从证据中得出结论
topics.description: 用口头和书面解释报告探究发现，得出简单结论，做出预测，并提出改进建议
evidence: Write or present a clear report of findings from an investigation
Draw a conclusion that answers the original question, supported by data
Make a prediction for a new situation based on the results, and suggest improvements to the method
topics.assessmentPrompt: After finishing an experiment, can {{name}} explain what they found out, what it means, what they'd predict for next time, and how they could improve the test?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 公平测试
topics.description: 设计简单的实践探究、对比测试和公平测试，理解一次只改变一个变量的重要性
evidence: Explain what makes a test 'fair' (only one variable changes, everything else stays the same)
Identify the variable to change, the variable to measure, and the variables to keep the same
Set up and carry out a comparative or fair test with support
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to find out which soil is best for growing beans, can they set up a fair test where only the soil changes and everything else stays the same?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 精确测量
topics.description: 进行系统而仔细的观察，使用标准单位和设备（包括温度计和数据记录器）进行精确测量。
evidence: Use at least three types of measuring equipment correctly (ruler, thermometer, measuring jug, scales)
Read measurements in standard units (cm, ml, °C, g) with reasonable accuracy
Make systematic observations by following a planned method consistently
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} use a thermometer to measure temperature accurately, read a ruler in centimetres, and record measurements carefully during an experiment?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 用证据回答问题
topics.description: 识别与科学想法相关的不同点、相似点或变化，并使用简单的科学证据来回答问题或支持发现。
evidence: Identify at least one pattern (similarity, difference, or trend) in a set of scientific data
Explain how the pattern relates to the scientific idea being investigated
Use specific data points as evidence when answering a scientific question
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} looks at their experiment results, can they spot patterns — like things that are similar, different, or changing — and use the evidence to back up their answer?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 比较可能的解决方案
topics.description: 针对一个问题，根据每个方案满足标准和限制条件的程度，生成并比较多个可能的解决方案。
evidence: Generate at least three possible solutions to a defined design problem
Compare solutions against the specified criteria and constraints
Select the most promising solution with reasoning for the choice
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} brainstorm several different solutions to a design challenge and then compare them to decide which one best meets the requirements?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 相关性与因果关系
topics.description: 两件事同时发生并不意味着其中一件导致了另一件——在得出结论之前，要认识到相关性和因果关系的区别。
evidence: developmental changes in children's recognition of evidence relevance to causal explanations
causal learning research
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} noticed that children who eat breakfast tend to do better at school, would they understand that breakfast might not be the cause — there could be another reason both things are true?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 公平测试（8岁以上）
topics.description: 设计并实施公平测试，控制变量并考虑可能失败的地方，找出模型或原型中可以改进的方面。
evidence: Plan a fair test of a prototype with clearly identified variables to control
Carry out the test and identify failure points or weaknesses in the design
Propose specific improvements based on test results and retest
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} builds and tests a prototype, can they run a fair test, find what didn't work, and figure out how to make it better?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 简单的设计问题
topics.description: 定义一个简单的设计问题，反映某种需求或愿望，包括明确的成功标准和材料、时间或成本方面的限制条件
evidence: Define a design problem by describing the need or want it addresses
Specify at least two criteria for a successful solution (e.g. must hold X weight, must cost less than Y)
Identify constraints such as available materials, time limits, or cost
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} clearly state what problem they're trying to solve with a design, what would make it successful, and what limits they have on materials or time?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 精确测量
topics.description: 使用各种科学仪器进行越来越准确和精确的测量，并在适当的时候重复读数
evidence: Use scientific equipment (scales, thermometers, measuring cylinders, stopwatches) with increasing precision
Explain why repeat readings improve reliability and take at least three readings
Identify and deal with anomalous results (measurements that don't fit the pattern)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} measure things precisely during experiments, know when to take repeat readings for reliability, and spot when a measurement seems wrong?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 生物分类（9岁以上）
topics.description: 使用科学图表、分类检索表、表格、散点图、条形图和折线图，记录日益复杂的数据和结果。
evidence: Choose and create an appropriate graph type for the data (bar chart, line graph, scatter graph)
Draw graphs with correctly labelled axes, appropriate scales, and accurate plotting
Use classification keys and scientific diagrams to present complex findings
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} choose the right type of graph for their data — a bar chart for categories or a line graph for continuous data — and draw it accurately?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 控制变量
topics.description: 设计不同类型的科学探究来回答问题，在必要时识别并控制变量
evidence: Independently plan an investigation identifying the independent, dependent, and controlled variables
Choose the appropriate type of enquiry for the question (fair test, observation over time, pattern seeking, research)
Explain why controlling variables is essential for valid results
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} plan their own experiment from scratch — deciding what to test, what to measure, what to keep the same, and how many times to repeat it?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 从证据中得出结论（9岁以上）
topics.description: 用口头和书面形式报告和展示发现，包括结论、因果关系、解释以及对结果的信任程度
evidence: Present findings clearly in written and oral form with appropriate scientific vocabulary
Identify causal relationships (X caused Y because...) supported by evidence
Discuss the degree of trust in results, considering sample size, repeat readings, and possible errors
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write up or present their experiment results, explain what caused what, and discuss how confident they are in their findings?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 支持观点的证据
topics.description: 识别用来支持或反驳观点或论点的科学证据，并评估证据的力度。
evidence: Distinguish between a claim and the evidence supporting it
Evaluate whether evidence is strong (fair test, multiple trials) or weak (single observation, no controls)
Identify when evidence supports or refutes a scientific idea and explain why
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads a science claim — like 'plants grow faster with music' — can they evaluate whether the evidence actually supports it or if the test wasn't fair?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 公平测试（9岁以上）
topics.description: 利用测试结果做出预测，并设计进一步的比较测试和公平测试，以探究新的问题。
evidence: Use results from an investigation to make a specific, testable prediction
Design a follow-up test to verify the prediction
Explain the reasoning linking the original results to the new prediction
topics.assessmentPrompt: After getting results from one experiment, can {{name}} use the pattern to predict what would happen in a new situation and then design a follow-up test to check?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 科学是可以修正的
topics.description: 科学知识是暂时性的——它是基于现有证据的最佳解释，当有更好的证据出现时，它可以也应该被修正。
evidence: Give an example of a scientific idea that changed when new evidence was found — e.g. people once thought the Sun orbited the Earth
Explain that scientists update their ideas when experiments give unexpected results, and that this is a strength not a weakness
Describe why it is important to keep testing ideas rather than just accepting them because an expert said so
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand that scientific facts can be revised as new discoveries are made — and that this is science working properly, not a sign that scientists were wrong?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 控制变量（11岁以上）
topics.description: 提出一个可检验的科学假设，将自变量与预测结果联系起来；设计完整的探究计划，识别自变量、因变量和控制变量、样本量以及风险评估。
evidence: Writes a hypothesis in the form 'I predict that [IV] will affect [DV] because...' supported by scientific reasoning
Identifies and labels the independent variable, dependent variable, and at least three control variables
Plans repeat readings and an appropriate sample size, and identifies relevant hazards with control measures
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wanted to investigate whether temperature affects how quickly sugar dissolves, could they write a clear prediction, state exactly what they would change and measure, list three things to keep the same, and identify any safety steps?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 通过重复测试提高可靠性
topics.description: 区分精密度（重复读数的稳定性）和准确度（与真实值的接近程度），正确使用有效数字和标准形式，并选择和使用合适的测量工具来减少不确定性。
evidence: Explains the distinction between precision and accuracy with examples
Rounds measurements to an appropriate number of significant figures
Selects a measuring instrument with appropriate resolution for the context (e.g. choosing a 10 ml measuring cylinder rather than a 1-litre measuring jug for a 5 ml measurement)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} weighed the same stone five times and got very similar answers but they were all slightly too high, could they explain the difference between being precise and being accurate — and why having lots of repeats doesn’t always fix the problem?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 从证据中得出结论（12岁以上）
topics.description: 识别数据中的规律和趋势，得出直接回应假设的结论，并定量引用证据，通过区分系统误差和随机误差来评估探究过程，并提出有针对性的改进建议。
evidence: Identifies the pattern or trend in a graph or data table using specific values
Writes a conclusion that references the hypothesis, states whether the prediction was supported, and quotes numerical evidence
Distinguishes between a systematic error (affects all readings in the same direction) and a random error, and proposes a specific procedural improvement to address each
topics.assessmentPrompt: After finishing an experiment, can {{name}} describe the trend in the results, write a conclusion that says whether their prediction was right (with figures), and suggest one specific improvement that would make the results more reliable — rather than just saying 'do more repeats'?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 表格、图表和图形
topics.description: 制作带有正确标题和国际单位制单位的数据表格，绘制合适的图表类型（条形图、折线图、散点图），画出最佳拟合线，并计算直线图形的斜率。
evidence: Constructs a table with column headings that include quantity and unit (e.g. Mass / g)
Selects the appropriate graph type for the data and plots it accurately with labelled axes and scales
Draws a line of best fit for linear data and correctly calculates its gradient using two points
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} collected data on how spring length changes with the weight added, could they put it in a correct table, plot it as a line graph with axes labelled in the right units, draw a line of best fit, and calculate the gradient?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 撰写科学报告
topics.description: 使用适当的科学词汇、国际单位制（SI）和标准符号，以结构化的报告形式交流科学发现；描述同行评审和重复实验如何促进科学知识的可靠性。
evidence: Writes a structured scientific report including aim, hypothesis, method, results, conclusion, and evaluation using appropriate scientific vocabulary
Uses SI units and standard form consistently throughout a report
Explains what peer review is and why replication by independent researchers is essential for scientific claims to be accepted
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} write up an experiment with all the right sections and scientific language, and explain why a scientific discovery isn’t accepted straight away — describing what peer review means and why other scientists need to repeat the experiment?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 月相
topics.description: 观察并描述月亮在大约一个月内形状的变化，认识到月亮会经历一个重复的月相周期，从新月（看不见）到满月（完整的圆形）再回到新月。
evidence: Describe that the Moon appears to change shape over about a month
Name or draw at least three phases: new moon (dark), half moon, and full moon
State that the pattern repeats — the Moon goes through the same shapes again and again
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you asked {{name}} to look at the Moon several nights in a row, could they notice that it changes shape and describe the pattern?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 我们的太阳系
topics.description: 知道除了地球以外还有其他行星，围绕太阳运行的行星群体被称为太阳系——太空是地球天空之外的广阔区域。
evidence: State that Earth is a planet and there are other planets too
Use the term 'solar system' to describe the Sun and the planets that orbit it
Explain that space is the area beyond the Earth's sky, where the planets and stars are
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that Earth is one of several planets that go around the Sun, and that this group is called the solar system?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 寻找星座
topics.description: 在夜空中认出一些星星的图案（星座），从北斗七星开始，并知道可以用北斗七星找到北极星。
evidence: Identify or draw the Big Dipper (the Plough) as a pattern of seven stars
Explain that the two end stars of the Big Dipper's bowl point towards the North Star
State that constellations are patterns of stars that people have named
topics.assessmentPrompt: On a clear night, could {{name}} find the Big Dipper in the sky — or draw its shape from memory?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 太阳、月亮和星星
topics.description: 能识别天空中的太阳、月亮和星星，并描述它们的基本区别：太阳在白天提供光和热，星星在夜晚是小小的光点，月亮在白天和夜晚都可能出现在天空中。
evidence: Name the Sun, Moon, and stars as objects in the sky
State that the Sun appears during the day and gives us light and heat
State that stars appear at night and the Moon can sometimes be seen during the day too
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} point out the Sun, Moon, and stars and tell you something simple about each one — like that the Sun gives us light and heat?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 宇航员做什么
topics.description: 知道宇航员是乘坐火箭去太空的人，人类已经登上过月球（阿波罗任务），现在的宇航员在国际空间站上生活和工作。
evidence: Define an astronaut as a person who travels to space
State that humans landed on the Moon during the Apollo missions
Describe the International Space Station as a place where astronauts live and work in orbit around Earth
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you what an astronaut is, and that people have actually walked on the Moon and live on a space station?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 小行星、彗星和矮行星
topics.description: 认识太阳系中除行星以外的其他天体：小行星（岩石天体，大多位于火星和木星之间）、彗星（冰质天体，靠近太阳时会出现尾巴）以及流星体/流星/陨石（进入地球大气层的太空岩石）
evidence: Describe asteroids as rocky bodies mostly found in the belt between Mars and Jupiter
Describe comets as icy bodies that develop a glowing tail when they approach the Sun
Explain the difference between a meteoroid (in space), meteor (streak of light in atmosphere), and meteorite (lands on Earth)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a shooting star, could they explain that it’s actually a tiny space rock burning up in our atmosphere — and tell you the difference between that and a comet?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 地球的自转与公转
topics.description: 了解地球有两种运动方式：它绕地轴自转，每24小时转一圈，形成白天和黑夜；它绕太阳公转，每365天转一圈，也就是一年。
evidence: Demonstrate with a globe or ball that Earth's rotation causes day on the Sun-facing side and night on the opposite side
State that one full rotation takes about 24 hours (one day)
State that one full orbit around the Sun takes about 365 days (one year)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that we have day and night because the Earth spins, and that a year is the time it takes Earth to go all the way around the Sun?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 望远镜如何工作
topics.description: 知道望远镜是帮助我们观察太空中遥远物体的仪器，而像哈勃和詹姆斯·韦伯这样的太空望远镜在地球大气层上方运行，以获得更清晰的宇宙视图。
evidence: Explain that a telescope magnifies distant objects so we can see them in more detail
State that Earth's atmosphere blurs the view, so space telescopes get clearer pictures
Name at least one space telescope (Hubble or James Webb) and describe what it does
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know what a telescope does and why some telescopes are sent into space — like the Hubble or James Webb telescopes?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 行星的特征
topics.description: 描述每颗行星的一个主要特征：水星最小且离太阳最近，金星最热，火星因生锈而呈红色，木星最大且有巨大的红斑，土星有光环，天王星侧躺着自转，海王星最远且非常寒冷。
evidence: State one distinctive feature for at least six of the eight planets
Compare at least two planets (e.g. Jupiter is much bigger than Earth, Venus is hotter than Mercury)
Explain why Mars appears red (iron oxide/rust in its rocks)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you named a planet, could {{name}} tell you one interesting fact about it — like Saturn's rings or Jupiter's Great Red Spot?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 太空机器人与漫游车
topics.description: 描述机器人和漫游车如何探索人类难以到达的地方——像好奇号和毅力号这样的火星漫游车在火星上行驶，拍摄照片、采集岩石样本，并寻找过去存在水的迹象。
evidence: Name at least one Mars rover (Curiosity or Perseverance) and state it drives on Mars's surface
Explain that rovers take photos, analyse rocks, and look for evidence of water
State why we send robots instead of people: Mars is very far away and has no breathable air
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know about the Mars rovers? Can they tell you what Curiosity or Perseverance does on Mars?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 八大行星
topics.description: 按离太阳从近到远的顺序说出八大行星（水星、金星、地球、火星、木星、土星、天王星、海王星），知道冥王星是矮行星，并能区分岩石质的类地行星和气体巨行星
evidence: List all eight planets in order from the Sun
State that Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006
Explain that the four inner planets are small and rocky while the four outer planets are large gas giants
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list all eight planets in order from the Sun — maybe using a memory trick like 'My Very Eager Mother Just Served Us Nachos'?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 月球的轨道
topics.description: 知道月球大约每个月绕地球一圈，它自己不发光，而是反射太阳光，我们看到的月相变化是因为从地球上能看到月球被太阳照亮部分的大小不同。
evidence: State that the Moon orbits Earth roughly once every 28-30 days
Explain that the Moon reflects sunlight rather than producing its own light
Describe how Moon phases happen: we see different amounts of the lit-up side as the Moon orbits Earth
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the Moon seems to change shape — that it’s always round but we only see the part lit up by the Sun?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 太阳是一颗恒星
topics.description: 知道太阳是一颗恒星——离地球最近的恒星——并且它位于太阳系的中心，所有八颗行星都围绕它运行。
evidence: State that the Sun is a star, not a unique type of object
Explain that the Sun appears bigger and brighter than other stars because it is much closer
Describe the solar system as the Sun at the centre with planets orbiting around it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that the Sun is actually a star — just a very close one — and that the planets go around it?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 关于太空的观念变迁
topics.description: 了解人们对太阳系的看法是如何随时间改变的：古代人认为地球在中心（地心说，托勒密），直到哥白尼提出太阳在中心（日心说），后来由伽利略的望远镜观测所证实。
evidence: Describe the geocentric model (Earth at the centre) and name Ptolemy as its main proponent
Describe the heliocentric model (Sun at the centre) and name Copernicus as the person who proposed it
Explain that Galileo used a telescope to find evidence supporting the heliocentric model (e.g. moons orbiting Jupiter)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you that people used to think the Sun went around the Earth, and explain how scientists like Copernicus and Galileo changed our understanding?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 重力让物体下落
topics.description: 理解重力是一种将物体拉向地心的力，无论你站在球体上的哪个位置，“下”都指向地心，并且重力使月球绕地球运行、行星绕太阳运行。
evidence: Define gravity as a pulling force that attracts objects towards the centre of the Earth
Explain that 'down' points towards Earth's centre, so people on opposite sides of the globe both feel pulled 'down'
State that gravity keeps the Moon orbiting Earth and planets orbiting the Sun
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why things fall 'down' and that gravity is the same force keeping the Moon going around the Earth?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 恒星的生命周期
topics.description: 了解恒星生命周期的基本知识：恒星诞生于气体和尘埃云（星云）中，通过核聚变将氢转化为氦，发光数百万或数十亿年，最终死亡——大质量恒星爆炸成为超新星，而较小的恒星则逐渐冷却变成白矮星。
evidence: Describe that stars form from clouds of gas and dust called nebulae
State that stars produce energy by fusing hydrogen into helium in their cores
Explain that massive stars end in a supernova explosion while smaller stars shrink to become white dwarfs
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that stars are born, live for a very long time, and eventually die — and that really big stars can explode at the end?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 太阳系的尺度
topics.description: 使用比例模型、示意图或计算来表示太阳系中天体的相对大小和距离，理解行星之间的距离比行星本身大得多。
evidence: Explain that if the Sun were the size of a beach ball, Earth would be a pea about 26 metres away
State that the distances between planets are much greater than the sizes of the planets themselves
Create or interpret a scale model showing both relative sizes and distances
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} ever built or looked at a scale model of the solar system? Can they explain why the planets would need to be spread across a whole playing field to be the right distance apart?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 季节性星座
topics.description: 认识不同季节可见的命名星座，并理解为什么一年中不同时间看到的星座不同——因为地球绕太阳公转，改变了我们夜晚面向天空的方向。
evidence: Name at least three constellations (e.g. Orion, Ursa Major/Big Dipper, Leo, Cassiopeia)
State that different constellations are visible in different seasons
Explain that this happens because Earth's orbit means we face different directions in space at different times of year
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that you can see different constellations in winter than in summer, and can they explain why?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 太空探索里程碑
topics.description: 描述人类太空探索的关键里程碑：太空竞赛（斯普特尼克号、尤里·加加林、阿波罗11号登月）、航天飞机时代、国际空间站以及当前任务（阿尔忒弥斯计划、火星探索计划、商业太空飞行）
evidence: Name Sputnik as the first satellite (1957) and Yuri Gagarin as the first person in space (1961)
Describe the Apollo 11 Moon landing (1969) with Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin
Name at least one current space programme (Artemis, SpaceX, ISS) and describe its goal
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you about the history of space exploration — from the first satellite to the Moon landing to what’s happening now?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 浩瀚的宇宙尺度
topics.description: 用层层嵌套的方式描述宇宙的尺度：地球是太阳系中的一颗行星，太阳是银河系中数十亿颗恒星中的一颗，而银河系又是宇宙中数十亿个星系中的一个。
evidence: State that the Milky Way is our galaxy and it contains billions of stars
Explain the hierarchy: planet → solar system → galaxy → universe
Use a comparison to convey cosmic scale (e.g. if the Sun were a football, Earth would be a peppercorn 26 metres away)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how our place in the universe works — that we’re on a planet in a solar system in a galaxy among billions of galaxies?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 为什么太阳看起来最亮
topics.description: 解释为什么太阳看起来比其他恒星亮得多：它是离地球最近的恒星，而不是宇宙中最大或最亮的恒星——理解视觉亮度（看起来有多亮）和实际亮度之间的区别。
evidence: State that the Sun is a medium-sized star that appears brightest because it is the closest star to Earth
Explain the difference between apparent brightness (how bright it looks) and actual brightness (how much light it gives off)
Give an example: a torch held close looks brighter than a distant floodlight, even though the floodlight is more powerful
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} understand that the Sun looks so bright because it’s close, not because it’s the biggest star — and that some faraway stars are actually much larger?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 寻找系外行星
topics.description: 描述天文学家如何利用凌星测光法（行星经过恒星前方时星光出现的微弱下降）和径向速度法（恒星的 Doppler 摆动）来探测其他恒星周围的行星，解释宜居带的概念，并讨论大气生物特征——例如同时探测到氧气、甲烷和水蒸气——对行星意味着什么。
evidence: Explains transit photometry: the small, periodic dip in a star's brightness when a planet passes in front of it
Explains the habitable zone as the range of distances from a star where liquid water could exist on a planet's surface
Describes two or more atmospheric biosignatures and explains why their co-presence is significant (e.g. oxygen + methane together suggests active life replenishing both)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that a planet the size of Earth had been found in the habitable zone of a nearby star, could they explain how astronomers detected it, what the habitable zone means, and what they'd look for in its atmosphere to decide if life might exist there?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 用光波观测宇宙
topics.description: 解释电磁波谱如何成为现代天文学的主要工具——不同波长（无线电波、红外线、可见光、紫外线、X射线、伽马射线）揭示不同的现象，为什么有些望远镜必须放在太空，以及每个波长范围带来了哪些具体发现（例如微波中的宇宙微波背景辐射、X射线中的黑洞喷流、无线电波中的冷气体云）。
evidence: Lists at least four regions of the EM spectrum and gives a specific astronomical object or phenomenon observed in each
Explains why some telescopes must be placed in space (Earth's atmosphere blocks X-ray, gamma-ray, and much infrared radiation)
Describes the James Webb Space Telescope or Hubble and explains which part of the spectrum each primarily observes and why that was chosen
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was told that we can't see most of the universe with our eyes, could they explain why — and describe two types of telescope that detect something other than visible light, naming what they've helped us discover?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 轨道力学
topics.description: 运用牛顿定律解释轨道运动：为什么轨道是持续向侧方下落而不是漂浮；引力助推（弹弓机动）如何将行星的动量传递给航天器；以及为什么火箭需要达到特定速度才能进入轨道——用概念性（而非代数）的方式讲解齐奥尔科夫斯基火箭方程
evidence: Explains that orbit is a state of continuous freefall — the spacecraft is falling towards Earth but moving so fast horizontally that it keeps missing
Describes how a gravity assist works: a spacecraft flying past a planet gains speed by 'borrowing' from the planet's orbital momentum
Explains the key insight of the rocket equation: the ratio of fuel to final spacecraft mass grows exponentially with required Δv, explaining why large rockets are mostly fuel
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why astronauts in the ISS float even though they're still close to Earth and gravity hasn't disappeared, could they explain that they're actually in freefall and describe what 'being in orbit' really means physically?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 元素从哪里来
topics.description: 解释恒星核合成：宇宙大爆炸主要产生了氢和氦；主序星内部的核聚变反应能合成直到铁的元素；而比铁更重的元素则需要在超新星爆发中产生，并被抛洒到太空中——这意味着我们身体里的原子，都是在远古恒星中锻造出来的。
evidence: States that the Big Bang produced primarily hydrogen and helium, and that all heavier elements were made later in stars
Explains that nuclear fusion in main-sequence stars converts hydrogen to helium and can continue building heavier elements up to iron

Explains why elements heavier than iron require supernova explosions to form, and describes how supernovae distribute these elements into interstellar space where they become the raw material for new stars, planets, and life
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was told that the calcium in their bones and the iron in their blood were made inside ancient stars that exploded billions of years ago, could they explain the chain of events from the Big Bang to the formation of those atoms to how they ended up on Earth?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 火星之旅
topics.description: 评估前往火星的长期太空飞行所面临的工程和人类挑战——辐射暴露、肌肉和骨骼流失、心理孤立、通信延迟——并评估SETI计划的现状：使用了哪些方法，迄今探测到了什么，以及什么是费米悖论。
evidence: Identifies and explains at least three major challenges of a Mars mission: radiation (no magnetosphere), bone/muscle loss from low gravity, psychological isolation, and delayed communications
Describes how SETI searches for intelligent life (radio signals, laser pulses, technosignatures) and explains why the lack of detection so far is not proof of absence
States the Fermi Paradox ('Where is everybody?') and discusses two contrasting proposed resolutions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked whether they'd volunteer for a 3-year mission to Mars, could they describe at least three serious scientific or engineering challenges that would need to be solved first — and explain why the 20-minute communication delay alone changes almost everything about how the mission would operate?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 给行星命名
topics.description: 按照离太阳从近到远的顺序说出太阳系中的行星，并使用太空词汇——行星、恒星、太阳、月球、卫星、轨道、太阳系、星系、宇宙、小行星、彗星——在描述太阳系结构和我们天空中看到的物体时正确运用这些词汇。
evidence: Name the eight planets in order from the Sun without prompting
Use 'orbit' correctly to describe the movement of planets around the Sun and moons around planets
Distinguish between a planet, a moon, a star, and an asteroid using the correct vocabulary
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name the planets in order from the Sun — and explain the difference between a star, a planet, and a moon?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 为什么季节会变化
topics.description: 在不同季节进行观察，将日照时间与一年中的时间联系起来，注意夏天白天更长，冬天白天更短
evidence: Describe the pattern: more daylight hours in summer, fewer in winter
Compare sunrise/sunset times at different points in the year
Relate amount of daylight to seasonal changes in weather and nature
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} noticed that it's still light at bedtime in summer but dark much earlier in winter, and can they explain this pattern?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 太阳、月亮和星星
topics.description: 通过观察太阳、月亮和星星，描述可预测的规律，例如太阳升起和落下、月亮形状的变化以及星星在夜晚出现
evidence: Describe the daily pattern of sunrise and sunset
Describe the pattern of the moon's shape changing over about a month
Explain that stars are visible at night and describe any seasonal patterns observed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe patterns they've noticed in the sky — like the sun rising in the east, the moon changing shape over weeks, and stars coming out at night?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 地球的快速变化
topics.description: 利用多个来源的信息来证明地球事件可以发生得很快（地震、火山喷发），也可以发生得很慢（侵蚀、造山运动）。
evidence: Give at least two examples of rapid Earth events (earthquake, volcanic eruption, landslide, flood)
Give at least two examples of slow Earth processes (erosion, mountain formation, canyon carving)
Use evidence from text, images, or video to support the distinction between fast and slow changes
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} give examples of things that change the Earth quickly, like an earthquake, and things that change it very slowly, like a river carving a valley?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 地球与太空词汇
topics.description: 使用专业词汇来描述地球的运动和更广阔的宇宙——自转、公转、地轴、倾斜、轨道、光年、引力、大气层、月相、盈、亏、至点、分点、食——并运用这些词汇解释昼夜、季节和月相的形成
evidence: Use 'rotation' and 'revolution' correctly to describe Earth's two distinct types of movement and explain what each causes
Use 'waxing' and 'waning' to describe the Moon's phases and explain what causes them
Apply 'solstice' and 'equinox' correctly when explaining why seasons exist and why day length varies
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between the Earth rotating and the Earth orbiting the Sun — using the actual science words 'rotation' and 'revolution'?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 地球自转与昼夜
topics.description: 用地球自转的概念解释昼夜以及太阳在天空中看起来的移动
evidence: Explain that the Earth rotates (spins) on its axis once every 24 hours
Describe how this rotation causes day (facing the sun) and night (facing away)
Explain that the sun appears to move across the sky because we are rotating, not the sun
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that the sun doesn't actually move across the sky — it's the Earth spinning that makes it look like it does, and that's what causes day and night?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 化石是如何形成的
topics.description: 从岩层中的岩石构造和化石规律中找出证据，来支持对地貌随时间变化的解释。
evidence: Explain that rock layers (strata) form over time, with the oldest at the bottom
Describe how fossils in different layers provide evidence of organisms that lived at different times
Use patterns in rock formations to explain how a landscape has changed over millions of years
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees layers of rock in a cliff face, can they explain that the bottom layers are oldest and any fossils tell us what lived there long ago?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 太阳系
topics.description: 描述太阳、地球和月球近似为球体，并描述太阳系中地球和其他行星绕太阳运动的情况。
evidence: State that the sun, Earth, and moon are approximately spherical
Name the planets in order from the sun and explain they all orbit the sun
Describe the moon orbiting the Earth while both orbit the sun
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe the solar system — how Earth and the other planets orbit the sun, and how the moon orbits Earth, and that they're all roughly ball-shaped?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 影子
topics.description: 用图表展示数据，揭示影子长度和方向每日变化、昼夜循环以及季节性星空图案的规律
evidence: Measure and record shadow length and direction at different times of day
Create a graph showing how shadow length changes throughout the day
Connect shadow patterns to the sun's apparent position and Earth's rotation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} measure their shadow at different times of day, plot it on a chart, and explain why it's longest in the morning and evening but shortest at midday?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 星星的亮度和距离
topics.description: 支持太阳和星星看起来的亮度是由它们与地球的相对距离决定的观点，理解太阳是一颗相对较近的恒星。
evidence: Explain that the sun is a star, and it appears much brighter because it is much closer to Earth
Describe how a torch looks brighter close up and dimmer far away as an analogy
Argue that differences in apparent brightness of stars are mainly due to their different distances from Earth
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the sun looks so much brighter than other stars, even though many stars are actually bigger — it's because the sun is much closer to us?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 月相
topics.description: 解释从地球上看到的月球表面阳光角度变化所形成的月相，并描述日食和月食是如何发生的。
evidence: Explains that the phases of the Moon arise from the changing geometry of Sun, Earth, and Moon, not Earth's shadow
Describes the sequence of Moon phases over approximately 28 days
Distinguishes between a solar eclipse (Moon between Sun and Earth) and a lunar eclipse (Earth between Sun and Moon)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} noticed the Moon looking like a thin crescent one night and a full circle two weeks later, could they explain what has changed and why — and describe what happens during a lunar eclipse?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 太阳系（11岁以上）
topics.description: 描述太阳系的详细结构，包括卫星、小行星和彗星，比较行星的公转周期和距离，并区分行星、矮行星和其他天体。
evidence: Names the eight planets in order and gives one distinguishing fact about each
Describes the difference between a planet, a dwarf planet, an asteroid, and a comet
Explains the relationship between distance from the Sun and orbital period (planets further out take longer)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was making a model of the solar system, could they describe the difference between a planet, a moon, an asteroid, and a comet — and explain why planets closest to the Sun take less time to complete an orbit?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 为什么我们有四季
topics.description: 解释四季是由地球绕太阳公转时地轴的倾斜造成的，并区分常见的误解——即四季是由地球与太阳距离的变化造成的。
evidence: Explains that Earth's axis is tilted at about 23.5° relative to its orbit
Describes how the tilted axis causes one hemisphere to receive more direct sunlight in summer and less in winter
Refutes the misconception that distance from the Sun causes seasons by noting Earth is actually slightly closer to the Sun in January
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why the UK is hot in summer but Australia is cold at the same time, could they explain that it's not about being closer to the Sun but about which half of the Earth is tilted towards the Sun?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 星系与宇宙
topics.description: 描述宇宙的尺度，包括星系的结构、太阳在银河系中的位置，以及使用光年作为距离单位，并理解为什么太空探索需要极其漫长的时间。
evidence: Defines a light year as the distance light travels in one year
Describes the structure of a galaxy and states that the Sun is a star in the Milky Way galaxy
Compares the distances within the solar system with the distances between stars and between galaxies, expressing them in appropriate units
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that a star is 400 light years away, could they explain what a light year means, roughly how far that is, and why we will never be able to visit it with current spacecraft?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 万有引力
topics.description: 把引力描述为所有有质量的物体之间普遍存在的吸引力，解释轨道运动之所以产生是因为引力提供了使物体保持在轨道上的向心力，并比较不同行星上的引力场强度。
evidence: States that gravity is a universal attractive force acting between all objects with mass
Explains that orbital motion occurs because gravity continuously deflects the path of the orbiting object
Compares gravitational field strength on different planets and explains how this affects weight
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why the Moon doesn't fly off into space but also doesn't crash into Earth, could they explain that gravity is constantly pulling it into a curved path — like swinging a ball on a string?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 恒星的生命周期
topics.description: 描述恒星从星云到主序星，再到最终状态（根据质量不同，可能是白矮星、中子星或黑洞）的生命周期，并将恒星的生命周期与比氢更重的元素的起源联系起来。
evidence: Describes the main stages in the life cycle of a star similar to the Sun: nebula → protostar → main sequence → red giant → planetary nebula → white dwarf
Explains that more massive stars end as a supernova followed by a neutron star or black hole
States that nuclear fusion inside stars produces heavier elements from hydrogen and helium
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was told that the iron in their blood was forged inside a star that exploded billions of years ago, could they explain the life cycle of a star and how elements are made inside stars?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 身体的基本需求
topics.description: 知道身体需要食物来获得能量，需要水来保持水分，需要睡眠来休息和成长，需要运动来保持肌肉和心脏强壮——这些都是每个人身体的基本需求。
evidence: List the four basic needs: food (energy), water (hydration), sleep (rest and growth), exercise (strength)
Explain that food gives the body energy to move, think, and grow
Describe what happens if one need isn't met (e.g. feeling tired without sleep, thirsty without water)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why their body needs food, water, sleep, and exercise — and what happens if they miss any of them?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 骨骼和肌肉
topics.description: 知道身体内部有一套由骨头组成的骨架，它支撑身体、塑造体形，并保护大脑（头骨）和心脏（胸腔）等重要器官；连接在骨头上的肌肉能让身体动起来。
evidence: State that bones give the body shape, support, and protection
Name at least three bones or bone groups (e.g. skull, ribcage, spine, leg bones)
Explain that muscles pull on bones to make the body move
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} feel their own ribs or skull and explain what those bones are protecting inside?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 呼吸是怎样进行的
topics.description: 知道我们通过鼻子和嘴巴把空气吸入肺里，肺从空气中吸收身体维持生命所需的氧气，并且我们呼出身体不需要的二氧化碳废气。
evidence: Trace the path of air: nose/mouth → windpipe → lungs
State that lungs take oxygen from the air, which the body needs
State that we breathe out carbon dioxide, which the body doesn't need
topics.assessmentPrompt: After running around, can {{name}} notice their faster breathing and explain that their lungs are taking in air that the body needs?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 大脑控制身体
topics.description: 理解大脑是身体的指挥中心：它接收来自感官的信息，思考并做出决定，然后通过神经发送信息告诉肌肉该做什么。
evidence: State that the brain is inside the skull and controls the whole body
Describe the basic loop: senses send information to the brain, the brain decides what to do, and sends messages to muscles
Give an example (e.g. eyes see a ball coming, brain decides to catch it, nerves tell hands to move)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the brain does — that it’s in charge of thinking, feeling, and telling the body what to do?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 五种感官
topics.description: 详细探索五种感官：视觉用眼睛探测光线，听觉用耳朵探测声音，触觉用皮肤感受压力和温度，味觉用舌头辨别味道，嗅觉用鼻子闻气味。
evidence: Name all five senses and match each to the correct body part
Describe what each sense detects (e.g. eyes detect light, ears detect sound waves)
Give an example of using each sense in everyday life (e.g. smelling food cooking, feeling hot water)
