topics.assessmentPrompt: If you blindfolded {{name}} and gave them something to smell, taste, and touch, could they name which sense they were using each time and which body part does the job?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 心脏与血液
topics.description: 了解心脏是一块肌肉，它通过叫做血管的管道把血液泵到全身各处；我们把手放在胸口或用手指按住手腕，就能感觉到心跳。
evidence: Locate their own heartbeat by touch (chest or pulse point)
State that the heart pumps blood through the body continuously
Describe blood vessels as tubes that carry blood to every part of the body
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find their own pulse on their wrist or neck, and explain that it’s their heart pumping blood?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 均衡饮食与食物种类
topics.description: 认识主要的食物种类（碳水化合物、蛋白质、脂肪、维生素、矿物质、膳食纤维、水），并理解均衡饮食需要从每种食物中摄取适量的营养，以保持身体健康，提供能量、生长所需的材料和抵抗疾病的能力。
evidence: Name at least five food groups and give an example food for each (e.g. carbohydrates = bread, protein = chicken)
Explain what carbohydrates (energy), proteins (growth and repair), and fats (energy and warmth) do for the body
State that vitamins and minerals protect against illness and help the body work properly
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at their dinner plate, could they identify which foods give energy, which help muscles grow, and which keep them healthy?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 细胞、组织和器官
topics.description: 理解身体是按层级组织起来的：微小的细胞是构成身体的基本单位，相似的细胞组合在一起形成组织，组织组合成器官（如心脏或胃），器官在器官系统中协同工作（如循环系统）。
evidence: State that cells are the smallest building blocks of the body, too small to see without a microscope
Describe the hierarchy: cells → tissues → organs → organ systems
Give an example: muscle cells form muscle tissue, which forms the heart organ, which is part of the circulatory system
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that the body is made of tiny cells, and that cells group together to make tissues, which make organs, which make whole systems?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 肌肉如何带动骨骼运动
topics.description: 了解肌肉是成对配合来带动骨骼运动的：当一块肌肉收缩（变短并产生拉力）时，另一块相反的肌肉就会放松；有些肌肉是随意肌（我们可以自主控制），而像心脏这样的肌肉则是不随意肌（自动工作）。
evidence: Demonstrate or describe how biceps and triceps work as a pair to bend and straighten the arm
Explain the difference between voluntary muscles (we control them) and involuntary muscles (they work automatically)
Name the heart and muscles of the digestive system as examples of involuntary muscles
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} bend their arm and explain that one muscle is pulling while the other is relaxing — and that their heart muscle works without them thinking about it?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 眼睛是如何工作的
topics.description: 描述眼睛是如何工作的：光线通过瞳孔进入眼睛，晶状体将光线聚焦到眼睛后部的视网膜上，视网膜通过视神经将信号发送到大脑，大脑解读图像
evidence: Name the main parts: pupil (lets light in), lens (focuses light), retina (detects light), optic nerve (sends signals to brain)
Describe the sequence: light enters → lens focuses → retina detects → nerve signals brain → brain interprets image
Explain that the pupil gets bigger in dim light and smaller in bright light to control how much light enters
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happens inside their eye when they look at something — how light comes in through the pupil and the brain turns it into a picture?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 说出主要骨骼的名称
topics.description: 能说出人体骨骼中主要骨骼的名称（头骨、脊柱/椎骨、肋骨、骨盆、股骨、肱骨），并解释骨骼的三大作用：支撑身体形状、保护器官、与肌肉配合实现运动。
evidence: Name and locate at least six major bones or bone groups on a diagram or their own body
Explain the three functions: support (holds us upright), protection (skull protects brain, ribs protect heart/lungs), movement (bones work with muscles)
State that not all animals have internal skeletons — some have shells or exoskeletons
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} point to different parts of their body and name the bones underneath — like the femur in the thigh or the vertebrae in the spine?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 消化之旅
topics.description: 追踪食物在消化系统中的旅程：食物进入嘴巴，牙齿把它嚼碎，唾液开始消化；然后沿着食道来到胃；再经过小肠，营养在这里被吸收；最后废物通过大肠排出体外。
evidence: List the organs in order: mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine
Describe what happens at each stage (teeth chew, stomach churns with acid, small intestine absorbs nutrients)
State that the small intestine is where most nutrients pass into the blood, and the large intestine removes water from waste
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} ate a sandwich, could they describe the journey it takes through their body — from mouth to stomach to intestines?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 牙齿的种类
topics.description: 认识人类的四种牙齿（门齿用来切，犬齿用来撕，前臼齿和臼齿用来磨），理解牙齿的形状和功能有关，就像其他动物一样——食草动物的牙齿是平的，食肉动物的牙齿是尖的
evidence: Name the four tooth types and describe each one's job: incisors cut, canines tear, premolars/molars grind
Compare human teeth to herbivore teeth (flat, for grinding plants) and carnivore teeth (sharp, for tearing meat)
Explain that humans have all types because we are omnivores — we eat both plants and meat
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} look in a mirror, point out their different types of teeth, and explain what each type is for?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 循环与呼吸的协作
topics.description: 了解循环系统和呼吸系统如何协同工作：肺部为血液提供氧气，心脏将血液泵送到全身，细胞利用氧气并产生二氧化碳废物，血液将废物带回肺部，然后通过呼吸排出体外。
evidence: Describe the cycle: lungs add oxygen to blood → heart pumps oxygenated blood to body → cells use oxygen → blood returns CO₂ to lungs
Explain why heart rate and breathing rate increase during exercise (muscles need more oxygen)
Measure their own resting and post-exercise heart rate and explain the difference
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why their heart beats faster when they run — and how their heart and lungs are working together to deliver more oxygen to their muscles?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 成长与青春期
topics.description: 描述人类从出生到老年的人生发展阶段：婴儿、幼儿、儿童、青少年（青春期）、青年、中年、老年——了解每个阶段发生的身体变化，尤其是青春期。
evidence: Name and order at least six life stages from birth to old age
Describe key physical changes during puberty (growth spurts, body shape changes, development of adult features)
Explain that puberty is triggered by hormones — chemical messengers released by glands
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe how a person’s body changes as they grow from a baby to an adult to an elderly person — and explain what happens during puberty?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 健康生活方式的选择
topics.description: 了解生活方式的选择如何影响身体健康：均衡饮食、规律运动、充足睡眠和远离有害物质（烟草、酒精、毒品）有助于身体系统正常运转，而不良选择会增加患病风险。
evidence: Explain how regular exercise strengthens the heart, lungs, and muscles
Describe how a poor diet high in sugar and fat can lead to obesity, tooth decay, and heart problems
State at least two harmful effects of smoking (damages lungs, increases heart disease risk) or alcohol (damages liver, affects brain)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how what they eat, how much they exercise, and how much they sleep affects how their body works — and why smoking or drugs are harmful?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 心脏与血液循环
topics.description: 详细描述循环系统：心脏有四个腔室（两个心房、两个心室），通过双循环泵送血液——一个循环将血液送到肺部获取氧气，另一个循环将血液送到全身各处输送氧气——血液通过动脉、静脉和微小的毛细血管流动。
evidence: Name the four heart chambers and describe the double-loop pathway (heart → lungs → heart → body)
Distinguish arteries (carry blood away from heart), veins (carry blood back to heart), and capillaries (tiny vessels where exchange happens)
Name the components of blood: red blood cells (carry oxygen), white blood cells (fight infection), platelets (help clotting), plasma (liquid)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} trace the path blood takes through the heart and body — explaining that it goes to the lungs first for oxygen, then out to the rest of the body?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 肺是怎样工作的
topics.description: 详细解释呼吸系统的工作过程：空气通过鼻子或嘴巴进入，沿着气管向下，进入支气管和细支气管，到达肺里微小的气囊（肺泡），在那里氧气进入血液，二氧化碳排出体外
evidence: Trace the air pathway: nose/mouth → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli
Explain gas exchange in the alveoli: oxygen passes into blood capillaries, carbon dioxide passes out
Describe the mechanical process: the diaphragm contracts to pull air in and relaxes to push air out
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what happens to the air they breathe in — how it travels deeper and deeper into the lungs until oxygen swaps into the blood?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 免疫系统
topics.description: 了解人体有免疫系统来抵御疾病：皮肤作为屏障，白细胞识别并消灭病菌（细菌和病毒），疫苗训练免疫系统在疾病引起不适之前识别特定疾病。
evidence: Describe the skin as the body's first line of defence against germs
Explain that white blood cells detect and fight bacteria and viruses inside the body
Describe how vaccines work: they contain weakened or inactive germs that train the immune system to recognise the real disease
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how their body fights off germs — and why getting a vaccine helps protect them from getting sick?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 神经系统
topics.description: 了解神经系统分为两部分——中枢神经系统（大脑和脊髓）以及遍布全身的神经——神经信号以极快的速度传递，从而协调感觉、思维和运动
evidence: Name the two parts of the nervous system: central (brain + spinal cord) and peripheral (nerves throughout the body)
Describe the reflex arc: stimulus → sensory nerve → spinal cord/brain → motor nerve → muscle response
State that nerve signals travel extremely fast, which is why reflexes happen almost instantly
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a message travels from their finger to their brain when they touch something hot, and then back to their hand to pull it away?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 免疫与疫苗
topics.description: 区分先天免疫（非特异性、即时反应）和适应性免疫（特异性、形成记忆）；解释B细胞如何产生能识别特定抗原的抗体，T细胞如何消灭被感染的细胞，以及为什么免疫记忆能让疫苗发挥作用；并将肠道微生物组描述为一个由数万亿微生物组成的群落，对免疫功能有重要影响。
evidence: Distinguishes innate immunity (rapid, non-specific barriers and inflammation) from adaptive immunity (slow, specific, memory-forming)
Explains how B cells produce antibodies that bind to specific antigens on pathogens, targeting them for destruction
Explains immunological memory: after first exposure, memory B and T cells remain, making subsequent response faster and stronger — the basis of vaccine protection
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why they don't get chickenpox twice, could they explain the difference between just fighting off a germ and actually 'remembering' it — and describe how a vaccine trains the immune system without causing the disease?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 神经元与大脑结构
topics.description: 解释神经元如何通过电化学冲动在突触间传递信号，描述大脑的组织方式（脑叶及其功能、负责情绪的边缘系统），并解释神经可塑性——为什么学习和练习会从物理上改变大脑结构——同时联系视错觉现象，说明大脑是在主动构建现实，而不是被动记录现实。
evidence: Describes the neuron-to-neuron signal pathway: electrical impulse travels along axon, neurotransmitter crosses the synapse, new impulse begins in the next neuron
Names the four lobes of the cerebral cortex (frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital) and gives one function for each
Explains neuroplasticity: repeated neural pathways become stronger and faster — this is the biological mechanism of learning and skill development
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked why practising a skill like piano or football makes you better over time, could they explain what's actually happening physically in the brain — and describe what it means to say the brain 'rewires itself'?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: DNA与基因
topics.description: 描述DNA的双螺旋结构（碱基配对、互补性），解释基因是DNA上编码蛋白质的片段，从概念上介绍中心法则（DNA→mRNA→蛋白质），并讨论CRISPR基因编辑的伦理影响——包括潜在益处（治疗遗传病）和担忧（生殖细胞编辑、‘设计婴儿’）。
evidence: Describes DNA as a double helix with four bases (A, T, C, G) where A pairs with T and C pairs with G
Explains that a gene is a section of DNA that codes for a specific protein, and that proteins carry out most of the body's functions
Describes CRISPR as a molecular tool that can cut and edit DNA sequences, and raises at least two distinct ethical considerations about its use in humans
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that scientists have edited a human gene to prevent a hereditary disease, could they explain what DNA actually is, how genes work, and why some people think editing human DNA raises serious ethical questions?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 身体如何保持平衡
topics.description: 解释稳态是维持稳定内部环境的过程；以血糖调节（胰岛素/胰高血糖素）和体温为例，描述主要的反馈回路系统（负反馈）；并将内分泌系统（分泌激素的腺体）与神经系统联系起来，说明它们是两个互补的通信系统，具有不同的速度和持续时间。
evidence: Defines homeostasis and explains why maintaining a stable internal environment is essential for survival
Describes the blood glucose negative feedback loop: glucose rises → pancreas releases insulin → cells take up glucose → glucose falls → insulin release stops
Compares the nervous system (fast, electrical, short-duration signals) with the endocrine system (slower, chemical, longer-duration signals) and gives an example where each is more appropriate
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} ate a large meal of sugary food and was asked what their body does to keep blood sugar from getting dangerously high, could they explain the role of insulin and describe how the feedback system brings levels back to normal?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 癌症与干细胞
topics.description: 解释当DNA突变使正常的细胞周期控制失效时，会导致细胞分裂失控和肿瘤形成，从而引发癌症；描述干细胞与特化细胞的区别及其在再生医学中的潜力；并评估围绕胚胎干细胞研究和基因检测的伦理争议。
evidence: Explains cancer as the result of DNA mutations that disable tumour suppressor genes or activate oncogenes, causing unchecked mitosis
Distinguishes stem cells (unspecialised, can differentiate) from specialised cells (fixed function) and explains why stem cells are medically valuable
Presents the embryonic stem cell debate with at least two specific scientific arguments in favour and two ethical objections against, without simply asserting one side is correct
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked to explain what cancer actually is at a cellular level, could they describe what goes wrong with cell division — and explain why some people object to using stem cells from embryos for medical research, even if it could save lives?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 地球由岩石构成
topics.description: 理解地球是由岩石和其他固体物质构成的
evidence: State that the ground beneath us is made of rock
Identify rocks and stones as pieces of the Earth
Explain that Earth is solid and made of natural materials
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} picks up a stone in the garden, can they tell you that the whole Earth is made of rock and other materials like that stone?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 地震安全
topics.description: 了解基本的地震安全知识：趴下、掩护、稳住；远离窗户；告诉信任的大人
evidence: Demonstrate the drop, cover, and hold on procedure
Explain why to move away from windows and shelves during shaking
Name a trusted adult to tell if they feel an earthquake
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you asked {{name}} what to do if the ground started shaking, could they show you 'drop, cover, and hold on' and say they'd move away from windows?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 地球表面的快与慢变化
topics.description: 了解地球表面会发生变化：有些变化很快（如火山喷发、地震），有些变化很慢（如风、水慢慢侵蚀岩石）。
evidence: Give an example of a quick change to Earth's surface like a volcanic eruption
Give an example of a slow change to Earth's surface like erosion by wind or water
Compare quick and slow changes and explain the difference
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you point out a cliff being worn away by waves, can {{name}} explain that this happens slowly, while a volcanic eruption or earthquake changes the land quickly?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 喷发的力量
topics.description: 了解火山喷发是强大的事件，能够改变地貌
evidence: Describe an eruption as a powerful, dramatic event
Give examples of how an eruption changes the area around a volcano
Compare the landscape before and after an eruption using pictures
topics.assessmentPrompt: After watching a video of a volcano erupting, does {{name}} show excitement and talk about how powerful it is and how it changes the land around it?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 什么是地震
topics.description: 了解什么是地震：地面突然震动，可能强烈也可能微弱
evidence: Describe an earthquake as the ground shaking suddenly
Explain that earthquakes vary in strength from barely noticeable to very strong
Describe what it might feel like during an earthquake
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that an earthquake is when the ground suddenly shakes, and that some earthquakes shake harder than others?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 什么是火山
topics.description: 知道火山是什么：地球表面的一个开口，炽热的熔化岩石（熔岩）从这里喷出
evidence: Describe a volcano as a place where hot material comes out of the Earth
Explain that lava is rock so hot it has melted
Point to a volcano in a picture and describe what is happening
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a picture of a volcano erupting, can they explain that it's an opening in the ground where very hot melted rock comes out?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 活火山、休眠火山和死火山
topics.description: 将火山分类为活火山（随时可能喷发）、休眠火山（正在睡觉但可能醒来）或死火山（不会再喷发）
evidence: Define active, dormant, and extinct volcanoes
Explain that a dormant volcano is not safe just because it has not erupted recently
Classify a given volcano based on its eruption history
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you told {{name}} about a volcano that last erupted 500 years ago, could they explain whether it's active, dormant, or extinct, and why a dormant volcano might still be dangerous?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 地球的圈层
topics.description: 知道地球有圈层——薄薄的外层地壳、厚厚的炽热地幔，以及中心的地核——并且地球内部极其炽热。
evidence: Name Earth's three main layers: crust, mantle, and core
Explain that the crust is thin compared to the other layers
State that Earth's interior is extremely hot — hot enough to melt rock
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} cracks open a hard-boiled egg, can they compare it to Earth and name the three layers — crust on the outside, mantle in the middle, and core at the centre?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 火山内部
topics.description: 了解火山的内部结构：岩浆是地下高温熔化的岩石，熔岩是岩浆到达地表后的同一种物质，火山有岩浆房、火山通道和火山口。
evidence: Explain that magma is melted rock underground and lava is the same material above ground
Label a magma chamber, vent, and crater on a volcano cross-section
Describe the path magma takes from underground to the surface during an eruption
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks at a cross-section diagram of a volcano, can they point to the magma chamber, vent, and crater, and explain the difference between magma underground and lava on the surface?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 庞贝与维苏威火山
topics.description: 了解庞贝古城的故事：一座罗马城市在公元79年被维苏威火山喷发掩埋，被火山灰保存下来，几百年后被考古学家重新发现。
evidence: Retell the key events: Vesuvius erupted, Pompeii was buried under ash
Explain that the ash preserved the city, its buildings, and even people's shapes
Describe how archaeologists uncovered the city and what we can learn from it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a picture of the ruins of Pompeii, can they tell the story of how a Roman city was buried by a volcanic eruption and then found again hundreds of years later?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 环太平洋火山地震带
topics.description: 认识到火山和地震往往发生在某些特定地方——尤其是太平洋边缘（环太平洋火山地震带）——而不是在地球上随机分布
evidence: Describe the pattern that volcanoes and earthquakes cluster in certain zones
Locate the Ring of Fire on a world map
Explain that the locations of earthquakes and volcanoes are not random
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a world map showing where earthquakes and volcanoes happen, could they spot the pattern — that they cluster in certain lines and bands rather than being scattered everywhere?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 海啸
topics.description: 了解什么是海啸：一种由海底地震或火山喷发引起的巨大、快速的海洋波浪，到达陆地时可能造成巨大破坏
evidence: Explain that a tsunami is caused by an earthquake or eruption under the sea
State that tsunamis travel very fast across the ocean
Describe the damage a tsunami can cause when it reaches the coast
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears the word 'tsunami' on the news, can they explain that it's a huge wave caused by an earthquake or eruption under the ocean, and that it can travel very fast across the sea?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 岩石的种类
topics.description: 了解三大类岩石——火成岩（由岩浆或熔岩冷却形成）、沉积岩（由层层物质压紧形成）和变质岩——以及化石存在于沉积岩中。
evidence: Name the three main rock types: igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic
Explain that igneous rock forms when lava or magma cools and hardens
State that fossils are preserved in sedimentary rock because it forms in layers
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} finds different rocks on a beach walk, can they sort them and explain that some formed from cooled lava, some from layers pressed together over time, and that fossils are found in the layered ones?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 为什么会发生地震
topics.description: 了解当地下的岩石突然移动或断裂时，就会发生地震，释放出的能量使地面震动。
evidence: Explain that earthquakes are caused by rocks underground suddenly moving
Describe how this movement sends shaking through the surrounding ground
Distinguish between the underground cause and the surface effects of an earthquake
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} felt a small tremor or saw footage of an earthquake, could they explain that it happens because rocks deep underground suddenly shift or crack?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 抗震设计
topics.description: 知道建筑物可以设计成能抵抗地震，海啸预警系统可以提醒沿海社区，社区通过疏散计划和演习来做好准备。
evidence: Describe at least one feature that makes buildings more earthquake-resistant
Explain how tsunami warning systems detect danger and alert communities
Describe how communities prepare for earthquakes and eruptions through drills and evacuation plans
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a documentary about earthquake-proof buildings in Japan, could they explain how engineers design buildings to withstand shaking and how tsunami warnings give people time to evacuate?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 喷发类型与火山形状
topics.description: 了解并非所有火山喷发都一样：有些是温和的溢流（溢流式），有些是剧烈的爆炸（爆炸式），这取决于岩浆的性质，并且火山的形状与喷发类型有关。
evidence: Contrast effusive eruptions (gentle lava flows) with explosive eruptions (violent blasts of ash and rock)
Explain that eruption type depends on properties of the magma such as thickness and gas content
Connect volcano shape to eruption style: shield volcanoes from runny lava, steep cones from thick explosive magma
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared pictures of a gently oozing Hawaiian volcano and a violently erupting one like Mount St Helens, could they explain why eruptions look so different and how that relates to the volcano's shape?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 著名火山喷发与盘古大陆
topics.description: 了解著名的火山喷发及其全球影响：圣海伦斯火山（1980年）、埃亚菲亚德拉冰盖火山（2010年），以及大规模喷发如何影响全球天气和气候；理解大陆曾经连在一起（盘古大陆），并已缓慢漂移分开。
evidence: Describe at least one famous volcanic eruption and its key effects
Explain how volcanic ash and gases in the atmosphere can cool global temperatures
State that continents were once joined in a supercontinent and have slowly moved apart over millions of years
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you about a famous volcanic eruption like Mount St Helens and explain how a really big eruption can send so much ash into the sky that it affects weather around the whole world?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 测量地震强度
topics.description: 知道科学家使用地震仪来测量地震，地震释放的能量以波的形式在地面传播，震级用来描述地震的强度。
evidence: Explain that a seismometer is an instrument that detects and records ground shaking
Describe earthquake energy as waves that travel outward from where rocks broke
Interpret a magnitude number as a measure of an earthquake's strength
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard a news report about a magnitude 6 earthquake, could they explain what a seismometer is, that earthquakes send waves through the ground, and that higher numbers mean stronger quakes?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 监测火山
topics.description: 了解火山学家如何通过寻找预警信号——气体排放、地面膨胀、小地震——来监测火山，并且预测涉及证据和不确定性，而非确定性
evidence: Name at least two warning signs scientists look for before an eruption
Explain that volcanologists combine multiple types of evidence to assess risk
Discuss why volcanic prediction involves uncertainty and cannot guarantee exact timing
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how scientists watch for signs that a volcano might erupt — like gas, ground bulging, or tiny earthquakes — and why they can warn people but can't predict the exact moment?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 自然灾害解决方案
topics.description: 提出并比较多种解决方案，以减少地震、洪水或火山喷发等自然地球过程对人类的影响
evidence: Identify at least two natural hazards and their impacts on human life and property
Generate multiple solutions for reducing impacts (e.g. earthquake-resistant buildings, flood barriers, early warning systems)
Compare solutions based on criteria like effectiveness, cost, and feasibility
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} come up with different ideas for keeping people safe from earthquakes or floods, and compare which ones would work best?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 板块边界
topics.description: 解释板块边界如何引发地震和火山：板块相互挤压、分离或错动，会产生触发这些事件的力量，当板块碰撞时会形成山脉。
evidence: Describe three types of plate boundary movement: convergent, divergent, and transform
Explain that earthquakes occur when plates grind or collide at boundaries
Explain that volcanoes form where plates pull apart or one slides under another, allowing magma to rise
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why most volcanoes and earthquakes happen at the edges of tectonic plates — where plates push together, pull apart, or slide past each other?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 板块构造
topics.description: 了解地球的地壳分裂成许多大块，叫做板块，它们漂浮在下面更热、更软的岩石上，移动得非常缓慢——每年只有几厘米
evidence: Describe Earth's crust as broken into large plates
Explain that the plates float on hotter, partially melted rock underneath
State that plates move very slowly, typically a few centimetres per year
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you showed {{name}} a map of the tectonic plates, could they explain that Earth's surface is cracked into huge pieces that move very slowly — about as fast as their fingernails grow?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 岩石循环
topics.description: 了解岩石循环：岩石在数百万年间缓慢地从一种类型变成另一种类型——火成岩风化后变成沉积物，沉积物变成沉积岩，高温和高压形成变质岩，而熔化又让循环重新开始。
evidence: Describe the rock cycle as a continuous process with no beginning or end
Trace at least one complete path through the cycle from igneous to sedimentary to metamorphic and back
Explain that the rock cycle operates over millions of years through weathering, pressure, heat, and melting
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw igneous rock, sandstone, and marble side by side, could they explain how each type forms and how rocks slowly transform from one type to another in a never-ending cycle?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 板块如何运动
topics.description: 理解熔融地幔中的对流驱动了刚性板块的运动；区分汇聚型（碰撞/俯冲）、离散型（扩张脊）和转换型（滑动）板块边界；解释为什么火山、地震和山脉带集中在板块边界；介绍超大陆聚合与裂解的威尔逊旋回。
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks at a world map showing where volcanoes and earthquakes happen, can they explain why these events follow specific ring-shaped patterns rather than occurring randomly around the globe?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 地震波与地球内部
topics.description: 区分P波（压缩波，可通过固体和液体）和S波（剪切波，不能通过液体）；解释为什么地震远侧存在地震影区；描述地震学家如何利用波的折射和反射推断地球有固态内核、液态外核、地幔和地壳。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how scientists know Earth has a liquid outer core if nobody has ever drilled that deep — what clues do earthquake waves give us about Earth's hidden interior?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 灾害评估与疏散
topics.description: 解释使用喷发重现间隔和断层滑动速率进行概率灾害评估；描述火山观测站如何监测地面变形、气体排放和地震活动以发布警报级别；探讨为什么社区仍然留在活跃灾害附近（肥沃的火山土壤、贫困、文化联系）；讨论疏散决策的伦理和政治以及灾害风险的社会正义维度。
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read a news story about a town that refused to evacuate before a predicted volcanic eruption, can they describe at least two reasons — beyond just stubbornness — why people might genuinely choose to stay?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 超级火山与火山冬天
topics.description: 描述像黄石和托巴这样的破火山口是超级火山，能够喷发出数千立方公里的火山灰；解释平流层中的二氧化硫气溶胶如何散射阳光并导致火山冬天；讨论托巴灾难理论以及巨型喷发如何与冰期相互作用；对比超级火山喷发与普通喷发在规模和气候影响上的差异。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} heard of a supervolcano? Can they describe how a single enormous eruption could cool the entire planet for years — what gets into the atmosphere and why does it block warmth?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 火山与物种大灭绝
topics.description: 解释大火成岩省（LIPs）——数百万年间大规模熔岩喷发——如何导致全球变暖和海洋酸化，从而引发物种大灭绝；将西伯利亚暗色岩与二叠纪末大灭绝联系起来，将德干暗色岩与白垩纪末事件联系起来；探索早期地球上的热液喷口如何可能成为生命的摇篮；理解火山在生命历史中既是毁灭者也是创造者。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how enormous volcanic eruptions millions of years ago may have triggered some of Earth's biggest mass extinctions — what's the chain of events from lava to species dying out?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 用光和声音通信
topics.description: 设计并制作一个利用光或声音来解决远距离通信问题的装置
evidence: Design a device that uses light or sound to communicate over a distance (e.g. string telephone, torch signals)
Build and test the device, identifying what works and what could be improved
Explain how the device uses properties of light or sound to transmit information
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} design a simple device — like a string telephone or a mirror signalling system — to send a message to someone far away?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 光与在黑暗中看见
topics.description: 观察在黑暗中，物体只有被光源照亮时才能被看见
evidence: Explain that we need light to see objects — without any light source, it is completely dark
Describe an observation showing objects become visible only when light reaches them
Distinguish between light sources (sun, torch, lamp) and objects that just reflect light
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you go into a completely dark room with {{name}}, can they explain why they can't see anything until a torch is switched on?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 光和声音的词汇
topics.description: 命名并使用描述光和声音行为的词汇——光源、透明、半透明、不透明、影子、反射、振动、音高、音量——并在描述光的传播方式以及声音如何产生和变化时正确使用这些术语。
evidence: Correctly classify a set of materials as transparent, translucent, or opaque and explain each term
Explain what causes a shadow using the words 'opaque' and 'light source' correctly
Describe what changes the pitch or volume of a sound using vibration vocabulary
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you held up a piece of frosted glass, could {{name}} say whether it's transparent, translucent, or opaque — and explain what that word means?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 透明、半透明与不透明
topics.description: 研究将不同材料的物体放在光束路径上会产生什么效果，认识透明、半透明和不透明的材料。
evidence: Test at least six materials and classify them as transparent, translucent, or opaque
Define transparent (light passes through clearly), translucent (some light passes, blurry), opaque (no light passes)
Predict whether a given material will let light through based on its appearance
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} test different materials with a torch and sort them into ones light goes through, ones that block light, and ones in between?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 振动与声音
topics.description: 理解振动的物体会产生声音，声音也能让物体振动
evidence: Describe that sounds are made when objects vibrate (move back and forth quickly)
Give at least three examples of vibrating objects making sound (drum skin, guitar string, voice box)
Demonstrate that sound can cause objects to vibrate (e.g. rice on a drum jumps when you shout near it)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} pluck a rubber band and explain that the vibrating band makes the sound, and then hold a ruler on a speaker and see it shake from the music?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 影子是怎么形成的
topics.description: 知道当光源发出的光被不透明的物体挡住时，就会形成影子，并发现影子大小变化的规律
evidence: Explain that a shadow forms because an opaque object blocks light from reaching a surface
Describe the pattern: shadow gets larger when object moves closer to the light source
Predict the shape and relative size of a shadow given the position of light and object
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} make shadow puppets and explain why the shadow gets bigger when you move the puppet closer to the torch?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 保护眼睛免受阳光伤害
topics.description: 认识到太阳光可能很危险，并知道有办法保护眼睛。
evidence: State that looking directly at the sun can damage eyes permanently
Name at least two ways to protect eyes from bright sunlight (sunglasses, hat, shade)
Explain that the sun is an extremely bright light source unlike any artificial light
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know why you should never look directly at the sun and what you can do to protect your eyes on bright days?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 光的反射
topics.description: 注意光会从物体表面反射，光滑明亮的表面反射光的效果最好。
evidence: Explain that light bounces off surfaces, which is called reflection
Identify that smooth, shiny surfaces (mirrors, still water) reflect light best
Give everyday examples of reflection: mirror, puddle, polished floor
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why they can see themselves in a mirror or a shiny spoon, and why a rough wall doesn't reflect light the same way?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 声音的音高
topics.description: 找出声音的音高与发声物体特征之间的规律
evidence: Describe the pattern: shorter/thinner/tighter objects produce higher-pitched sounds
Demonstrate pitch changes using at least one instrument or everyday object
Explain pitch as how high or low a sound is, determined by how fast the object vibrates
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a short guitar string makes a higher sound than a long one, or why a small drum sounds higher than a big one?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 声音随距离减弱
topics.description: 认识到随着离声源距离的增加，声音会变得越来越轻。
evidence: State that sound gets quieter as distance from the source increases
Describe an observation or investigation demonstrating this pattern
Explain that vibrations spread out and get weaker as they travel further from the source
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a friend's voice gets harder to hear the further away they walk?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 声音在不同材料中的传播
topics.description: 认识到声音的振动通过介质（固体、液体或气体）传播到耳朵
evidence: Explain that sound vibrations need a material (medium) to travel through — they can't travel in a vacuum
Give examples of sound travelling through different media: air, water, solid objects
Describe how a string telephone works: voice vibrates the cup, vibrations travel along the string to the other cup
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why you can hear someone talking through a wall, and why sound travels through water when you're swimming underwater?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 音量与振动
topics.description: 发现声音的音量与产生它的振动强度之间的关系
evidence: Describe the pattern: stronger vibrations (larger movements) produce louder sounds
Demonstrate volume changes by varying the force applied to a sound-making object
Explain volume as how loud or quiet a sound is, determined by the size of vibrations
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why hitting a drum harder makes a louder sound, and what's happening to the drum skin differently?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 我们如何看见物体
topics.description: 建立一个模型来描述：光线从物体反射并进入眼睛，我们才能看见物体。
evidence: Draw a diagram showing light source → light hits object → reflects into eye
Explain that we see objects because reflected light enters our eyes, not because our eyes send out light
Use this model to explain why we can't see in total darkness (no light to reflect)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw a diagram showing how light bounces off a book and enters your eye, which is how you actually see the book?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 信息模式与编码
topics.description: 生成并比较多种利用模式传递信息的方案，例如编码和信号
evidence: Describe at least two systems that use patterns of light or sound to transfer information (e.g. Morse code, semaphore, drum signals)
Design a simple code using light or sound patterns to send a message
Compare the advantages and disadvantages of different information transfer methods
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} come up with different ways to send a secret message using patterns of light or sound, like Morse code or drum beats?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 波的特性词汇
topics.description: 使用专业词汇描述波的行为——折射、吸收、反射、散射、振幅、频率、波长、回声、光谱、入射角、反射角——并运用这些词汇解释光和声音如何传播以及如何与不同材料相互作用。
evidence: Use 'refraction' correctly to explain why a straw appears bent in a glass of water
Distinguish 'reflection' from 'refraction' using the correct definitions
Explain what an echo is using the vocabulary of sound reflection correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a straw looks bent in a glass of water using a proper science word — or tell you what's actually happening when you hear an echo?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 波与波的传播
topics.description: 建立波的模型，用振幅和波长描述波的规律，并理解波可以使物体移动。
evidence: Describe a wave using the terms amplitude (height) and wavelength (distance between peaks)
Demonstrate that larger amplitude means more energy (bigger waves move objects more)
Model wave patterns using a slinky, rope, or water and describe what they observe
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} use a slinky or rope to show how waves work, and explain that bigger waves have more energy and can move things more?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 光沿直线传播
topics.description: 认识到光似乎沿直线传播，并运用这一原理解释我们如何看到物体，以及为什么影子的形状与投射它的物体相同。
evidence: State and demonstrate that light travels in straight lines (e.g. can't see around corners, laser pointer)
Use straight-line light to explain why shadows have the same outline shape as the object
Draw ray diagrams showing light travelling from source, being blocked by object, creating shadow on screen
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a shadow of a hand looks like a hand shape, using the idea that light travels in straight lines?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 声音是如何传播的
topics.description: 解释声音是由物体振动产生的，并以纵波的形式通过固体、液体和气体传播；描述声音的反射（回声）和吸收；解释为什么声音不能在真空中传播。
evidence: Explains how a vibrating object creates regions of compression and rarefaction in air
Explains why sound travels fastest in solids and cannot travel in a vacuum
Describes how an echo is produced and gives a practical application (sonar, ultrasound)
Explains what sound absorption means and why soft furnishings reduce echoes
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard an echo in a large empty hall, could they explain what causes the echo, why the same sound in a carpeted living room doesn’t echo, and what would happen to sound in outer space?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 反射与折射
topics.description: 说出反射定律（入射角等于反射角），并解释折射是光穿过两种介质的分界面时速度和方向发生的变化；能运用光路图表示平面镜和折射面。
evidence: States the law of reflection and applies it to draw a reflected ray correctly
Draws a ray diagram for a plane mirror showing a virtual image
Explains why a pencil looks bent in a glass of water using refraction
Explains qualitatively why light bends towards the normal when entering a denser medium
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} put a straw in a glass of water and it looked bent at the surface, could they explain why that happens — drawing a diagram to show the path of light at the water’s surface?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 波的性质与类型
topics.description: 用振幅、波长、频率和波速来描述波；区分横波（振动方向与传播方向垂直）和纵波（振动方向与传播方向平行）；并运用波方程 v = fλ。
evidence: Labels a wave diagram with amplitude, wavelength, crest, and trough
Distinguishes transverse and longitudinal waves and gives an example of each
Uses v = fλ to calculate wave speed, frequency, or wavelength given the other two
Explains what happens to wavelength if frequency increases while wave speed stays constant
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked to describe a wave and how fast it travels, could they sketch one, label the wavelength and amplitude, and use the wave equation to work out speed from the frequency and wavelength?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 白光与颜色
topics.description: 解释白光是由所有可见颜色混合而成的（红、橙、黄、绿、蓝、靛、紫），描述光通过棱镜的色散现象，解释物体为什么呈现颜色（选择性地反射和吸收不同波长的光），并描述使用滤光片的颜色混合。
evidence: Lists the colours of the visible spectrum in order of increasing frequency
Explains why a prism disperses white light into a spectrum
Explains why a red object looks red under white light but black under blue light
Predicts the colour of an object seen through a colour filter
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} shone white light through a prism, could they explain why a rainbow of colours appears — and then predict what colour a blue jumper would look under red light and why?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 绘制光线图
topics.description: 绘制光线图来展示平面镜的反射（入射角等于反射角）和介质分界面处的折射；使用光线图来确定像的位置，并解释透镜和平面镜的工作原理。
evidence: Draw a ray diagram for a plane mirror showing the incident ray, normal, reflected ray, and virtual image
Draw a ray diagram showing a ray bending towards the normal when passing from air into glass
Use a ray diagram to locate the image formed by a convex lens and describe whether it is real or virtual
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw a diagram showing how a ray of light bounces off a mirror or bends when it passes from air into glass — labelling the angles correctly?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 光线图与成像
topics.description: 绘制光线图，展示平面镜和凸透镜如何成像，并判断像是实像还是虚像、放大还是缩小、正立还是倒立。
evidence: Draws an accurate ray diagram for a plane mirror showing a virtual, upright, same-size image
Draws a ray diagram for a converging lens to show image formation
Uses a ray diagram to determine whether the image is real or virtual and which side of the lens it forms
Applies ray diagram knowledge to explain how glasses, cameras, or projectors work
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was asked to show on a diagram where their reflection appears to be when they look in a mirror, could they draw the correct ray paths and explain whether the image is real or virtual — and where it actually appears to be located?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 电磁波谱
topics.description: 按照频率和能量从低到高的顺序，描述从无线电波到伽马射线的完整电磁波谱；说明所有电磁波在真空中传播速度相同；并描述不同波段的用途和危害。
evidence: Lists the seven regions of the EM spectrum in order of increasing frequency
States that all EM waves travel at 3 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum
Gives at least one use and one hazard for each region of the spectrum
Explains why some EM waves are more dangerous to living tissue than others (linked to frequency/energy)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard about microwaves, X-rays, and visible light all being part of the same family, could they explain what makes them different from each other and name one useful application and one risk for each?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 波与不同材料
topics.description: 解释波如何被不同材料吸收、传播或反射，并应用这些相互作用来解释颜色感知、视觉、通信技术以及不同表面如何影响波的行为。
evidence: Explains the difference between absorption, transmission, and reflection of waves
Uses the three interactions to explain how we see coloured objects
Explains how radio waves, visible light, and infrared are used in different communication technologies
Describes how the properties of a surface (colour, texture, material) determine how it interacts with radiation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} was wearing a black t-shirt on a sunny day and a friend was wearing white, could they explain using wave interactions why the black shirt gets hotter — and which properties of materials determine how they absorb or reflect radiation?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 根据天气穿衣服
topics.description: 根据不同的天气选择合适的衣服和装备——下雨天穿外套、带雨伞，大太阳天戴遮阳帽、涂防晒霜，寒冷天穿保暖的衣物——理解天气会影响我们每天的活动和准备
evidence: Select appropriate clothing for at least three different weather conditions
Explain why certain clothes or equipment are needed for specific weather
Describe how weather affects daily activities like playtime, walking to school, or outdoor events
topics.assessmentPrompt: Before going outside, can {{name}} check the weather and choose the right clothes — like grabbing a raincoat if it's cloudy or a sun hat if it's hot?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雨和积水
topics.description: 知道雨从天空中的云里落下来，水坑消失是因为水回到了空气中，这是水循环的一部分——水升到天空中，再落下来
evidence: State that rain falls from clouds
Explain that puddles disappear because the water goes into the air
Describe the basic idea that water goes up and comes back down in a repeating process
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} notices a puddle has disappeared on a sunny afternoon, can they explain that the water went up into the air, and that it will come back down again as rain from a cloud?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 季节与天气规律
topics.description: 知道天气会随着季节变化——春天带来雨水和新生命，夏天最温暖，白天最长，秋天天气转凉，树叶飘落，冬天最冷，白天最短——而且这个规律每年都会重复出现。
evidence: Name the four seasons and describe typical weather for each
Explain that days are longer in summer and shorter in winter
State that the seasonal pattern repeats every year
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you what kind of weather to expect in each season and explain that summer has the longest days while winter has the shortest?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 风暴安全
topics.description: 知道基本的风暴安全知识：打雷闪电时，要进入室内或汽车里，远离树木和水；明白风暴虽然可怕，但有办法保证安全。
evidence: State at least two safety rules for thunderstorms
Explain why going indoors is the safest option during lightning
Describe that storms are natural events and there are ways to stay safe
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard thunder while playing outside, would they know to come inside straight away and could they explain why standing under a tree isn't safe during a lightning storm?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 温度和温度计
topics.description: 理解温度表示物体的冷热程度，温度计用来测量温度，并能用热、温暖、凉爽、冷等词语描述不同天气下空气的冷热感觉。
evidence: Explain that temperature describes how hot or cold something is
Identify a thermometer as the tool used to measure temperature
Use words like hot, warm, cool, and cold appropriately to describe air temperature
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a thermometer outside, could they explain that it tells us how hot or cold the air is, and describe today as hot, warm, cool, or cold?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 天气的种类
topics.description: 识别并描述不同的天气类型——晴天、雨天、刮风、下雪、多云、雾天、暴风雨——并用简单的词汇描述今天的天气是什么样的
evidence: Name at least five types of weather
Describe today's weather accurately using appropriate vocabulary
Match weather types to simple pictures or symbols
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} looks out the window in the morning, can they describe the weather using words like sunny, cloudy, rainy, or windy, and say whether it's a nice day or a wet day?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 天气预报与安全
topics.description: 通过提问了解天气预报的作用，以及人们如何准备和应对恶劣天气
evidence: Explain that weather forecasts help people plan and stay safe
Describe how people prepare for at least two types of severe weather (storm, flood, heat wave, blizzard)
Ask relevant questions about weather hazards and find answers from appropriate sources
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why we check the weather forecast and what people do to get ready for a big storm or very hot weather?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 风是什么？
topics.description: 知道风就是流动的空气，风可以很轻柔（微风），也可以很猛烈（大风），风能吹动树叶、风筝、旗帜，甚至能推动人。
evidence: Define wind as air that is moving
Describe the difference between a gentle breeze and a strong wind
Give examples of things that wind can move or affect
topics.assessmentPrompt: On a windy day, can {{name}} explain that wind is air moving, point out things being blown around, and describe whether it's a gentle breeze or a strong gust?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 云的类型
topics.description: 认识三种主要的云——积云（蓬松，晴天出现）、层云（平坦成层，阴天或下毛毛雨）、卷云（细丝状，高高飘在天上）——并理解云是空气中的水蒸气冷却凝结成小水滴时形成的。
evidence: Name and describe the three main cloud types: cumulus, stratus, cirrus
Explain that clouds form when water vapour cools and condenses
Use cloud type to make a simple prediction about the weather
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked up at the sky, could they identify whether the clouds are fluffy cumulus, flat stratus, or wispy cirrus, and explain that clouds are made of tiny water droplets?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 地理与当地天气
topics.description: 知道世界上不同地方的典型天气很不一样——热带地区全年又热又湿，沙漠非常干燥，极地地区极其寒冷——并且地理因素（离赤道的距离、海拔、离海的远近）会影响当地的天气
evidence: Describe typical weather in at least three different climate types
Explain that places near the equator tend to be hotter
Name at least one factor that affects a place's weather besides latitude
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared weather in a tropical rainforest, a desert, and the Arctic, could they describe how different each is and explain why — like distance from the equator?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 水循环
topics.description: 了解水循环：太阳加热海洋和湖泊中的水，使水蒸发变成水蒸气；水蒸气上升冷却形成云（凝结）；水以雨、雪或冰雹的形式落回地面（降水）——然后循环重复。
evidence: Name the three main stages: evaporation, condensation, precipitation
Explain the Sun's role in driving the water cycle
Describe the water cycle as a continuous loop with no beginning or end
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} trace the journey of a raindrop — from the ocean being heated by the Sun, rising as invisible vapour, forming a cloud, and falling back down as rain — and explain it keeps going round and round?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 雷和闪电
topics.description: 知道雷和闪电发生在雷雨天气中：闪电是云层中形成的巨大电火花，雷是闪电发出的声音，我们总是先看到闪电后听到雷声，因为光比声音传播得快。
evidence: Describe lightning as a large electrical discharge in clouds
Explain that thunder is the sound caused by lightning
State that we see lightning before hearing thunder because light travels faster than sound
topics.assessmentPrompt: During a thunderstorm, can {{name}} explain that lightning is electricity in the clouds, thunder is its sound, and that we see the flash before the boom because light is faster than sound?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 使用天气仪器
topics.description: 使用天气仪器来测量和记录天气数据：用温度计测量摄氏温度，用雨量器测量降雨量，用风向标测量风向，用风速计测量风速——并长期坚持写天气日记。
evidence: Name at least three weather instruments and explain what each measures
Read a thermometer and record the temperature in degrees Celsius
Record weather data in a table or diary over several days
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} had a thermometer, rain gauge, and wind vane at school, could they take daily readings, record them in a table, and spot patterns over a week or month?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 天气预报
topics.description: 知道气象学家是研究和预报天气的科学家，他们使用卫星、雷达、气象气球和计算机模型，天气预报帮助人们安排活动并防范危险天气。
evidence: Define a meteorologist as a scientist who studies and predicts weather
Name at least three tools meteorologists use
Explain why weather forecasting is useful for safety and daily planning
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what a meteorologist does, name some tools they use like satellites and radar, and describe why weather forecasts are important for keeping people safe?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 天气与气候
topics.description: 区分天气和气候：天气是大气现在或今天的状况（可能每小时都在变化），而气候是一个地方多年来的典型天气模式。
evidence: Define weather as short-term atmospheric conditions
Define climate as the long-term pattern of weather in a place
Give an example showing the difference: a cold day doesn't change the overall climate
topics.assessmentPrompt: If someone said 'It's raining today so climate change isn't real,' could {{name}} explain the difference between weather (today's conditions) and climate (patterns over many years)?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 风是怎么形成的
topics.description: 了解风是怎么形成的：太阳让地球表面受热不均匀，热空气变轻上升，冷空气跑过来补充，空气的这种流动就是风。
evidence: Explain that the Sun heats Earth's surface unevenly
State that warm air rises and cooler air moves in to replace it
Define this air movement as wind
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why wind blows — that the Sun warms some areas more than others, warm air floats upward, and cooler air rushes in to fill the gap?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 为天气灾害设计
topics.description: 针对减少天气相关灾害（如洪水、风灾或极端温度）影响的设计方案，提出关于其优点的主张
evidence: Identify a specific weather-related hazard and its impacts on people
Describe at least two design solutions intended to reduce those impacts
Make a claim supported by evidence about which solution is most effective and why
topics.assessmentPrompt: If there's a risk of flooding in a town, can {{name}} evaluate different solutions like building levees, planting trees, or improving drainage and argue which works best?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 气候变化基础
topics.description: 了解气候变化的基础知识：地球的大气层会留住一部分太阳的热量（温室效应），燃烧化石燃料会释放出额外的温室气体（尤其是二氧化碳），这使地球逐渐变暖，而这种变暖会改变天气模式、融化冰川并导致海平面上升。
evidence: Describe the greenhouse effect: the atmosphere traps heat from the Sun
Explain that burning fossil fuels increases CO₂ in the atmosphere
Name at least two consequences of global warming: changing weather patterns, melting ice, rising seas
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the greenhouse effect in simple terms and describe how burning oil, gas, and coal adds extra CO₂ to the air, making Earth warmer and changing weather patterns?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 气候带
topics.description: 了解地球上有不同的气候带——热带（赤道附近，炎热潮湿）、温带（气候温和，四季分明）、极地（严寒冰冷）、干旱/沙漠（非常干燥）和山地（高海拔地区寒冷）——每个气候带都孕育着不同的生态系统和生活方式。
evidence: Name and describe at least four climate zones
Explain what determines which zone a place belongs to (mainly latitude and geography)
Give an example of how a climate zone affects the plants, animals, or people living there
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a world map showing climate zones, could they explain why the Amazon rainforest, the Sahara desert, and the Arctic all have such different weather, plants, and animals?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 极端天气事件
topics.description: 了解极端天气事件——飓风（温暖海洋上旋转的风暴）、龙卷风（剧烈旋转的空气柱）、洪水、干旱和暴风雪——它们是如何形成的、通常发生在哪里，以及它们对人和环境的影响。
evidence: Describe how at least two types of extreme weather form
Explain where hurricanes and tornadoes typically occur and why
Describe the effects of extreme weather on communities and landscapes
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw news about a hurricane, could they explain how it forms over warm ocean water, why it spins, and what makes it so destructive when it reaches land?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 自然资源
topics.description: 获取并整合信息，说明能源和燃料来源于自然资源，以及它们的使用对环境的影响。
evidence: Name natural resources used for energy and fuels (coal, oil, gas, wind, sun, water)
Describe how extracting and using these resources affects the environment (pollution, habitat loss, climate change)
Distinguish between renewable (wind, solar) and non-renewable (fossil fuels) energy sources
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain where petrol, electricity, and gas come from — that they come from natural resources like oil, coal, wind, or sunlight — and how using them affects the environment?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 阅读天气图
topics.description: 阅读并解读天气图、数据表格和图表——识别太阳、雨、风和温度的符号；发现数周、数月或季节的天气数据趋势和规律；并利用数据做出简单的预测。
evidence: Interpret common weather map symbols for temperature, precipitation, and wind
Read a data table or graph of weather data and identify patterns
Use weather data to make a simple prediction about upcoming conditions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a weather map with symbols on the news, could they read it and explain what weather is coming — and if shown a graph of monthly rainfall, could they spot the wettest and driest months?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 太阳驱动的天气系统
topics.description: 了解太阳如何驱动天气：太阳不均匀地加热地球表面（陆地比水升温快，赤道比两极获得更多热量），产生气压差异，从而引起风型、洋流和大规模天气系统
evidence: Explain that the Sun heats land and water at different rates
Describe how temperature differences create air pressure differences that drive wind
Connect uneven heating to large-scale weather patterns
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why coastal areas often have sea breezes and why the equator is hotter than the poles, connecting it all back to the Sun heating Earth unevenly?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 大气层
topics.description: 知道地球被一层叫做大气层的空气包围着，空气有重量并产生压力，大气层保护我们免受有害辐射，并使地球保持足够温暖以维持生命，天气发生在最低的一层（对流层）
evidence: Define the atmosphere as the layer of air surrounding Earth
State that air has weight and exerts pressure
Explain that weather occurs in the troposphere, the lowest layer of the atmosphere
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that we're surrounded by a blanket of air called the atmosphere, that this air actually has weight and pushes on everything, and that all our weather happens in the lowest layer?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 抗天气工程设计
topics.description: 了解工程师设计建筑物、防洪设施和预警系统来保护社区免受极端天气的影响——如抗飓风屋顶、防洪屏障、龙卷风避难所和早期预警系统——并评估这些解决方案的优点。
evidence: Describe at least two engineering solutions designed to protect against extreme weather
Explain how a specific design feature reduces damage from a weather hazard
Evaluate the advantages and limitations of a weather protection solution
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw pictures of houses on stilts in a flood zone and a tornado shelter, could they explain how each design protects people and discuss whether one solution works better than another?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 全球风带
topics.description: 解释太阳加热不均匀如何驱动大规模大气环流：哈得来环流（0-30°）、费雷尔环流（30-60°）和极地环流（60-90°）产生信风、西风和极地东风；描述地球自转产生的科里奥利效应如何使北半球的风向右偏转；解释急流是快速的高空风，引导天气系统；将急流的波动和北极放大效应与持续的极端天气联系起来。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the UK tends to get wet weather arriving from the west — what global pattern of winds is steering weather systems, and how does Earth's rotation contribute to this?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 温室气体科学
topics.description: 描述电磁波谱，区分短波太阳辐射和地球发出的长波红外辐射；解释温室气体分子（二氧化碳、甲烷、一氧化二氮、水蒸气）如何通过分子振动吸收并重新发射红外线，而氧气和氮气则不能；区分自然的温室效应（使地球宜居）和由人类排放驱动的增强温室效应；评估不同温室气体的相对效力。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain, in terms of light and energy, why CO2 in the atmosphere traps heat but nitrogen and oxygen — which make up most of the air — don't? What's physically different about CO2 molecules?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 飓风、龙卷风与季风
topics.description: 解释飓风如何在温暖的海洋水面上形成并增强（潜热释放、低压螺旋）；描述龙卷风在超级单体雷暴中的形成过程；解释由陆地和海洋之间的温度差异驱动的季风机制；介绍归因科学——科学家如何利用气候模型计算气候变化是否以及以多大程度增加了特定极端天气事件发生的概率或强度
topics.assessmentPrompt: When scientists say that climate change made a recent hurricane stronger, can {{name}} explain what they actually mean and how scientists figure that out — what kind of calculation lets them link a specific storm to climate change?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 阅读古代气候记录
topics.description: 解释冰芯如何保存古代气泡、同位素比例和火山标记，从而重建80万年来的温度和二氧化碳；描述树木年轮、海洋沉积物岩芯、珊瑚骨骼和花粉记录作为额外的气候代用资料；解释气候模型如何建立并根据古气候记录进行验证；描述IPCC综合数千项研究的科学证据以形成共识评估的过程。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how scientists know what the climate was like 500,000 years ago — what kind of 'time capsules' exist in nature that preserve ancient air and temperature records, and how do scientists read them?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: 净零排放与能源转型
topics.description: 评估实现净零排放所需的能源转型：可再生能源规模化、交通和供暖电气化、绿氢；描述碳捕集与封存（CCS）和直接空气捕集（DAC）；介绍拟议的太阳辐射管理技术（平流层气溶胶注入、海洋云增白）及其潜在风险与治理挑战；批判性评估个人行为改变与系统性政策在减排中的作用。
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} heard of geoengineering? Can they describe one proposal for deliberately cooling the Earth and explain one potential risk of attempting it — and say whether they think individuals or governments bear more responsibility for tackling climate change?
